body.text: Jagannātha Paṇḍitarāja: Rasagaṅgādhara, Ānana 1:
body.translated_text: <s>Jagannātha Paṇḍitarāja</s>: <s>Rasagaṅgādhara</s>, Section (<s>Ānana</s>) 1:

body.text:
smṛtāpi taruṇātapaṃ karuṇayā harantī nṛṇām
abhaṅguratanutviṣāṃ valayitā śatair vidyutām/
kalindagirinandinītaṭasuradrumālambinī
madīyamaticumbinī bhavatu kāpi kādambinī//
body.translated_text: May a certain cloud-mass — which, even when merely remembered, compassionately removes the scorching heat of youth from men, which is encircled by hundreds of lightnings whose slender radiance is unbroken, which clings to the celestial wish-fulfilling trees on the banks of the daughter of Mount <s>Kalinda</s> (<s>Yamunā</s>) — kiss my intellect!

body.text:
śrīmajjñāneṃdrabhikṣor adhigatasakalabrahmavidyāprapañcaḥ
kāṇādīrākṣapādīr api gahanagiro yo mahendrādavedīt/
devādevādhyagīṣṭa smaraharanagare śāsanaṃ jaiminīyaṃ
śeṣāṅkaprāptaśeṣāmalabhaṇitir abhūt sarvavidyādharo yaḥ//
body.translated_text: [<s>Jagannātha</s>], who mastered the entire expanse of the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> from the venerable <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) <s>Jñānendra</s>, who learned even the profound doctrines of <s>Kaṇāda</s> and <s>Akṣapāda</s> (the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> and <s>Nyāya</s> systems) from <s>Mahendra</s>, who studied the <s>Jaiminīya</s> teaching (the <s>Mīmāṃsā</s> system) in the city of the god of gods (<s>Vārāṇasī</s>), who is the Supreme Destroyer (<s>Śiva</s>), and whose stainless speech obtained the remainder [of all learning] marked by <s>Śeṣa</s> — he became the bearer of all sciences.

body.text:
pāṣāṇād api pīyūṣaṃ syandate yasya līlayā/
taṃ vande perubhaṭṭākhyaṃ lakṣmīkāntaṃ
mahāgurum//
body.translated_text: From whom nectar flows even from stone, effortlessly — I bow to that great teacher (<s>mahāguru</s>) named <s>Perubhaṭṭa</s>, the beloved of <s>Lakṣmī</s>.

body.text:
nimagnena kleśair mananajaladher antarudaraṃ
mayonnīto loke lalitarasagaṅgādharamaṇiḥ/
harann antardhvāntaṃ hṛdayam adhirūḍho guṇavatām
alaṃkārān sarvān api galitagarvān racayatu//
body.translated_text: By me, plunged into the interior of the ocean of contemplation by afflictions, the jewel of the graceful <s>Rasagaṅgādhara</s> has been brought up to the world. May it, having ascended the hearts of the virtuous and dispelling the inner darkness, render all ornaments (<s>alaṃkāras</s>) humble!

body.text:
pariṣkurvantv arthān sahṛdayadhurīṇāḥ katipaye
tathāpi kleśo me katham api gatārtho na bhavitā/
timīndrāḥ saṃkṣobhaṃ vidadhatu payodheḥ punar ime
kim etenāyāso bhavati viphalo mandaragireḥ//
body.translated_text: Let a few connoisseurs (<s>sahṛdaya</s>), leaders [of taste], refine [these] meanings — even so, my labor will somehow not have been in vain. Let the great fish-lords churn the ocean again — does the effort of Mount <s>Mandara</s> thereby become fruitless?

body.text:
nirmāya nūtanam udāharaṇānurūpaṃ
kāvyaṃ mayātra nihitaṃ na parasya kiṃcit/
kiṃ sevyate sumanasāṃ manasāpi gandhaḥ
kastūrikājananaśaktibhṛtā mṛgeṇā//
body.translated_text: Having composed new poetry (<s>kāvya</s>) appropriate to the examples, I have placed it here — nothing of another's. Does the musk-deer, endowed with the power of generating musk, serve even in its mind the fragrance of flowers?

body.text:
mananataritīrṇavidyārṇavo jagannāthapaṇḍitanarendraḥ
rasagaṅgādharanāmnīṃ karoti kutukena kāvyamīmāṃsām
rasāgaṅgādharanāmā saṃdarbho 'yaṃ ciraṃ jayatu/
kiṃ ca kulāni kavīnāṃ nisargasamyañci rañjayatu//
body.translated_text: <s>Jagannātha</s>, the king among <s>paṇḍitas</s>, who has crossed the ocean of sciences through contemplation, with delight composes this inquiry into poetry (<s>kāvyamīmāṃsā</s>) named <s>Rasagaṅgādhara</s>. May this composition named <s>Rasagaṅgādhara</s> long be victorious! And moreover, may it delight the lineages of poets, [which are] naturally beautiful!

body.text: tatra kīrtiparamāhlādagururājadevatāprasādādyanekaprayojanakasya kāvyasya vyutpatteḥ kavisahṛdayayor āvaśyakatayā guṇālaṃkārādibhir nirūpaṇīye tasmin viśeṣyatāvacchedakaṃ taditarabhedabuddhau sādhanaṃ ca tallakṣaṇaṃ tāvan nirūpyate--
body.translated_text: Therein, since the education [in poetry] — which has many purposes such as fame, supreme delight, service to the teacher, grace of the deity, and so on — is necessary for both the poet and the connoisseur (<s>sahṛdaya</s>), and since that [poetry] is to be analyzed through [the examination of its] qualities (<s>guṇa</s>), ornaments (<s>alaṃkāra</s>), and the like — the definition of that [poetry], which is the delimiting factor of the qualified entity and the means of distinguishing it from other [things], is first established —

body.text: ramaṇīyārthapratipādakaḥ śabdaḥ kāvyam//
body.translated_text: Poetry (<s>kāvya</s>) is language (<s>śabda</s>) that conveys beautiful meaning (<s>ramaṇīyārtha</s>). //

body.text:
ramaṇīyatā ca lokottarāhlādajanakajñānagocaratā/ lokottaratvaṃ cāhlādagataś camatkāratvāparaparyāyo 'nubhavasākṣiko jātiviśeṣaḥ/ kāraṇāṃ ca tadavacchinne bhāvanāviśeṣaḥ punaḥpunar anusaṃdhānātmā/ "putras te jātaḥ," "dhanaṃ te dāsyāmi" iti vākyārthadhījanyasyāhlādasya na lokottaratvam/ ato na tasmin vākye kāvyatvaprasaktiḥ/ itthaṃ ca camatkārajanakabhāvanāviṣayārthapratipādakaśabdatvam, yatpratipāditārthaviṣayakabhāvanātvaṃ camatkārajanakatāvacchedakaṃ tattvam, svaviśiṣṭajanakatāvacchedakārthapratipādakatāsaṃsargeṇā camatkāratvavattvam eva vā kāvyatvam iti phalitam/ yat tu prāñcaḥ "adoṣau saguṇau sālaṃkārau śabdārthau kāvyam" ity āhuḥ, tatra vicāryate-- śabdārthayugalaṃ na kāvyaśabdavācyam, mānābhāvāt/ kāvyam uccaiḥ paṭhyate, kāvyād artho 'vagamyate, kavyaṃ śrutam artho na jñātaḥ, ityādiviśvajanīnavyavahārataḥ pratyuta śabdaviśeṣasyaiva kāvyapadārthatvapratipatteś ca/ vyavahāraḥ śabdamātre lakṣaṇayopapādanīya iti cet, syād apy evam, yadi kāvyapadārthatayā parābhimate śabdārthayugale kāvyaśabdaśakteḥ pramāpakaṃ dṛḍhataraṃ kim api pramāṇāṃ syāt/ tad eva tu na paśyāmaḥ/ vimatavākyaṃ tv aśraddheyam eva/ itthaṃ cāsati kāvyaśabdasya śabdārthayugalaśaktigrāhake pramāṇe, prāg uktād vyavahārataḥ śabdaviśeṣe siddhyantīṃ śaktiṃ ko nāma nivārayitum īṣṭe/ etena vinigamanābhāvād ubhayatra śaktir iti pratyuktam/ tadevaṃ śabdaviśeṣasyaiva kāvyapadārthatve siddhe tasyaiva lakṣaṇaṃ vaktuṃ yuktam, na tu svakalpitasya kāvyapadārthasya/ eṣaiva ca vedapurāṇādilakṣaṇeṣv api gatiḥ/ anyathā tatrāpīyaṃ duravasthā syāt/ yat tv āsvādodbodhakatvam eva kāvyatvaprayojakaṃ tacca śabde cārthe cāviśiṣṭam ity āhuḥ, tan na/ rāgasyāpi rasavyañjakatāyā dhvanikārādisakalālaṃkārikasaṃmatatvena prakṛte lakṣaṇīyatvāpatteḥ/ kiṃ bahunā nāṭyāṅgānāṃ sarveṣām api prāyaśas tathātvena tatvāpāttir durvāraiva/ etena rasodbodhasamarthasyaivātra lakṣyatvam ity api parāstam/ api ca kāvyapadapravṛttinimittaṃ śabdārthayor
vyāsaktam, pratyekaparyāptaṃ vā/ nādyaḥ/ eko na dvāv iti vyavahārasyeva ślokavākyaṃ na kāvyam iti vyavahārasyāpatteḥ/ na dvitīyaḥ/ ekasmin padye kāvyadvayavyavahārāpatteḥ/ tasmād vedaśāstrapurāṇalakṣaṇasyeva kāvyalakṣaṇasyāpi śabdaniṣṭhataivocitā/
lakṣaṇe guṇālaṅkārādiniveśo 'pi na yuktaḥ/ "uditaṃ maṇḍalaṃ vidhoḥ" iti kāvye dūtyabhisārikāvirahiṇyādisamudīrite 'bhisaraṇavidhiniṣedhajīvanābhāvādipareḥ "gato 'stam arkaḥ" ityādau cāvyāptyāpatteḥ/ na cedam akāvyam iti śakyaṃ vaditum/ kāvyatayā parābhimatasyāpi yathā vaktuṃ śakyatvāt/ kāvyajīvitaṃ camatkāritvaṃ cāviśiṣṭam eva/ guṇatvālaṅkāratvāder ananugamāc ca/ duṣṭa kāvyam iti vyavahārasya bādhakaṃ vinā lākṣaṇikatvāyogāc ca/ na ca saṃyogābhāvavān vṛkṣaḥ saṃyogītivad aṃśabhedena/ doṣarahitaṃ duṣṭam iti vyavahāre bādhakaṃ nāstīti vācyam/ "mūle mahīrūho vihaṃgamasaṃyogī, na śākhāyām" iti pratīter ivedaṃ padyaṃ pūrvārdhe kāvyam uttarārdhe tu na kāvyam iti svarasavāhino viśvajanīnānubhavasya virahād avyāpyavṛttitāyā api tasyāyogāt/ śauryādivadātmadharmāṇāṃ guṇānām, hārādivad upaskārakāṇām alaṃkārāṇāṃ ca śarīraghaṭakatvānupapatteś ca/ yat tu "rasavad eva kāvyam" iti sāhityadarpaṇe nirṇītam, tan na/ vastvalaṃkārapradhānānāṃ kāvyānām akāvyatvāpatteḥ/ na ceṣṭāpattiḥ, mahākavisaṃpradāyasyākulībhāvaprasaṅgāt/ tathā ca jalapravāhaveganipatanotpatanabhramaṇāni kavibhir varṇitāni kapibālādivilasitāni ca/ na ca tatrāpi yathākathaṃcit paramparayā rasasparśo 'sty eveti vācyam/ īdṛśarasasparśasya "gauś calati", "mṛgo dhāvati" ityādāv atiprasaktatvenāprayojakatvāt/ arthamātrasya vibhāvānubhāvavyabhicāryanyatamatvād iti dik/ tasya ca kāraṇaṃ kavigatā kevalā pratibhā/ sā ca kāvyaghaṭanānukūlaśabdārthopasthitiḥ/ tadgataṃ ca pratibhātvaṃ kāvyakāraṇatāvacchedakatayā siddho jātiviśeṣa upādhirūpaṃ
vākhaṇḍam/ tasyāś ca hetuḥ kvacid devatāmahāpuruṣaprasādādijanyam adṛṣṭam/ kvacic ca vilakṣaṇavyutpattikāvyakaraṇābhyāsau/ na tu trayam eva/ bālādes tau vināpi kevalān mahāpuruṣaprasādād api pratibhotpatteḥ/ na tatra tayor janmāntarīyayoḥ kalpanaṃ vācyam/ gauravān mānābhāvāt kāryasyānyathāpy upapatteś ca/ loke hi balavatā pramāṇenāgamādinā sati kāraṇātānirṇāye paścād upasthitasya vyabhicārasya vāraṇāya janmāntarīyam anyathānupapattyā kāraṇaṃ dharmādharmādi kalpyate/ anyathā tu vyabhicāropasthityā pūrvavṛttakāraṇatānirṇāye bhramatvapratipattir eva jāyate/ nāpi kevalam adṛṣṭam eva kāraṇam ity api śakyaṃ vaditum/ kiyantaṃcit kālaṃ kāvyaṃ kartum aśaknuvataḥ katham api saṃjātayor vyutpattyabhyāsayoḥ pratibhāyāḥ prādurbhāvasya darśanāt/ tatrāpy adṛṣṭasyāṅgīkāre prāg api tābhyāṃ tasyāḥ prasakteḥ/ na ca tatra pratibhāyāḥ pratibandhakam adṛṣṭāntaraṃ kalpyam iti vācyam/ tādṛśāneka sthalagatādṛṣṭadvayakalpanāpekṣayā kḷptavyutpattyabhyāsayor eva pratibhāhetutvakalpane lāghavāt/ ataḥ prāguktasaraṇir eva jyāyasī/ tādṛśādṛṣṭasya tādṛśavyutpattyabhyāsayoś ca pratibhāgataṃ vailakṣaṇyaṃ kāryatāvacchedakam, ato na vyabhicāraḥ/ pratibhātvaṃ ca kavitāyāḥ kāraṇātāvacchedakaṃ, pratibhāgatavailakṣaṇyam eva vā vilakṣaṇakāvyaṃ pratīti nātrāpi saḥ/ na ca sator api vyutpatyabhyāsayor yatra na pratibhotpattis tatrānvayavyabhicāra iti vācyam/ tatra tayos tādṛśavailakṣaṇye mānābhāvena kāraṇatāvacchedakānavacchinnatvāt/ pāpaviśeṣasya tatra pratibandhakatvakalpanād vā na doṣaḥ/ pratibandhakābhāvasya ca kāraṇatā samuditaśaktyāditrayahetutāvādinaḥ śaktimātrahetutāvādinaś cāviśiṣṭā/ prativādinā mantrādibhiḥ kṛte katipayadivasavyāpini vākstambhe vihitānekaprabandhasyāpi kaveḥ kāvyānudayasya darśanāt/
taccottamottamottamamadhyamādhamabhedāc caturdhā/
śabdārthau yatra guṇībhāvitātmānau kamapyartham abhivyaṅktas tad ādyam//
body.translated_text: And 'beauty' (<s>ramaṇīyatā</s>) means being the object of a cognition that produces a delight that is extraordinary (<s>lokottara</s>). And the 'extraordinariness' of the delight is a specific universality (<s>jātiviśeṣa</s>), testified to by experience, whose other designation is 'wonder' (<s>camatkāra</s>) with respect to [that] delight. And the cause [of that extraordinariness] is a particular kind of contemplation (<s>bhāvanāviśeṣa</s>), delimited by that [wonder], consisting of repeated meditation (<s>anusaṃdhāna</s>). The delight produced by the cognition of sentence-meanings such as 'A son has been born to you' or 'I will give you wealth' is not extraordinary. Therefore, there is no applicability of the term '<s>kāvya</s>' to such sentences. Thus, the essential nature [of kāvya] is: being language that conveys a meaning that is the object of a contemplation that produces wonder; or, [the nature is] that the contemplation directed toward the conveyed meaning — whose nature is the delimiting factor of the capacity to produce wonder — has the quality of producing wonder; or again, <s>kāvya</s>-ness is the possession of wonder-producing-ness through the conjunction of the capacity to convey meaning that delimits the production of [that which is] qualified by [wonder] itself — this is the conclusion. Now, the ancients have said: 'Poetry is word and meaning that are free from faults, endowed with qualities, and furnished with ornaments.' Regarding this, we examine: The pair of word and meaning is not the referent of the word '<s>kāvya</s>,' because there is no valid evidence [for this]. From universally accepted usage such as 'poetry is recited aloud,' 'meaning is understood from poetry,' 'poetry was heard but the meaning was not understood' — on the contrary, it is a specific [type of] language (<s>śabdaviśeṣa</s>) alone that is understood as the referent of the word <s>kāvya</s>. If it is said that the usage [can be] explained through secondary meaning (<s>lakṣaṇā</s>) with respect to language alone — this might be so, if there were some stronger valid means of knowledge establishing the denotative power (<s>śakti</s>) of the word <s>kāvya</s> for the pair of word-and-meaning as accepted by the other side. But we do not see any such [evidence]. And a disputed statement is indeed unreliable. Thus, in the absence of a valid means establishing the denotative power of the word <s>kāvya</s> for the word-meaning pair, who could prevent the [denotative] power from being established for a specific [type of] language, based on the previously mentioned usage? By this, the [objection] that 'the power [of the word kāvya] applies to both [word and meaning] due to the absence of a decisive determination' is answered. Thus, since the referent of the word <s>kāvya</s> is established as a specific [type of] language alone, it is proper to state the definition of that alone, not of a self-invented referent of the word <s>kāvya</s>. And this same approach [applies] in the definitions of <s>Veda</s>, <s>Purāṇa</s>, and the like. Otherwise, the same difficulty would arise there too. As for what they say — that it is the capacity to awaken aesthetic relish (<s>āsvāda</s>) that is the cause of <s>kāvya</s>-ness, and that this is equally [present] in both word and meaning — that is not so; because <s>rāga</s> (musical melody) too, its capacity to suggest <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment) being accepted by all <s>alaṃkārikas</s> (rhetoricians) beginning with the author of the <s>Dhvani</s> [theory], would then have to be included in what is to be defined here. Why say more? — the unpreventable consequence would be that all the limbs of dramatic art (<s>nāṭyāṅga</s>) too, being generally of the same nature, would be [wrongly] included. By this, the [view] that 'only what is capable of awakening <s>rasa</s> is to be defined here' is also refuted. Moreover, the basis for the application of the word <s>kāvya</s> is either spread across both word and meaning, or is sufficient in each individually. Not the first — because just as the usage 'one, not two' [would be contradicted], so too the usage 'this verse-sentence is not <s>kāvya</s>' would follow as absurd. Not the second — because the usage of 'two poems' for a single verse would follow. Therefore, just as the definitions of <s>Veda</s>, <s>śāstra</s>, and <s>Purāṇa</s> are grounded in language, so too is it proper for the definition of <s>kāvya</s>. The inclusion of <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), <s>alaṃkāras</s> (ornaments), and the like in the definition is also not proper — because in the poem 'The orb of the moon has risen,' when uttered by a messenger-woman, a woman going to a tryst, a woman separated [from her lover], and so on, with meanings pertaining to the injunction or prohibition of going to a tryst, or the [lover's] life or death — and [similarly] in 'The sun has set' and the like — the undesirable consequence of [these] not being [recognized as] <s>kāvya</s> [would arise, since they lack explicit alaṃkāras]. Nor can one say 'this is not <s>kāvya</s>' — because even what is accepted by the other side as <s>kāvya</s> could be so contested. And the <s>camatkāritva</s> (wonder-producing quality), which is the life-force of poetry, is equally [present in both types]. And because the qualities of being a <s>guṇa</s>, an <s>alaṃkāra</s>, and the like cannot be consistently tracked. And because in the absence of an invalidating cognition, the usage 'bad poetry' (<s>duṣṭa kāvya</s>) cannot be made merely figurative. Nor should it be said — as with 'a tree possessing the absence of contact is [still] a possessor of contact' [through different parts] — that there is no invalidation for the usage 'a faultless [poem] is defective,' [explaining it] through a distinction of parts; because the universally experienced natural perception 'this verse is <s>kāvya</s> in the first half but not <s>kāvya</s> in the second half' is absent, and hence the [supposed] non-pervasion [of the definition] is also untenable. And because it is untenable that <s>guṇas</s>, which are inherent properties like valor etc., and <s>alaṃkāras</s>, which are embellishments like necklaces etc., are constituents of the body [of poetry]. As for what is concluded in the <s>Sāhityadarpaṇa</s> — 'only that which possesses <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment) is <s>kāvya</s>' — that is not so; because the undesirable consequence would arise that poems predominantly of the factual (<s>vastu</s>) and ornamental (<s>alaṃkāra</s>) types would not be <s>kāvya</s>. Nor is this a welcome consequence, because the tradition of great poets would be thrown into confusion. For poets have described the falling, rising, and whirling by the force of a stream of water, and the playful antics of monkey-cubs and the like. Nor should it be said that even there, some touch of <s>rasa</s> exists in some indirect way — because such a 'touch of rasa' being overly applicable even to 'the cow walks' and 'the deer runs,' it would serve no purpose. The meaning-matter alone [can function as] one of the <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants), <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequents), or <s>vyabhicārins</s> (transitory emotions) — this much is [the point] in brief. And the cause of that [kāvya] is the poet's pure creative genius (<s>pratibhā</s>) alone. And that is the presentation of words and meanings conducive to the composition of poetry. And the <s>pratibhā</s>-nature residing therein is a specific universality established as the delimiting factor of being the cause of <s>kāvya</s>, [or alternatively] a nominal fragment of the nature of a limiting adjunct (<s>upādhi</s>). And the cause of that [<s>pratibhā</s>] is, in some cases, an unseen merit (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>) produced by the grace of a deity or a great person. In other cases, it is extraordinary erudition (<s>vyutpatti</s>) and practice (<s>abhyāsa</s>) of composing poetry. But it is not exclusively [any one of] the three — because even for a child etc., <s>pratibhā</s> arises from the grace of a great person alone, without those two. Nor should it be said that there, those two [erudition and practice] are to be postulated from a previous birth — because of the cumbersomeness [of such a theory], the absence of valid evidence, and because the effect can be otherwise explained. For in the world, when there is a stronger valid means of knowledge such as scripture for the non-determination of causality, then to prevent a later-arising anomaly, a cause from a previous birth — such as <s>dharma</s> or <s>adharma</s> — is postulated through the method of 'otherwise inexplicable.' But otherwise, when the anomaly arises and the previously assumed causal determination [is shaken], the understanding arises that it was simply an error. Nor can it be said that unseen merit alone is the cause — because for one who was unable to compose poetry for some time, when erudition and practice somehow arise, the manifestation of <s>pratibhā</s> is observed. And even there, if unseen merit is accepted [as a co-factor], then [<s>pratibhā</s>] should have arisen even before those two [erudition and practice]. Nor should it be said that there, some other unseen [factor] obstructing <s>pratibhā</s> is to be postulated — because compared to the postulation of a pair of unseen [factors] in many such cases, it is more parsimonious to postulate erudition and practice alone as the cause of <s>pratibhā</s>. Therefore, the path stated earlier is indeed superior. The specific distinction in <s>pratibhā</s> [arising] from such unseen merit and from such erudition and practice is the delimiting factor of the effect-nature — hence there is no deviation. And <s>pratibhā</s>-nature is the delimiting factor of the causal nature of poetic composition; or rather, the specific distinction in <s>pratibhā</s> itself [is the cause of] distinctive poetry — hence there too, no [deviation arises]. Nor should it be said that where, despite the presence of both erudition and practice, <s>pratibhā</s> does not arise, there is a failure of positive concomitance — because there, in the absence of valid evidence for such specific distinction in those two, [they are] not delimited by the delimiting factor of causality. Or, by postulating a specific sin as an obstruction there, no fault [arises]. And the causality of the absence of obstruction is equally [applicable] for the proponents of the theory that the triad of combined power etc. is the cause, and for the proponents of the theory that power alone is the cause. [This is established] from the observation that even for a poet who has composed many works, poetry does not arise when speech-paralysis lasting for some days is effected by an opponent through <s>mantras</s> and the like. That [<s>kāvya</s>] is fourfold, due to the divisions of highest-of-the-highest, highest, middling, and lowest. Where word and meaning, having subordinated themselves, suggest some [other] meaning — that is the first [type].

body.text:
kamapīti camatkṛtibhūmim/ tenātigūḍhasphuṭavyaṅgyayor nirāsaḥ/ aparāṅgavācyasiddhyaṅgavyaṅgyasyāpi camatkāritayā tadvāraṇāya guṇībhāvitātmānāv iti svāpekṣayā vyaṅgyaprādhānyābhiprāyakam/
udāharaṇam--
śayitā savidhe 'pyanīśvarā saphalīkartum aho manorathān/
dayitā dayitānanāmbujaṃ daramīlannayanā nirīkṣayate//
body.translated_text: 'Some [meaning]' means: the ground of aesthetic wonder (<s>camatkāra</s>). By this, [<s>kāvya</s>] with an extremely hidden or [merely] explicit suggested meaning (<s>vyaṅgya</s>) is excluded. [And] even the suggested meaning that is an accessory to a principal [meaning] established through another [element] such as the expressed sense (<s>vācya</s>) — since it too possesses wonder — to prevent its [unwarranted inclusion], the phrase 'having subordinated themselves' is [used], indicating the predominance of the suggested [meaning] relative to themselves [i.e., the expressed word and meaning]. Example: 'Though lying near, unable to fulfill, alas, her desires — the beloved gazes at the lotus-face of her beloved with eyes barely closing.'

body.text:
atrālambanasya nāyakasya, savidhaśayanākṣiptasya rahaḥsthānāder uddīpanasya ca vibhāvasya, tādṛśanirīkṣaṇāder anubhāvasya, trapautsukyādeś ca vyabhicāriṇaḥ, saṃyogād ratir abhivyajyate/ ālambanādīnāṃ svarūpaṃ vakṣyate/ na ca yady ayaṃ śayitaḥ syāt tadāsyānanāmbujaṃ cumbeyam iti nāyikecchāyā eva vyaṅgayatvam atreti vācyam/ manorathān saphalīkartum asamarthetyanena manorathāḥ sarve 'syā hṛdi tiṣṭanti iti pratīteḥ svaśabdena manorathapadena sāmānyākāreṇa tādṛśecchāyā api nivedanāt/ na ca manorathapadena manorathatvākāreṇā sāmānyecchāyā abhidhāne 'pi cumbeyam iti viṣayaviśeṣaviśiṣṭecchātvena vyaṅgyatve kiṃ bādhakam iti vācyam/ camatkāro na syād ityasyaiva bādhakatvāt/ na hi viśeṣākāreṇa vyaṅgyo 'pi sāmānyākāreṇābhihito 'rthaḥ sahṛdayānāṃ camatkṛtim utpādayitum īṣṭe/ katham api vācyavṛttyanāliṅgitasyaiva vyaṅgyasya camatkāritvenālaṃkārikaiḥ svīkārāt/ cumbanecchāyā ratyanubhāvatayaiva sundaratvena tadavyañjane cumbāmīti śabdabalāc cumbanecchāvad acamatkāritvāc ca/ evaṃ trapāyā api na prādhānyena vyaṅgyatvam/ anuvādyatāvacchedakatayā pratītāyāṃ tasyāṃ mukhyavākyārthatvāyogāt/ na ca daramīlannayanātvaviśiṣṭanirīkṣaṇaṃ vidheyam iti nānuvādyatāvacchedakatvaṃ tasyā iti vācyam/ evam api nayanagatadaramīlanasya tatkāryatve 'pi daramīlannayanātvaviśiṣṭanirīkṣaṇasya ratimātrakāryatvāt/ trapāyā eva mukhyatvena vyaṅgyatve nirīkṣaṇokter anatiprayojanakatvāpatteḥ/
vācyavṛttyā rater anubhāve nirīkṣaṇo trapāyā anubhāvasya daramīlanasyeva vyañjanayā tasyāṃ tasyā api guṇībhāvapratyayaucityāt/
yathā vā--
gurumadhyagatā mayā natāṅgī nihatā nīrajakorakeṇa mandam/
darakuṇḍalatāṇḍavaṃ natabhrūlatikaṃ mām avalokya ghūrṇitāsīt//
body.translated_text: Here, the <s>ālambana</s> (foundational determinant) is the hero (<s>nāyaka</s>); the <s>uddīpana</s> (excitant determinant) is the secret place, the bedside, etc. — [all of which comprise] the <s>vibhāva</s> (determinant); the <s>anubhāva</s> (consequent) is the kind of gaze etc. of such a nature; and the <s>vyabhicārin</s> (transitory emotion) is modesty (<s>trapā</s>), eagerness (<s>autsukya</s>), etc. — through the combination of these, <s>rati</s> (erotic love) is suggested. The specific nature of the <s>ālambana</s> and the rest will be explained [later]. Nor should one say: 'What is suggested here is merely the heroine's desire — namely, "If he were asleep, I would kiss his lotus-face."' For since the expression 'unable to fulfill [her] wishes' conveys that all her wishes reside in her heart, through the word 'own' (<s>sva</s>) and the word 'wish' (<s>manoratha</s>), such a desire too has already been communicated in its general form. Nor should one say: 'Even though the word "wish" (<s>manoratha</s>) communicates, in its general form, the wish under the aspect of being-a-wish, what objection is there to the suggestion [of the specific wish] "I would kiss" as a specific-object-qualified desire?' — for the answer is that [in that case] there would be no aesthetic relish (<s>camatkāra</s>), and that itself is the objection. For a meaning that is suggested in its specific form, when [already] stated in its general form, is not able to produce aesthetic delight (<s>camatkṛti</s>) in connoisseurs (<s>sahṛdayas</s>). Because the <s>ālaṃkārikas</s> (rhetoricians) accept as producing aesthetic relish only that which is suggested and not grasped by the function of the literal meaning (<s>vācya-vṛtti</s>). And since the desire to kiss, being beautiful only as a <s>rati-anubhāva</s> (consequent of love), if it is not suggested through that [love] but is expressed by the mere force of the word 'I would kiss,' it would be devoid of aesthetic relish like [any explicit statement of] the desire to kiss. Likewise, modesty (<s>trapā</s>) too is not principally what is suggested. For when [modesty] is apprehended as the delimiting factor of what is being restated (<s>anuvādya</s>), it cannot qualify as the primary sentence-meaning. Nor should one say: 'The gaze qualified by the half-closing of the eyes is the predicate (<s>vidheya</s>); therefore [modesty] does not serve as the delimiting factor of the restated [element].' For even so, while the half-closing belonging to the eyes is an effect of [modesty], the gaze qualified by half-closing-of-the-eyes is an effect of <s>rati</s> (love) alone. [And] if modesty alone were principally suggested, the mention of the gaze would incur the fault of serving no purpose. Through the literal meaning (<s>vācya-vṛtti</s>), the gaze is the <s>anubhāva</s> (consequent) of <s>rati</s>; and the half-closing — which is the <s>anubhāva</s> of modesty (<s>trapā</s>) — by means of suggestion, [serves to indicate] that [modesty], because of the propriety of its becoming subordinate to [<s>rati</s>]. Or, [consider] another [example]: 'Situated among her elders, the slender-bodied woman, gently struck by a lotus bud, [watching] the slight dance of [her] ear-ornaments, the curve of her bent brow — having looked at me, she became dizzy.'

body.text:
atra ghūrṇitāsīd ityanenāsamīkṣyakārin kimidam anucitaṃ kṛtavān asīty arthasamvalito 'marṣaś carvaṇāviśrāntidhāmatvāt prādhānyena vyajyate/ tatra śabdo 'rthaś ca guṇaḥ/
yathā vā--
"talpagatāpi ca sutanuḥ śvāsāsaṅga na yā sehe/
samprati sā hṛdayagataṃ priyapāṇiṃ mandam ākṣipati//"
idaṃ ca padyaṃ mannirmitaprabandhagatatvena pūrvasākāṅkṣam iti diṅmātreṇa vyākhyāyate --- yā navavadhūḥ palyaṅkaśayitā śvāsasyāsaṅgamātreṇāpi saṃkucad aṅgalatikābhūt sā samprati prasthānapūrvarajanyāṃ pravatsyatpatikā priyeṇa saśaṅkena samarpitaṃ hṛdi pāṇiṃ navavadhūjātisvābhāvyād ākṣipati, paraṃ tu mandam/ atra śanaiḥ svasthānaprāpaṇātmanā mandākṣepeṇa ratyākhyaḥ sthāyī saṃlakṣyakramatayā vyajyate/ upapādayiṣyate ca sthāyyādīnām api saṃlakṣyakramavyaṅgayatvam/ amum eva ca prabhedaṃ dhvanim āmananti/
yat tu citramīmāṃsāyām appayyadīkṣitaiḥ "niḥśeṣacyutacandanam" iti padyaṃ dhvanyudāharaṇaprasaṅge vyākhyātam-- uttarīyakarṣaṇena candana-cyutir ityanyathāsiddhiparihārāya niḥśeṣagrahaṇam/ tataś candanacyuteḥ snānasādhāraṇyavyāvartanena saṃbhogacihnoddhāṭanāya taṭagrahaṇam/
snāne hi sarvatra candana cyutiḥ syāt, tava tu stanayos taṭa upari bhāga eva dṛśyate/ iyam āśleṣakṛtaiva/ tathā nirmṛṣṭarāgo 'dhara ity atra tāmbūlagrahaṇavilambāt prācīnarāgasya kiṃcin mṛṣṭatety anyathāsiddhiparihārāya nirmṛṣṭarāga iti rāgasya niḥśeṣamṛṣṭatoktā/ punaḥ snānasādhāraṇyavartanena saṃbhogacihnodghāṭanāyādhara iti viśiṣya grahaṇam/ uttaroṣṭhe sarāge 'dharoṣṭhamātrasya nirmṛṣṭarāgatā cumbanakṛtaiva ityādinā, "idam api dhvaner udāharaṇam" ityantena sandarbheṇa/ "taṭādighaṭitā vākyārthāḥ snānavyāvṛttidvārā saṃbhogāṅgānām āśleṣacumbanādīnāṃ pratipādanena pradhānavyaṅgyavyañjane sāhāyakam ācaranti iti, tad etad alaṃkāraśāstratattvānavabodhanibandhanam/ prācīnasakalagranthaviruddhatvād upapattivirodhāc ca/ tathā hi-- pañcamollāsaśeṣe "niḥśeṣetyādau gamakatayā yāni candanacyavanādīny upāttāni tāni kāraṇāntarato 'pi bhavanti/ yataś cātraiva snānakāryatvenopāttānīti nopabhoga eva pratibaddhānīty anaikāntikāni iti kāvyaprakāśakṛtoktam/ tathā tatraiva tena--
"bhama dhammia vīsattho so suṇao ajja mālido teṇa/
golāṇaikacchakuḍaṅgavāsiṇā dariasīheṇa//"
ityādau liṅgajaliṅgijñānarūpeṇānumānena vyaktiṃ gatārthayato vyaktivivekakṛto mataṃ pratyācakṣāṇena vyabhicāritvenāsiddhatvena ca saṃdihyamānād api liṅgād vyañjanam abhyupagatam/ ittham eva ca dhvanikṛtāpi prathamoddyote/ evaṃ ca vyañjakānāṃ sādhāraṇyaṃ pratipādayatāṃ prāmāṇikānāṃ granthaiḥ sahāsādhāraṇyaṃ pratipādayatas tava granthasya virodhaḥ sphuṭaḥ/ kiṃ ca yad idaṃ niḥśeṣetyādyavāntaravākyārthānāṃ vāpīsnānavyāvṛttidvāreṇa vyaṅgyāsādhāraṇyaṃ saṃpādyate tat kim artham iti pṛcchāmaḥ/ vyaṅgyasya vyañjanārtham iti cen na/ vyañjakagatāsādhāraṇyasya vyañjanānupāyatvāt/
body.translated_text: Here, by the expression 'she became dizzy,' the indignation (<s>amarṣa</s>) — [whose meaning is] 'What is this inappropriate thing he has done without consideration?' — is principally suggested, since it is the resting-place of aesthetic relish (<s>carvaṇā-viśrānti-dhāma</s>). Therein, both the word (<s>śabda</s>) and the meaning (<s>artha</s>) are subordinate. Or, [consider] another [example]: 'She who, even when lying on the bed, the slender one, could not endure even the mere contact of [his] breath — she now slowly pushes away the hand of her beloved placed upon her heart.' This verse, being part of a poetic composition authored by me, is [here] explained only briefly with reference to what precedes. The new bride, who, lying on the couch, had become [so sensitive that] her body-creeper contracted at the mere contact of breath — she now, on the night preceding [his] departure, being one whose husband is about to depart, slowly pushes away the hand placed on her heart by her beloved, who [placed it there] with apprehension — [she pushes it away] out of the natural disposition of a new bride, but only slowly. Here, through the slow pushing-away — whose nature is the gradual restoring to its place — the permanent emotion (<s>sthāyin</s>) called <s>rati</s> (love) is suggested in the mode of being apprehended gradually (<s>saṃlakṣyakrama</s>). And it will be demonstrated that even the <s>sthāyin</s> (permanent emotion) and the rest are suggestible through the mode of gradual apprehension. This is the very subdivision that they call <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion). Now, as for what was stated by <s>Appayya Dīkṣita</s> in the <s>Citramīmāṃsā</s> in the course of explaining the verse 'the sandal-paste completely fallen off' as an example of <s>dhvani</s>: 'The word "completely" (<s>niḥśeṣa</s>) is used to prevent the alternative explanation that the sandal-paste fell off due to the pulling of the upper garment. Then, the word "bank" (<s>taṭa</s>) [is used] to indicate signs of sexual union by excluding the commonality [of sandal-paste falling off] with bathing — for in bathing, sandal-paste falls off everywhere, but yours is seen only on the upper part (<s>taṭa</s>) of the breasts; this [falling off] is caused by embrace alone. Likewise, in "the color has been wiped off [from] the lip," the expression "completely wiped off" (<s>nirmṛṣṭarāga</s>) indicates the complete removal of the [lip] color — to prevent the alternative explanation that the earlier color [merely] faded somewhat due to the delay in chewing betel. Then, to indicate signs of sexual union by excluding commonality with bathing, the specification "lip" (<s>adhara</s>) is used — since the lower lip alone having its color removed, while the upper lip retains its color, is caused by kissing alone' — and so on, ending with 'This too is an example of <s>dhvani</s>.' [<s>Jagannātha</s> responds:] 'The sentence-meanings constructed through "bank" (<s>taṭa</s>) and the like assist in the suggestion of the principal <s>vyaṅgya</s> (suggested meaning) by indicating — through the exclusion of bathing — the elements of sexual union such as embrace and kissing.' But this [interpretation] is grounded in a failure to understand the true nature of <s>alaṃkāra-śāstra</s> (the science of rhetoric), since it contradicts all earlier texts and is logically untenable. For as follows: at the end of the fifth <s>ullāsa</s> [of the <s>Kāvyaprakāśa</s>], [<s>Mammaṭa</s> states:] 'In the [verse] "completely" etc., those [details] such as the falling off of sandal-paste, which were taken up as indicators (<s>gamaka</s>), can also arise from other causes. And since here they are taken up as effects of bathing alone, they are not bound exclusively to sexual enjoyment — thus they are inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>).' This was stated by the author of the <s>Kāvyaprakāśa</s>. And similarly, in that very [work], in explaining [the verse in Prakrit] '<s>bhama dhammia vīsattho</s>...' etc. — where the meaning sought through inference based on indicative sign and indicated thing is refuted — [<s>Mammaṭa</s>], rejecting the view of the author of the <s>Vyaktiviveka</s>, accepted suggestion (<s>vyañjana</s>) even from a doubtful sign — [one that is] subject to the charge of inconclusiveness (<s>vyabhicāritva</s>) and unestablished-ness (<s>asiddhatva</s>). And the author of the <s>Dhvani</s> [<s>Ānandavardhana</s>] [said] the same in the first <s>uddyota</s> (chapter). Thus, the contradiction between your work — which establishes the non-commonality [of suggestive elements] — and the works of the authoritative [authors] who establish their commonality is manifest. Moreover, we ask: for what purpose is the non-commonality of the subordinate sentence-meanings in 'completely' etc. [sought to be] established through the exclusion of bathing in a pool? If [you say:] 'For the purpose of suggesting the suggested meaning' — [we reply:] no, because non-commonality pertaining to the suggestive [element] is not a means of suggestion.

body.text:
"auṇiddaṃ dobballaṃ cintā alasaṃtaṇaṃ saṇīsasiam
maha mandabhāiṇīe keraṃ sahi tuha paribhavai//"
ityādau sādhāraṇānām evaunnidryādīnāṃ vaktrādivaiśiṣṭyavaśād arthaviśeṣavyañjakatāyā abhyupagateḥ/ pratyutāsādhāraṇyasya vyāptyaparaparyāyasyānumānānukūlatayā vyaktipratikūlatvāc ca/ atha taṭādighaṭitatve 'pi na niḥśeṣetyādivākyārthānām asādhāraṇyam/ salilārdravasanakaraṇakaproñchanādināpi tatsambhavād iti cet tarhi vāpīsnānavyāvartanena kaḥ puruṣārthaḥ/ ekatrānaikāntikatvasyeva bahuṣv anaikāntikatāyā api jñātāyā anumitipratikūlatvād vyaktyapratikūlatvāc ca/ api cātra hi tadantikam eva rantuṃ gatāsīti vyaṅgyaśarīre tadantikagamanaṃ ramaṇarūpaphalāṃśaś ceti dvayaṃ ghaṭakam/ tatra tāvat tadantikaṃ gatāsītyaṃśasya tvanmate vyaṅgyatvaṃ durupapādam/ tvaduktarītyā viśeṣaṇavākyārthānāṃ niḥśeṣetyādipratipādyānāṃ vācyārthe vāpīsnāne bādhitatvād vācyakakṣāgatapradhānavākyārthībhūtavidhiniṣedhapratipādakābhyāṃ gatā na gateti śabdābhyāṃ virodhilakṣaṇayā niṣedhasya vidheś ca pratīter upapatteḥ/ na hi mukhyārthabādhenonmīlite 'rthe vyaktivedyatocitā/ yathā "aho pūrṇaṃ saro yatra luṭhantaḥ snānti mānavāḥ" ityatra kartṛviśeṣaṇānupapattyadhīnollāse pūrṇatvābhāve/
atha tadantikagamanasya lakṣaṇāvedyatve 'pi ramaṇasya phalāṃśasya lakṣyaśaktimūladhvananavedyatvam avyāhatam eveti cet, "adhamatvam aprakṛṣṭatvaṃ tac ca jātyā karmaṇā vā bhavati/ tatra jātyāpakarṣaṃ nottamanāyikā nāyakasya vākti" ityādinā saṃdarbheṇa bhavataivārthāpattivedyatāyāḥ sphuṭaṃ vacanāt/ anyalabhyasyaca śabdārthatāyā asvīkṛteḥ/ anyac ca yathā kathaṃcid aṅgīkuru vātra vyañjanāvyāpāraṃ tathāpi na taveṣṭasiddhiḥ/ vācyānāṃ
niḥśeṣacyutacandanastanataṭatvādīnām adhamatvasya ca tvaduktarītyā prakārāntareṇānupapadyamānatayā dūtīsaṃbhogamātraniṣpādyatvena guṇībhūtavyaṅgyatvaprasaṅgāt/ evaṃ copapattivirodho 'pi sphuṭatara eva/ tasmād vācyārthasādhāraṇyam evocitam atividagdhanāyikānirūpitānāṃ viśeṣaṇavākyārthānām/ tathā hi-- ayi bāndhavajanasyājñātapīḍāgame svārthaparāyaṇe snānakālātikramabhayavaśena nadīmadīyapriyayor antikam agatvaiva vāpīṃ snātum ito mamāntikād gatāsi, na punas tasya paravedanānabhijñatayā duḥkhadātṛtvenādhamasyāntikam/ yato niḥśeṣacyutacandanaṃ stanayos taṭam eva noraḥsthalam, vāpīgatabahulayuvajanatrapāpāravaśyād aṃśadvayalagnāgrasvastikīkṛtabhujalatāyugalena taṭasyaivonnatatayā muhur āmarṣāt/ evaṃ tvarayā samyag akṣālanenottaroṣṭho na nirmṛṣṭarāgo 'dharas tu tadapekṣayā gaṇḍūṣajalaradanaśodhanāṅgulyādīnām adhikasaṃmardam āvahatīti tathā/ kiṃ ca samyag akṣālanena netre jalamātrasaṃsagad dūram uparibhāga evānañjane/ śītavaśāt tānavāc ca tava tanuḥ pulakiteti/ evaṃ tasyā vidagdhāyā gūḍhatātparyaivoktir ucitā, anyathā vaidagdhyabhaṅgāpatteḥ/ evaṃ sādhāraṇoṣv eṣu vākyārtheṣu mukhyārthe bādhābhāvāt tātparyārthasya jhaṭity anākalanāt kuto 'tra lakṣaṇāvakāśaḥ/ anantaraṃ ca vācyārthapratipatter vaktṛboddhavyanāyakādīnāṃ vaiśiṣṭyasya pratītau satyām adhamapadena svapravṛttiprayojako duḥkhadātṛtvarūpo dharmaḥ sādhāraṇātmā vācyārthadaśayām aparādhāntarānimittakaduḥkhadātṛtvarūpeṇa sthito vyañjanāvyāpāreṇa dūtīsaṃbhoganimittakaduḥkhadātṛtvākāreṇa paryavasyatīty ālaṃkārikasiddhāntaniṣkarṣaḥ/ etena "adhamatvam apakṛṣṭatvaṃ tac ca jātyā karmaṇā vā bhavati/ tatra jātyāpakarṣaṃ nottamanāyikā nāyakasya vakti/ nāpi svāparādhaparyavasāyidūtīsaṃbhogādihīnakarmātiriktena karmaṇā/ tādṛśaṃ ca dūtīsaṃpreṣaṇāt prācīnaṃ
soḍham eveti nodghāṭanārham itītaravyāvṛtyā saṃbhogarūpam eva paryavasyati" iti yad uktam, tad api nirastam/ vidagdhottamanāyikāyāḥ sakhīsamakṣaṃ tadupabhogarūpasya svanāyakāparādhasya sphuṭaṃ prakāśayitum atitamām anaucityena prācīnānām eva soḍhānām apy aparādhānām asahyatayā dūtīṃ prati pratipipādayiṣitatvād iti dik/
yatra vyaṅgyam apradhānam eva saccamatkārakāraṇaṃ tad dvitīyam//
body.translated_text: "The heat has made [me] weak, anxiety has made [me] languid, [my body is] covered with perspiration—O friend, in how many ways does my slow-moving one [i.e., the <s>mandabhāginī</s> (slow-fortuned one)] put you to shame!" In this and similar [verses], since it is accepted that the general (<s>sādhāraṇa</s>) [qualities] such as lassitude and so forth, by virtue of the distinguishing characteristics of the speaker and others, have the capacity to suggest (<s>vyañjakatā</s>) particular meanings; and conversely, because non-generality (<s>asādhāraṇya</s>), which is another name for pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>), while favorable to inference (<s>anumāna</s>), is contrary to poetic suggestion (<s>vyakti</s>). Now, if one objects that even though [the actions are] connected with the bank and so forth, the sentence-meanings such as "completely" and so forth are non-general, since those [effects] could also arise from wiping off with a cloth moistened with water and the like—then what purpose is served by specifying a return from bathing in the tank? Because just as the fallacy of inconclusiveness (<s>anaikāntikatva</s>) in one case, so too the inconclusiveness recognized in many cases is contrary to inference but not contrary to poetic suggestion. Moreover, here in the body of the suggested meaning (<s>vyaṅgya</s>)—namely that "she had gone to his very presence to enjoy him"—two elements are constituent: the going to his presence, and the enjoyment (<s>ramaṇa</s>) as the result-portion. Now, of these, the suggestedness of the element "she had gone to his presence" is difficult to establish on your view. Because, according to the method you have stated, since the qualifier-sentence-meanings—those conveyed by [expressions like] "completely" and so forth—are sublated (<s>bādhita</s>) with respect to the denoted meaning (<s>vācyārtha</s>), namely bathing in the tank, [those meanings] are cognized through <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (indication) of contradiction, by means of the words "went" and "did not go" which convey affirmation and negation as the principal sentence-meaning belonging to the level of the denoted. For when a meaning is revealed through sublation of the primary meaning (<s>mukhyārthabādha</s>), it is not proper for it to be cognized through suggestion (<s>vyakti</s>). Just as in "Ah, the lake is full, where people roll about and bathe," the absence of fullness [is understood] when the flash [of meaning] depends on the impossibility of the qualifier of the agent. Now, if one says that even though the going to his presence is cognized through <s>lakṣaṇā</s>, the enjoyment-as-result portion is cognized through <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion) rooted in the power of indication (<s>lakṣyaśaktimūla</s>), and this remains unobstructed—[we reply:] because you yourself have clearly stated in the passage beginning "Baseness means non-excellence, and that arises either from birth or from action; of these, the excellent <s>nāyikā</s> (heroine) does not speak of the <s>nāyaka</s>'s (hero's) degradation by birth" and so forth, that it is cognized through presumption (<s>arthāpatti</s>); and because the status of word-meaning has not been accepted for what is obtainable through other means. Furthermore, even if you somehow accept the operation of <s>vyañjanā</s> (suggestion) here, still your desired conclusion does not follow. Because the denoted meanings—such as the chest being completely devoid of sandal paste, and so forth—and the baseness, according to the method you have stated, being inexplicable in any other way, are accomplished merely through the messenger-liaison (<s>dūtīsaṃbhoga</s>), and thus the undesired consequence of <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> (subordinated suggestion) would arise. And thus the contradiction with logical reasoning is all the more evident. Therefore, generality (<s>sādhāraṇya</s>) of the denoted meaning is indeed appropriate for the qualifier-sentence-meanings attributed to the exceedingly clever <s>nāyikā</s> (<s>atividagdhā nāyikā</s>). That is to say: "O you who are intent upon your own interests, heedless of the suffering of your kinsmen, arriving at an unknown [time], out of fear of missing the time for bathing, without going near the river or my beloved, you went from here, from my presence, to bathe in the tank—and not to the presence of that base one who, being ignorant of others' pain, is a giver of suffering. Therefore the chest-region of [your] breasts is completely devoid of sandal paste and not the chest [of the lover]; because of modesty arising from the multitude of young men present at the tank, the vine-like pair of arms, with their tips joined in a <s>svastika</s> pattern clinging to both sides, [show] that the chest-region itself is elevated, [hence the rubbing is] repeatedly out of vexation. Likewise, due to hasty and improper washing, the upper lip has not had its color wiped off, while the lower lip [has], since gargling water and tooth-cleaning with the finger and the like apply greater pressure to it. Moreover, due to improper washing, the eyes, from mere contact with water, are far above unannointed. Due to cold and thinness, your body has goosebumps." Thus, speech with concealed purport (<s>gūḍhatātparya</s>) is fitting for that clever [<s>nāyikā</s>], since otherwise the cleverness (<s>vaidagdhya</s>) would be destroyed. Thus, since in these general sentence-meanings there is no sublation of the primary meaning, and since the intended meaning (<s>tātparyārtha</s>) is not immediately grasped, where is there scope for <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (indication) here? And then, after cognition of the denoted meaning, when the distinguishing characteristics of the speaker, the one to be informed, the <s>nāyaka</s>, and others are cognized, the quality expressed by the word "base" (<s>adhama</s>)—namely the general (<s>sādhāraṇa</s>) attribute of being a giver of suffering that motivates one's own conduct—which at the level of the denoted meaning stands as giving suffering for reasons other than [his] offense, through the operation of <s>vyañjanā</s> (suggestion) culminates in the form of giving suffering caused by the messenger-liaison (<s>dūtīsaṃbhoga</s>). This is the established conclusion of <s>alaṃkāra</s> theory. By this, what was stated—"Baseness means non-excellence, and that arises either from birth or from action; of these, the excellent <s>nāyikā</s> does not speak of the <s>nāyaka</s>'s degradation by birth; nor by any action other than inferior conduct culminating in messenger-liaison and the like due to one's own offense; and such [offenses] prior to the sending of a messenger have been endured, so they are not worth exposing—thus, by exclusion of the other, it culminates precisely in the form of [his] liaison"—that too is refuted. Because the excellent clever <s>nāyikā</s> (<s>vidagdhottamanāyikā</s>), finding it supremely improper to openly reveal before her friend the offense of her own <s>nāyaka</s> in the form of his enjoyment [of another], wishes to convey to the messenger-woman that even previously endured offenses are now unbearable—this is the gist. Where the suggested meaning (<s>vyaṅgya</s>) is subordinate yet is the cause of aesthetic delight (<s>camatkāra</s>), that is the second type [of <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s>].

body.text:
vācyāpekṣayā pradhānībhūtaṃ vyaṅgyāntaram ādaya guṇībhūtaṃ vyaṅgyam ādāyātivyāptivāraṇāyāvadhāraṇam/ tena tasya dhvanitvam eva/ līnavyaṅgyavācyacitrātiprasaṅgavāraṇāya camatkāretyādi/ yat tu "atādṛśi guṇībhūtavyaṅgyam" ityādi kāvyaprakāśagatalakṣaṇe citrānyatvaṃ ṭīkākārair dattam, tan na/ paryāyoktasamāsoktyādipradhānakāvyeṣv avyāptyāpatteḥ/ teṣāṃ guṇībhūtavyaṅgatāyāś citratāyāś ca sarvālaṃkārikasaṃmatatvāt/
udāharaṇam--
"rāghavavirahajvālāsaṃtāpitasahyaśailaśikhareṣu/
śiśire sukhaṃ śayānāḥ kapayaḥ kupyanti pavanatanayāya//"
atra jānakīkuśalāvedanena rāghavaḥ śiśirīkṛta iti vyaṅgyam ākasmikakapikartṛkahanumadviṣayakakopopapādakatayā guṇībhūtam api durdāivavaśato dāsyam anubhavad rājakalatram iva kām api kamanīyatām āvahati/
nanv evaṃ prāg uktam ākṣepagataṃ māndyam api navavadhūprakṛtivirodhād anupapadyamānaṃ vyaṅgyenaivopapādyata iti katham uttamottamatā tasya kāvyasyeti cet, na/ yato hy anudinasakhyupadeśādibhir anaticamatkāribhir apy upapadyamānaṃ māndyam idaṃ
prathamacittacumbinīṃ vipralambharatim aprakāśayan na prabhavati svātantryeṇa paranirvṛticarvaṇāgocaratām ādhātum/ ittham eva niḥśeṣacyutacandanam ityādipadyeṣv adhamatvādīni vācyāni vyaṅgyātiriktenārthenāpātato niṣpannaśarīrāṇi vyañjakānīti na tatrāpi guṇībhāvaḥ śaṅkanīyaḥ/ anayor bhedayor anapahnavanīyacamatkārayor api prādhānyāprādhānyābhyām asti kaścit sahṛdayavedyo viśeṣaḥ/
yat tu citramīmāṃsākṛtoktam--
praharaviratau madhye vāhnastato 'pi pareṇa vā
kim uta sakale yāte vāhni priya tvam ihaiṣyasi/
iti dinaśataprāpyaṃ deśaṃ priyasya yiyāsato
harati gamanaṃ bālālāpaiḥ sabāṣpagalajjalaiḥ//
body.translated_text: The qualification "taking another suggested meaning (<s>vyaṅgya</s>) that has become predominant relative to the denoted meaning (<s>vācya</s>)" is for the purpose of preventing over-extension, [namely] taking <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> (subordinated suggestion) [where there is already predominant suggestion]. Therefore, that [predominant suggestion] is indeed <s>dhvani</s> (resonance). The [phrase] "of <s>camatkāra</s> (aesthetic wonder)" and so forth is for preventing the undesired consequence of [including] hidden suggestion (<s>līnavyaṅgya</s>), denoted meaning (<s>vācya</s>), and <s>citra</s> (pictorial/ornamental poetry). Now, as for the definition given in the <s>Kāvyaprakāśa</s>—"that which is not of that kind is <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s>"—the commentators have interpreted "otherness from <s>citra</s>" [as the distinguishing criterion], but that is incorrect. Because there would be the fault of non-inclusion (<s>avyāpti</s>) with respect to poetry in which figures such as <s>paryāyokta</s> (circumlocution) and <s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression) are predominant. Since the status of those [poems] as <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> and as <s>citra</s> is accepted by all <s>alaṃkārikas</s> (poeticians). An example: "On the peaks of <s>Sahya</s> mountain, scorched by the flames of <s>Rāghava</s>'s (<s>Rāma</s>'s) separation [from <s>Sītā</s>], the monkeys who had been sleeping comfortably in the cool [air] are angry at the son of the Wind (<s>Hanumān</s>)." Here, the suggested meaning—that <s>Rāghava</s> was cooled by the news of <s>Jānakī</s>'s (<s>Sītā</s>'s) well-being—though subordinated (<s>guṇībhūta</s>) by serving as the ground for establishing the sudden anger of the monkeys directed at <s>Hanumān</s>, nevertheless, by force of ill fortune, brings about a certain captivating beauty, like a royal consort experiencing servitude [yet retaining her inherent dignity]. Now, if one objects: thus, the dullness (<s>māndya</s>) mentioned earlier in the context of objection, which is inexplicable due to its contradiction with the nature of a new bride, is established only through suggestion (<s>vyaṅgya</s>)—so how can that poem be of the highest excellence (<s>uttamottama</s>)?—[we reply:] No. Because this dullness, though explicable through everyday [causes] such as repeated advice from friends and the like, which do not produce much <s>camatkāra</s> (aesthetic wonder), [when explained thus] does not reveal the heart-touching <s>vipralambha rati</s> (love-in-separation) and therefore cannot independently bring about the state of being an object of another's blissful aesthetic savoring (<s>paranirvṛticarvaṇā</s>). In exactly this way, in verses such as "the chest completely devoid of sandal paste" and so forth, the denoted meanings such as baseness and the like, having their form readily established through a meaning beyond the suggested, are [themselves] the suggestors (<s>vyañjaka</s>)—therefore in those cases too, subordination (<s>guṇībhāva</s>) should not be suspected. Between these two types [of <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s>], though both possess undeniable <s>camatkāra</s>, there is a certain difference perceptible to the <s>sahṛdaya</s> (connoisseur) in terms of predominance and non-predominance. Now, as for what the author of the <s>Citramīmāṃsā</s> has stated: "When one watch of the day has passed, or in the middle, or after the next, or indeed when the entire day has gone—O beloved, will you come here?" Thus, the departure of the beloved who wishes to go to a place reachable only in a hundred days is arrested by the childish prattle [of the young wife], accompanied by tears streaming down [her face].

body.text:
ity atra sakalam ahaḥ paramāvadhis tataḥ paraṃ prāṇāndhārayituṃ na śaknomīti vyaṅgyaṃ priyagamananivāraṇarūpavācyasiddhyaṅgam ato guṇībhūtavyaṅgyam" iti/ tan na/ sa bāṣpagalajjalānāṃ praharaviratāv ityādyālāpānām eva priyagamananivāraṇarūpavācyasiddhyaṅgatayā vyaṅgyasya guṇībhāvābhāvāt/ ālāpair iti tṛtīyayā prakṛtyarthasya haraṇakriyākaraṇatāyāḥ sphuṭaṃ pratipatteḥ/ na ca vyaṅgyasyāpi vācyasiddhyaṅgatātra saṃbhavatīti tathoktam iti vācyam/ niḥśeṣacyutacandam ityādāv ivādhamatvarūpavācyasiddhyaṅgyatāyā dūtīsaṃbhogādau saṃbhavād guṇībhāvāpatteḥ/ astu vā tataḥ paraṃ prāṇān dhārayituṃ na śaknomīti vyaṅgyasya vācyasiddhyaṅgatayā guṇībhāvas tathāpi nāyakāder vibhāvasya bāṣpāder anubhāvasya cittāvegādeś ca saṃcāriṇaḥ saṃyogād abhivyajyamānena vipralambhena dhvanitvaṃ ko nivārayet/
yatra vyaṅgyacamatkārāsamānādhikaraṇo
vācyacamatkāras tattṛtīyam//
body.translated_text: In this [verse], 'the whole day' is the maximum limit; beyond that, 'I am unable to sustain my life-breaths' — this is the suggested meaning (<s>vyaṅgya</s>), which serves as a subsidiary to the expressed meaning (<s>vācya</s>) that takes the form of prevention of the beloved's departure; hence [this is a case of] subordinated suggestion (<s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s>).' This is not correct. The suggested meaning does not become subordinated, because it is the very utterances such as 'tears, flowing water, at the pause of a [single] watch (<s>prahara</s>)' etc. that serve as subsidiaries to the expressed meaning of preventing the beloved's departure. Through the instrumental case in 'by [these] utterances,' the fact that the natural meaning — [namely, that the utterances are] the instrument of the action of removal — is clearly understood. And one cannot say that here the suggested meaning too could serve as a subsidiary to the expressed meaning — because [in verses] like 'the departed, fierce [heat of passion]' etc., the possibility of serving as a subsidiary to the expressed meaning in its lowest form, as in the case of the messenger and the enjoyment of the [heroine's] company, would lead to the [unwanted] consequence of subordination. Or, let it be that the suggested meaning 'I cannot sustain my life-breaths beyond that' is subordinated by serving as a subsidiary to the expressed meaning; even so, who could prevent the <s>dhvani</s> (suggestiveness) of <s>vipralambha</s> (<s>śṛṅgāra</s> in separation), which is manifested by the combination of the <s>vibhāva</s> (excitant) such as the hero etc., the <s>anubhāva</s> (consequent) such as tears etc., and the <s>saṃcārin</s> (transitory emotion) such as mental agitation etc.? Where the delight (<s>camatkāra</s>) of the expressed meaning is co-located with [but not subordinate to] the delight of the suggested meaning — that is the third [type of poetry]. //

body.text:
yathā yamunāvarṇane--"tanayamainākagaveṣaṇalambīkṛtajaladhijaṭharapraviṣṭahimagiribhujāyamānāyā bhagavatyā bhāgīrathyāḥ sakhī" iti/ atrotprekṣā vācyaiva camatkṛtihetuḥ/ śvaityapātālatalacumbitvādīnāṃ camatkāro leśatayā sann apy utprekṣācamatkṛtijaṭharanilīno nāgariketaranāyikākalpitakāśmīradravāṅgarāgani gīrṇo nijāṅgagaurim eva pratīyate/ na tādṛśo 'sti ko 'pi vācyārtho yo manāg anāmṛṣṭapratīyamāna eva svato ramaṇīyatām ādhātuṃ prabhavati/ anayor eva dvitīyatṛtīyabhedayor jāgarūkājāgarūkaguṇībhūtavyaṅgyayoḥ praviṣṭaṃ nikhilam alaṃkārapradhānaṃ kāvyam/
yatrārthacamatkṛtyupaskṛtā śabdacamatkṛtiḥ pradhānaṃ tad adhamaṃ caturtham// yathā--
"mitrātriputranetrāya trayīśātravaśatrave/
gotrārigotrajatrāya gotrātre te namo namaḥ//" iti/
atrārthacamatkṛtiḥ śabdacamatkṛtau līnā/ yady api yatrārthacamatkṛtisāmānyaśūnyā śabdacamatkṛtis tatpañcamam adhamādhamam api kāvyavidhāsu gaṇayitum ucitam, yathaikākṣarapadyārdhāvṛttiyamakapadmabandhādi, tathāpi ramaṇīyārthapratipādakaśabdatārūpakāvyasāmānyalakṣaṇānākrāntatayā vastutaḥ kāvyatvābhāvena mahākavibhiḥ pracīnaparamparām anurundhānais tatra tatra kāvyeṣu nibaddham api nāsmābhir gaṇitam, vastusthiter evānurodhyatvāt/ kecid imān api caturo bhedān agaṇayanta uttamamadhyamādhamabhāvena trividham eva kāvyam ācakṣate/ tatrārthacitraśabdacitrayor aviśeṣeṇādhamatvam ayuktaṃ vaktum, tāratamyasya sphuṭam upalabdheḥ/ ko hy evaṃ sahṛdayaḥ san "vinirgataṃ mānadam ātmamandirāt", "sa cchinnamūlaḥ kṣatajena reṇuḥ" ityādibhiḥ kāvyaiḥ "svacchandocchalad" ityādīnāṃ pāmaraślāghyānām aviśeṣaṃ brūyāt/ saty api tāratamye yady ekabhedatvaṃ kas tarhi dhvaniguṇībhūtavyaṅgyor īṣadantarayor vibhinnabhedatve durāgrahaḥ/ yatra ca
śabdārthacamatkṛtyor aikādhikaraṇyaṃ tatra tayor guṇapradhānabhāvaṃ paryālocya yathālakṣaṇaṃ vyavahartavyam/ samaprādhānye tu madhyamataiva/
yathā--
"ullāsaḥ phullapaṅkeruhapaṭalapatanmattapuṣpaṃdhayānāṃ
nistāraḥ śokadāvānalavikalahṛdāṃ kokasīmantinīnām/
utpātas tāmasānām upahatamahasāṃ cakṣuṣāṃ pakṣapātaḥ
saṃghātaḥ ko 'pi dhāmnām ayam udayagiriprāntataḥ prādurāsīt//"
atra vṛttyanuprāsaprācuryād ojoguṇaprakāśakatvāc ca śabdasya, prasādaguṇayogād anantaram evādhigatasya rūpakasya hetvalaṃkārasya vā vācyasya, camatkṛtyos tulyaskandhatvāt samam eva prādhānyam/
tatra dhvaner uttamottamasyāsaṃkhyabhedasyāpi sāmānyataḥ ke 'pi bhedā nirūpyante-- dvividho dhvaniḥ, abhidhāmūlo lakṣaṇāmūlaś ca/ tatrādyās trividhaḥ/ rasavastvalaṃkāradhvanibhedāt/ rasadhvanir ityalakṣyakramopalakṣaṇād rasabhāvatadābhāsabhāvaśāntibhāvodayabhāvasaṃdhibhāvaśabalatvānāṃ grahaṇam/ dvitīyaś ca dvivīdhaḥ/ arthāntarasaṃkramitavācyo 'tyantatiraskṛtavācyaś ca/ evaṃ pañcātmake dhvanau paramaramaṇīyatayā rasadhvanes tadātmā rasas tāvad abhidhīyate--
body.translated_text: For example, in the description of the <s>Yamunā</s>: 'The companion of the divine <s>Bhāgīrathī</s> (<s>Gaṅgā</s>), who [like a woman] entered the belly of the ocean that has been made to hang down in the search for her son <s>Mainākā</s>, [and thus] assumed the form of the <s>Himālaya</s>'s arms.' Here, the poetic fancy (<s>utprekṣā</s>) is the very expressed meaning that causes delight. The delight of whiteness, [the river's] touching the bottom of the nether world, and such [features], though present in a slight degree, is absorbed into the belly of the <s>utprekṣā</s>-delight — just as a coating of saffron paste, imagined [to be applied on the body] by a heroine other than the sophisticated one (<s>nāgarī</s>), when smeared [over] the fair limbs, is perceived [only] as [enhancing] the natural fairness of [her] own limbs. There is no such expressed meaning that, being perceived even slightly without being tasted [poetically], is capable of establishing beauty by itself. Within these two varieties — the second and the third — which are [respectively] the alert (<s>jāgarūka</s>) and the non-alert subordinated suggestion — the entirety of poetry in which ornament (<s>alaṃkāra</s>) predominates is included. Where the delight of verbal form (<s>śabdacamatkṛti</s>), enhanced by the delight of meaning (<s>arthacamatkṛti</s>), predominates — that is the fourth, the lowest [type]. // For example: 'Homage, homage to you — [you who are] the eye for the sons of <s>Mitra</s>, the enemy of the hundreds of foes of the three [<s>Vedas</s>], the destroyer of the families of the enemies of the family, the mountain-destroyer!' Here the delight of meaning is absorbed in the delight of verbal form. Even though it would be fitting to count as a fifth, lowest-of-the-lowest [type], that in which the verbal delight is devoid of any trace of delight of meaning — such as single-syllable verses, half-verse repetitions, <s>yamaka</s> (chiming), lotus-diagrams, and the like — nevertheless, since it is not encompassed by the general definition of poetry as 'language conveying beautiful meaning,' and since it is in truth not poetry at all, it is not counted by us, even though it has been composed here and there in poems by great poets following ancient tradition — for one should conform to the nature of things alone. Some, not counting even these four divisions, declare poetry to be only threefold, as best, middling, and lowest. But there, to declare the pictorial-in-meaning (<s>arthacitraḥ</s>) and the pictorial-in-word (<s>śabdacitraḥ</s>) as equally lowest is incorrect, since a gradation [between them] is clearly perceived. For what connoisseur (<s>sahṛdaya</s>), being a person of taste, would declare no difference between poems like 'The pride went forth from its own abode,' 'He, with severed roots, [stained] by blood-rain,' etc., and those beginning with 'freely surging' etc., which are praiseworthy [only] to the vulgar? Even if there is a gradation, if [you insist on] placing [them in] one category, then why the obstinate insistence on making a separate category for <s>dhvani</s> and <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s>, which differ only slightly? And where there is co-location of the delights of word and meaning, there, having considered which is the quality and which the principal, one should apply the [appropriate] designation according to the [relevant] definition. But in the case of equal predominance, it is [classified as] the middling. // For example: 'The delight of bees intoxicated by the falling petals of blooming lotus clusters, the rescue of the <s>cakravāka</s>-wives whose hearts are afflicted by the forest-fire of grief, the calamity of the darknesses whose light has been attacked, the partiality — a certain indescribable assemblage of radiance appeared from the edge of the sunrise mountain!' Here, because of the abundance of alliterative recurrence (<s>vṛttyanuprāsa</s>) and because the word reveals the quality of vigor (<s>ojas</s>); and because of the quality of lucidity (<s>prasāda</s>) and the immediately grasped metaphor (<s>rūpaka</s>) or the ornament of causation (<s>hetu</s>) as the expressed meaning — the delights are equally balanced; hence the predominance is equal. Therein, of <s>dhvani</s>, which is the highest of the highest and has innumerable varieties, some divisions are determined in general — <s>dhvani</s> is twofold: based on denotation (<s>abhidhāmūla</s>) and based on indication (<s>lakṣaṇāmūla</s>). The first is threefold: by the division into <s>rasa</s>-<s>dhvani</s>, <s>vastu</s>-<s>dhvani</s> (fact-suggestion), and <s>alaṃkāra</s>-<s>dhvani</s> (ornament-suggestion). '<s>Rasa</s>-<s>dhvani</s>' — by this being an illustrative designation of the imperceptible-sequence [type] — the inclusion of <s>rasa</s>, <s>bhāva</s>, <s>tadābhāsa</s> (semblance thereof), <s>bhāvaśānti</s> (subsidence of emotion), <s>bhāvodaya</s> (rise of emotion), <s>bhāvasaṃdhi</s> (juncture of emotions), and <s>bhāvaśabalatva</s> (mixed emotions) is [meant]. The second is also twofold: [that in which] the expressed meaning is transferred to another meaning (<s>arthāntarasaṃkramitavācya</s>), and [that in which] the expressed meaning is completely concealed (<s>atyantatiraskṛtavācya</s>). Thus, <s>dhvani</s> being fivefold, <s>rasa</s> — which is the essence of <s>rasa</s>-<s>dhvani</s> because of its supreme beauty — is first defined:

body.text: samucitalalitasaṃniveśacāruṇā kāvyena samarpitaiḥ sahṛdayahṛdayaṃ praviṣṭais tadīyasahṛdayatāsahakṛtena bhāvanāviśeṣamahimnā vigalitaduṣyantaramaṇītvādibhir alaukikavibhāvānubhāvavyabhicāriśabdavyapadeśyaiḥ śakuntalādibhir ālambanakāraṇaiḥ, candrikādibhir uddīpanakāraṇaiḥ, aśrupātādibhiḥ kāryaiḥ, cintādibhiḥ sahakāribhiś ca saṃbhūya prādurbhāvitenālaukikena vyāpāreṇa tatkālanivartitānandāṃśāvaraṇājñānenāta eva pramuṣṭaparimitapramātṛtvādinijadharmeṇa pramātrā svaprakāśatayā vāstavena nijasvarūpānandena saha gocarīkriyamāṇaḥ pragviniviṣṭavāsanārūpo ratyādir eva rasaḥ//
body.translated_text: <s>Rasa</s> is [the aesthetic experience of] <s>rati</s> (love) and the other [permanent emotions (<s>sthāyibhāvas</s>)], in the form of prior-deposited impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>), that are brought into the field of experience (<s>gocarīkriyamāṇa</s>), together with the genuine bliss of one's own essential nature (<s>nijasvarūpānanda</s>), through self-luminosity (<s>svaprakāśatā</s>), by a perceiver (<s>pramātṛ</s>) whose own qualities of limited subjectivity etc. have been stolen away — and therefore whose covering of the portion of bliss (<s>ānandāṃśāvaraṇa</s>) has been removed for that duration — through a transcendent operation (<s>alaukika-vyāpāra</s>) brought into being collectively by: the sustaining causes (<s>ālambana-kāraṇa</s>) — <s>Śakuntalā</s> and the like — which, through the special power of aesthetic contemplation (<s>bhāvanāviśeṣa</s>) aided by connoisseurship (<s>sahṛdayatā</s>), having entered the heart of the connoisseur when presented through poetry endowed with a fitting, graceful arrangement, have shed their worldly character as '<s>Duṣyanta</s>'s beloved' etc., and are designated by the term 'transcendent excitants' (<s>alaukika-vibhāva</s>); the stimulating causes (<s>uddīpana-kāraṇa</s>) such as moonlight and the like; the effects (<s>kārya</s>) such as the shedding of tears and the like; and the co-operative [transitory emotions] (<s>sahakārin</s>) such as anxiety and the like — all designated by the term 'transcendent consequents' (<s>alaukika-anubhāva</s>) and 'transcurrent emotions' (<s>vyabhicārin</s>). //

body.text:
(1) tathā cāhuḥ- "vyaktaḥ sa tair vibhāvādyaiḥ
sthāyībhāvo rasaḥ smṛtaḥ" iti/ vyakto vyaktiviṣayīkṛtaḥ/ vyaktiś ca bhagnāvaraṇā cit/ yathā hi śarāvādinā pihito dīpas tannivṛttau saṃnihitān padārthān prakāśayati svayaṃ ca prakāśate, evam ātmacaitanyaṃ vibhāvādisaṃvalitān ratyādīn/ antaḥkaraṇadharmāṇāṃ sākṣibhāsyatvābhyupagateḥ/ vibhāvādīnām api svapnaturagādīnām iva raṅgarajatādīnām iva sākṣibhāsyatvam aviruddham/ vyañjakavibhāvādicarvaṇāyā āvaraṇabhaṅgasya votpattivināśābhyām utpattivināśau rase upacaryete varṇanityatāyām iva vyañjakatālvādivyāpārasya gakārādau/ vibhāvādicarvaṇāvadhitvād āvaraṇabhaṅgasya, nivṛttāyāṃ tasyāṃ prakāśasyāvṛtatvād vidyamāno 'pi sthāyī na prakāśate/
yad vā vibhāvādicarvaṇāmāhimnā sahṛdayasya nijasahṛdayatāvaśonmiṣitena tattatsthāyyupahitasvasvarūpānandākārā samādhāv iva yoginaś cittavṛttir upajāyate, tanmayībhavanam iti yāvat/ ānando hy ayaṃ na laukikasukhāntarasādhāraṇaḥ, anantaḥkaraṇavṛttirūpatvāt/ itthaṃ cābhinavaguptamammaṭabhaṭṭādigranthasvārasyena bhagnāvaraṇacidviśiṣṭo ratyādiḥ sthāyī bhāvo rasa iti sthitam/
vastutas tu vakṣyamāṇaśrutisvārasyena ratyādyavacchinna bhagnāvaraṇā cid eva rasaḥ/ sarvathaiva cāsyā viśiṣṭātmano viśeṣaṇaṃ viśeṣyaṃ vā cidaṃśam ādāya nityatvaṃ svaprakāśatvaṃ ca siddham/ ratyādyaṃśam ādāya tv anityatvam itarabhāsyatvaṃ ca/ carvaṇā cāsya cidgatāvaraṇabhaṅga eva prāguktā, tadākārāntaḥkaraṇavṛttir vā/ iyaṃ ca parabrahmāsvādāt samādhervilakṣaṇā, vibhāvādiviṣayasaṃvalitacidānandālambanatvāt/ bhāvyā ca kāvyavyāpāramātrāt/ athāsyāṃ sukhāṃśabhāne kiṃ mānam iti cet samādhāv api tadbhāne kiṃ mānam iti paryanuyogasya tulyatvāt/ "sukham ātyantikaṃ yat tadbuddhigrāhyam atīndriyam", ityādiḥ śabdo 'sti tatra mānam iti cet, asty atrāpi "raso vai saḥ, rasaṃ hy evāyaṃ labdhvānandī bhavati" iti śrutiḥ, sakalasahṛdayapratyakṣaṃ ceti
pramāṇadvayam/
yeyaṃ dvitīyapakṣe tadākāracittavṛttyātmikā rasacarvaṇopanyastā sā śabdavyāpārabhāvyatvāc chābdī/ aparokṣasukhālambanatvāc cāparokṣātmikā/ tattvaṃ vākyajabuddhivat/ ityāhur abhinavaguptācāryapādāḥ/
(2) bhaṭṭanāyakās tu "tāṭasthyena rasapratītāv anāsvādyatvam/ ātmagatatvena tu pratyayo durghaṭaḥ/ śakuntalādīnāṃ sāmājikān pratyavibhāvatvāt/ vinā
vibhāvam anālambanasya rasāder apratipatteḥ/ na ca kāntātvaṃ sādhāraṇavibhāvatāvacchedakamatrāpyastīti vācyam/ aprāmāṇyanīścayānāliṅgitāgamyātvaprakārakajñānavirahasya viśeṣyatāsaṃbandhāvacchinnapratiyogitākasya vibhāvatāvacchedakakoṭāvavaśyaḥ niveśyatvāt/ anyathā svasrāder api kāntātvādinā tattvāpatteḥ/ evam aśocyatvakāpuruṣatvādijñānavirahasya tathāvidhasya karuṇarasādau/
tādṛśajñānānutpādas tu tatpratibandhakāntaranirvacanam antareṇa durupapādaḥ/ svātmani duṣyantādyabhedabuddhir eva tatheti cet, na/ nāyake dharādhaureyatvadhīratvāder ātmani cādhunikatvakāpuruṣatvāder vāidharmyasya sphuṭaṃ pratipatter abhedabodhasyaiva durlabhatvāt/ kiṃ ca keyaṃ pratītiḥ/ pramāṇantarānupasthānāc chābdīti cet, na/ vyāvahārikaśabdāntarajanyanāyakamithunavṛttāntavittīnām ivāsyā apy ahṛdyatvāpatteḥ/ nāpi mānasī/ cintopanītānāṃ teṣām eva padārthānāṃ mānasyāḥ pratīter asyā vailakṣaṇyopalambhāt/ na ca smṛtiḥ/ tathā prāg ananubhavāt/ tasmād abhidhayā niveditāḥ padārthā bhāvakatvavyāpāreṇāgamyātvādirasavirodhijñānapratibandhadvārā kāntātvādirasānukūladharmapuraskāreṇāvasthāpyante/ evaṃ sādhāraṇīkṛteṣu duḥṣyantaśakuntalādeśakālavayovasthādiṣu, paṅgau pūrvavyāpāramahimani, tṛtīyasya bhogakṛttvavyāpārasya mahimnā nigīrṇayo rajastamasor udriktasattvajanitena nijacitsvabhāvanirvṛtiviśrāntilakṣaṇena
sākṣātkāreṇa viṣayīkṛto bhāvanopanītaḥ sādhāraṇātmā ratyādiḥ sthāyī rasaḥ/ tatra bhujyamāno ratyādiḥ, ratyādibhogo vetyubhayam eva rasaḥ/ so 'yaṃ bhogo viṣayasaṃvalanād brahmāsvādasavidhavartītyucyate/ evaṃ ca trayo 'mśāḥ kāvyasya-- "abhidhā bhāvanā caiva tadbhogīkṛtir eva ca" ity āhuḥ/ matasyaitasya pūrvasmān matād bhāvakatvavyāpārāntarasvīkāra eva viśeṣa/ bhogas tu vyaktiḥ/ bhogakṛttvaṃ tu vyañjanād aviśiṣṭam/ anyā tu saiva saraṇiḥ/
(3) navyās tu "kāvye nāṭye ca kavinā naṭena ca prakāśiteṣu vibhāvādiṣu vyañjanavyāpāreṇa duṣyantādau śakuntalādiratau gṛhītāyām anantaraṃ ca sahṛdayatollāsitasya bhāvanāviśeṣarūpasya doṣasya mahimnā kalpitaduṣyantatvāvacchādite svātmany ajñānāvacchinne śuktikāśakala iva rajatakhaṇḍaḥ samutpadyamāno 'nirvacanīyaḥ sākṣibhāsyaḥ śakuntalādiviṣayakaratyādir eva rasaḥ/
ayaṃ ca kāryo doṣaviśeṣasya/ nāśyaś ca tannāśasya/ svottarabhāvinā lokottarāhlādena bhedāgrahāt sukhapadavyapadeśyo bhavati/ svapūrvopasthitena ratyādinā tadagrahāt tadratitvenaikatvādhyavasānād vā vyaṅgyo varṇanīyaś cocyate/ avacchādakaṃ duṣyantatvam apy anirvacanīyam eva/ avacchādakatvaṃ ca ratyādiviśiṣṭabodhe viśeṣyatāvacchedakatvam/ etena duṣyantādiniṣṭhasya ratyāder anāsvādyatvān na rasatvam/ svaniṣṭhasya tu tasya śakuntalādibhir atatsaṃbandhibhiḥ katham abhivyaktiḥ/ svasmin duṣyantādyabhedabuddhis tu bādhabuddhiparāhatetyādikam apāstam/
yad api vibhāvādīnāṃ sādhāraṇyaṃ prācīnair uktaṃ tad api kāvyena śakuntalādiśabdaiḥ śakuntalātvādiprakārakabodhajanakaiḥ pratipādyamāneṣu śakuntalādiṣu doṣaviśeṣakalpanaṃ vinā durupapādam/ ato 'vaśyakalpye doṣaviśeṣe tenaiva svātmani duṣyantādyabhedabuddhir api sūpapādā/
nanv evam api rater astu nāma duṣyanta iva sahṛdaye 'pi sukhaviśeṣajanakatā karuṇarasādiṣu tu sthāyinaḥ śokāder duḥkhajanakatayā prasiddhasya katham iva
sahṛdayāhlādahetutvam/ pratyuta nāyaka iva sahṛdaye 'pi duḥkhajananasyaivaucityāt/ na ca satyasya śokāder duḥkhajanakatvaṃ kḷptaṃ na kalpitasyeti nāyakānām eva duḥkham, na sahṛdayasyeti vācyam/
rajjusarpāder bhayakampādyanutpādakatāpatteḥ/ sahṛdaye rater api kalpitatvena sukhajanakatānupapatteś ceti cet/ satyam/ śṛṅgārapradhānakāvyebhya iva karuṇapradhānakāvyebhyo 'pi yadi kevalāhlāda eva sahṛdayahṛdayapramāṇakas tadā kāryānurodhena kāraṇasya kalpanīyatvāl lokottarakāvyavyāpārasyaivāhlādaprayojakatvam iva duḥkhapratibandhakatvam api kalpanīyam/
atha yady āhlāda iva duḥkham api pramāṇasiddhaṃ tadā pratibandhakatvaṃ na kalpanīyam/ svasvakāraṇavaśāc cobhayam api bhaviṣyati/ atha tatra kavīnāṃ kartum, sahṛdayānāṃ ca śrotum, kathaṃ pravṛttiḥ/ aniṣṭasādhanatvena nivṛtter ucitatvāt/ iti cet/ iṣṭasyādhikyād aniṣṭasya ca nyūnatvāc candanadravalepanādāv iva pravṛtter upapatteḥ/ kevalāhlādavādināṃ tu pravṛttir apratyūhaiva/ aśrupātādayo 'pi tattadānandānubhavasvābhāvyāt/ na tu duḥkhāt/ ata eva bhagavadbhaktānāṃ bhagavadvarṇanākarṇanād aśrupātādaya upapadyante/ na hi tatra jātvapi duḥkhānubhavo 'sti/
na ca karuṇarasādau svātmani śokādimaddaśarathāditādātmyārope yady āhlādas tadā svapnādau saṃnipātādau vā svātmani tadārope 'pi sa syāt/ ānubhavikaṃ ca tatra kevalaṃ duḥkham/ itīhāpi tad eva yuktam iti vācyam/ ayaṃ hi lokottarasya kāvyavyāpārasya mahimā, yatprayojyā aramaṇīyā api śokādayaḥ padārthā āhlādam alaukikaṃ janayanti/
vilakṣaṇo hi kamanīyaḥ kāvyavyāpāraja āsvādaḥ pramāṇāntarajād anubhavāt/ janyatvaṃ ca svajanyabhāvanājanyaratyādiviṣayakatvam/ tena rasāsvādasya kāvyavyāpārājanyatve 'pi na kṣatiḥ/ śakuntalādāv agamyātvajñānotpādas tu svātmani duṣyantādyabhedabuddhyā pratibadhyate" ity āhuḥ/
(4) pare tu "vyañjanavyāpārasyānirvacanīyakhyāteś
cānabhyupagame 'pi prāguktadoṣamahimnā svātmani duṣyantāditādātmyāvagāhī śakuntalādiviṣayakaratyādimadabhedabodho mānasaḥ vilakṣaṇaviṣayitāśālī rasaḥ/ svāpnādis tu tādṛśabodho na kāvyārthacintanajanmeti na rasaḥ/ tena tatra na tādṛśāhlādāpattiḥ/
evam api svasminn avidyamānasya ratyāder anubhavaḥ kathaṃ nāma syāt/ maivam/ na hy ayaṃ laukikasākṣātkāro ratyādeḥ, yenāvaśyaṃ viṣayasadbhāvo 'pekṣaṇīyaḥ syāt/ api tu bhramaḥ/ āsvādanasya rasaviṣayakatvavyavahāras tu ratyādiviṣayakatvālambanaḥ" ity api vadanti/
etaiś ca svātmani duṣyantatvadharmitāvacchedakaśakuntalādiviṣayakarativaiśiṣṭyāvagāhī, svātmatvaviśiṣṭe śakuntalādiviṣayakarativiśiṣṭaduṣyantatādātmyāvagāhī, svātmatvaviśiṣṭe duṣyantatvaśakuntalāviṣayakaratyor vāiśiṣṭyāvagāhī, vā trividho 'pi bodho rasapadārthatayābhyupeyaḥ/ tatra "rater viśeṣaṇībhūtāyāḥ śabdād apratītatvād vyañjanāyāś ca tatpratyāyikāyā anabhyupagamāc ceṣṭādiliṅgakam ādau viśeṣaṇajñānārtham anumānam abhyupeyam/
(5) "mukhyatayā duṣyantādigata eva raso ratyādiḥ kamanīyavibhāvādyabhinayapradarśanakovide duṣyantādyanukartari naṭe samāropya sākṣātkriyate" ity eke/ mate 'smin sākṣātkāro duṣyanto 'yaṃ śakuntalādiviṣayakaratimān" ityādiḥ prāgvad dharmyaṃśe laukika āropyāṃśe tv alaukikaḥ/
(6) duṣyantādigato ratyādir naṭe pakṣe duṣyantatvena gṛhīte vibhāvādibhiḥ kṛtrimair apy akṛtrimatayā gṛhītair bhinne viṣaye 'numitisāmagryā balavattvād anumīyamāno rasaḥ" ity apare/
(7) "vibhāvādayas trayaḥ samuditā rasāḥ" iti katipaye/
(8) "triṣu ya eva camatkārī sa eva raso 'nyathā tu trayo 'pi na" iti bahavaḥ/
(9)
"bhāvyāmāno vibhāva eva rasaḥ ity anye/
(10) "tathā anubhāvas tathā itītare/
(11) "tathā vyabhicāry eva tathā pariṇamati" iti kecit/
tatra "vibhāvānubhāvavyabhicārisaṃyogād rasaniṣpattiḥ" iti sūtraṃ tattanmataparatayā vyākhyāyate-- "vibhāvānubhāvavyabhicāribhiḥ saṃyogād vyañjanād rasasya cidānandaviśiṣṭasthāyyātmanaḥ sthāyyupahitacidānandātmano vā niṣpattiḥ svarūpeṇa prakāśanam" ity ādye/
"vibhāvānubhāvavyabhicāriṇāṃ samyaksādhāraṇātmatayā yogād bhāvakatvavyāpāreṇa bhāvanād rasasya sthāyyupahitasattvodrekaprakāśitasvātmānandarūpasya niṣpattir bhogākhyena sākṣātkāreṇa viṣayīkṛtiḥ" iti dvitīye/
"vibhāvānubhāvavyabhicāriṇāṃ saṃyogād bhāvanāviśeṣarūpād doṣād rasasyānirvacanīyaduṣyantaratyādyātmano niṣpattir utpattiḥ" iti tṛtīye/ "vibhāvādīnāṃ saṃyogāj jñānād rasasya jñānaviśeṣātmano niṣpattir utpattiḥ" iti caturthe/ vibhāvādīnāṃ saṃbandhād rasasya ratyāder niṣpattir āropaḥ iti pañcame/
vibhāvādibhiḥ kṛtrimair apy akṛtrimatayā gṛhītaiḥ saṃyogād anumānād rasasya ratyāder niṣpattir anumitir naṭādau pakṣa iti śeṣaḥ" iti ṣaṣṭhe/ "vibhāvādīnāṃ trayāṇāṃ saṃyogāt samudāyād rasaniṣpattī rasapadavyavahāraḥ" iti saptame/ "vibhāvādiṣu samyagyogāc camatkārāt" ity aṣṭame/ tad evaṃ paryavasitas triṣu mateṣu sūtravirodhaḥ/
vibhāvānubhāvavyabhicāriṇām ekasya tu rasāntarasādhāraṇatayā niyatarasavyañjakatānupapatteḥ sūtre militānām upādānam/ evaṃ ca prāmāṇike militānāṃ vyañjakatve yatra kvacid ekasmād evāsādhāraṇād rasodbodhas tatretaradvayam ākṣepyam/ ato nānaikāntikatvam/ itthaṃ nānājātīyābhiḥ
śemuṣībhir nānārūpatayāvasito 'pi manīṣibhiḥ paramāhlādāvinābhāvitayā pratīyamānaḥ prapañce 'smin raso ramaṇīyatām āvahatīti nirvivādam/
sa ca--
"śṛṅgāraḥ karuṇaḥ śānto raudro vīro 'dbhutas tathā/
hāsyo bhayānakaś caiva bībhatsaś ceti te nava//"
ity ukter navadhā/ munivacanaṃ cātra mānam/
kecit tu--
"śāntasya śamasādhyatvān naṭe ca tadasaṃbhavāt/
aṣṭāv eva rasā nāṭye na śāntas tatra yujyate//"
ity āhuḥ/ tac cāpare na kṣamante/ tathā hi-- naṭe śamābhāvād iti hetur asaṃgataḥ/ naṭe rasābhivyakter asvīkārāt/ sāmājikānāṃ śamavattvena tatra rasodbodhe bādhakābhāvāt/ na ca naṭasya śamābhāvāt tadabhinayaprakāśakatvānupapattir iti vācyam/ tasya bhayakrodhāder apy abhāvena tadabhinayaprakāśakatāyā apy asaṃgatyāpatteḥ/ yadi ca naṭasya krodhāder abhāvena vāstavatatkāryāṇāṃ vadhabandhādīnām utpattyasaṃbhave 'pi kṛtrimatatkāryāṇāṃ śikṣābhyāsādita utpattau nāsti bādhakam iti nirīkṣyate, tadā prakṛte 'pi tulyam/
atha nāṭye gītavādyādīnāṃ virodhināṃ sattvāt sāmājikeṣv api viṣayavaimukhyātmanaḥ śāntasya katham udreka iti cet, nāṭye śāntarasam abhyupagacchadbhiḥ phalabalāt tadgītavādyādes tasmin virodhitāyā akalpanāt/ viṣayacintāsāmānyasya tatra virodhitvasvīkāre tadīyālambanasya saṃsārānītyatvasya taduddīpanasya purāṇaśravaṇasatsaṅgapuṇyavanatīrthāvalokanāder api viṣayatvena virodhitvāpatteḥ/ ata eva caramādhyāye saṃgītaratnākare--
"aṣṭāv eva rasā nāṭyeṣv iti kecid acūcudan/
tadacāru yataḥ kaṃcin na rasaṃ svadate naṭaḥ//"
body.translated_text:
(1) And thus they say: 'The permanent emotion (<s>sthāyibhāva</s>), made manifest (<s>vyakta</s>) by the <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants) etc., is called <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment).' 'Manifest' means made the object of manifestation (<s>vyakti</s>). And <s>vyakti</s> is consciousness (<s>cit</s>) whose veil has been broken. Just as a lamp covered by a pot etc., when that [covering] is removed, illuminates the objects present nearby and itself shines forth — so the consciousness of the Self (<s>ātmacaitanya</s>) [illuminates] the <s>rati</s> (love) etc. that are accompanied by <s>vibhāvas</s> etc. This is because it is accepted that the properties of the inner organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) are illuminated by the witness-consciousness (<s>sākṣin</s>). And the illumination of the <s>vibhāvas</s> etc. by the witness-consciousness, like dream-horses etc. or like stage-silver etc., is not contradictory. The arising and destruction of <s>rasa</s> are figuratively attributed through the arising and destruction of the savoring (<s>carvaṇā</s>) of the <s>vibhāvas</s> etc. that are the manifesting agents, or of the breaking of the veil — just as the permanence of a phoneme is [spoken of figuratively through] the operation of the tongue etc. that serves as the manifesting agent for the 'ga' sound etc. Since the breaking of the veil has as its limit the savoring of the <s>vibhāvas</s> etc., when that [savoring] has ceased, since the luminosity is [again] covered, the permanent emotion, though existing, does not shine forth.
Alternatively: by the glory of the savoring of <s>vibhāvas</s> etc., through the connoisseur's (<s>sahṛdaya</s>'s) own sympathetic heart-nature (<s>sahṛdayatā</s>) that has blossomed forth, there arises in the connoisseur a mental activity (<s>cittavṛtti</s>) having the form of the bliss of one's own essential nature qualified by the respective permanent emotion — as the mental activity of a yogin in <s>samādhi</s>. This amounts to becoming one with that [emotion] (<s>tanmayībhavana</s>). And this bliss is not of the same kind as other worldly pleasures, because it is not of the nature of a mental modification (<s>antaḥkaraṇavṛtti</s>). Thus, in accordance with the import of the texts of <s>Abhinavagupta</s>, <s>Mammaṭabhaṭṭa</s>, etc., it is established that the permanent emotion such as <s>rati</s> (love) etc., qualified by consciousness whose veil has been broken, is <s>rasa</s>.
In reality, however, in accordance with the import of the Vedic texts (<s>śrutis</s>) to be cited below, it is consciousness (<s>cit</s>) itself — with its veil broken, delimited by <s>rati</s> etc. — that is <s>rasa</s>. And in every way, taking the consciousness-portion of this qualified entity — whether as qualifier or qualified — its eternality and self-luminosity are established. But taking the <s>rati</s>-etc.-portion, its non-eternality and its being illuminated by another [are established]. And the savoring (<s>carvaṇā</s>) of this [rasa] is indeed the breaking of the veil pertaining to consciousness, as stated before, or alternatively, the mental modification having that form. And this [aesthetic experience] is distinct from the <s>samādhi</s> that consists of the relishing of the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, because it has as its support the bliss of consciousness accompanied by objects such as <s>vibhāvas</s> etc. And it is to be brought about by the operation of poetry alone.
