Now, if [one asks] 'What is the evidence for the manifestation of the bliss-portion in this [experience]?' — since the counter-question 'What is the evidence for the manifestation of that [bliss] in <s>samādhi</s> also?' is equally applicable — 'The bliss that is supreme, grasped by the intellect, beyond the senses' — if [one says] such Vedic words are the evidence there, then here too there is the <s>śruti</s>: 'He indeed is <s>rasa</s>; for having obtained <s>rasa</s>, one becomes blissful' — and also the direct perception of all connoisseurs — thus there are two means of valid knowledge.
The savoring of <s>rasa</s> described in the second view as having the nature of the mental modification of that form — since it is to be brought about by the operation of language, it is verbal (<s>śābdī</s>). And since it has as its support directly perceived bliss, it is of the nature of direct perception. Its reality is like cognition born of a sentence. Thus say the venerable <s>Abhinavagupta</s> and his followers.
(2) <s>Bhaṭṭanāyaka</s>, however, [says]: 'In the cognition of <s>rasa</s> as belonging to another, there is no savoring. But the apprehension as belonging to oneself is difficult to establish, since <s>Śakuntalā</s> etc. are not <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants) with respect to the audience members. Without a <s>vibhāva</s>, there can be no apprehension of <s>rasa</s> etc. that has no substrate (<s>ālambana</s>). Nor should it be said that the quality of being a beloved woman is a delimiting factor of the general <s>vibhāva</s>-nature here too — because the absence of knowledge in the form of the ascertained non-validity, the unmarried and unapproachable character [of the heroine], must necessarily be placed in the category of delimiting factors of <s>vibhāva</s>-nature. Otherwise, even one's own sister etc. would [be a <s>vibhāva</s>] through the quality of being a beloved woman, and the same undesirable consequence would follow. Similarly, the absence of knowledge in the form of the un-mournable nature, the cowardly nature, etc. [applies] in the case of <s>karuṇa rasa</s> (the pathetic sentiment) etc.
But the non-arising of such knowledge is difficult to explain without specifying some other factor that obstructs it. If [one says] the cognition of non-difference of oneself with <s>Duṣyanta</s> etc. is itself such [a factor] — no, because the cognition of difference between the hero's qualities of ruling the earth, heroism, etc. and one's own qualities of being contemporary, being a coward, etc. is clearly perceived, making the cognition of non-difference itself difficult to obtain. Moreover, what kind of cognition is this? If [one says] it is verbal (<s>śābdī</s>) since no other means of knowledge presents itself — no, because just like other cognitions of the story of the hero and heroine generated by other ordinary words, this too would [undesirably] become lacking in charm. Nor is it mental (<s>mānasī</s>), because this [aesthetic cognition] is observed to be different from the mental cognition of those very same objects brought to mind through [ordinary] thought. Nor is it memory (<s>smṛti</s>), because there is no prior experience of such [a thing]. Therefore, the objects communicated by <s>abhidhā</s> (denotation) are established by the operation of <s>bhāvakatva</s> (the power of realization), with the quality of being a beloved etc. that is favorable to <s>rasa</s> being brought to the forefront through the obstruction of the knowledge of the unapproachable nature etc. that is opposed to <s>rasa</s>. When thus the circumstances of <s>Duṣyanta</s>, <s>Śakuntalā</s>, etc. — place, time, age, condition, etc. — have been made universal (<s>sādhāraṇīkṛta</s>), through the crippled [condition of <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>] by the glory of the prior operation, by the glory of the third operation of <s>bhogakṛttva</s> (the power of enjoyment), through the direct realization characterized by the repose in the bliss of one's own consciousness-nature generated by the predominance of <s>sattva</s> [over] <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> which have been swallowed — the permanent emotion such as <s>rati</s> etc., having a universal nature, brought about by <s>bhāvanā</s> (realization), is objectified and becomes <s>rasa</s>. Therein, the <s>rati</s> etc. being enjoyed, or the enjoyment of <s>rati</s> etc. — both are <s>rasa</s>. And this enjoyment, due to being accompanied by objects, is said to be in the neighborhood of the relishing of <s>Brahman</s>. And thus the three aspects of poetry [are]: 'denotation (<s>abhidhā</s>), realization (<s>bhāvanā</s>), and the making of that into enjoyment (<s>bhogīkṛti</s>)' — thus they say. The distinctive feature of this view compared to the previous one is only the acceptance of the additional operation of <s>bhāvakatva</s>. But enjoyment (<s>bhoga</s>) is [the same as] manifestation (<s>vyakti</s>). And <s>bhogakṛttva</s> is not different from <s>vyañjanā</s> (suggestion). The rest of the path is the same.
(3) The newer [school], however, [says]: 'In poetry and drama, when the <s>vibhāvas</s> etc. have been presented by the poet and the actor, and the <s>rati</s> (love) of <s>Duṣyanta</s> etc. toward <s>Śakuntalā</s> etc. has been apprehended through the operation of <s>vyañjanā</s> (suggestion), then immediately afterwards — by the glory of a defect (<s>doṣa</s>) in the form of a special <s>bhāvanā</s> (realization), stirred up by the connoisseur's sympathetic nature — upon one's own self, covered by ignorance and concealed by the superimposed <s>Duṣyanta</s>-nature, like a piece of silver upon a fragment of mother-of-pearl, arising as indescribable (<s>anirvacanīya</s>), illuminated by the witness-consciousness, the <s>rati</s> etc. having <s>Śakuntalā</s> etc. as its object — that alone is <s>rasa</s>. And this is an effect of the special defect; and is destroyed by the destruction of that [defect]. Due to the non-apprehension of difference from the extraordinary delight (<s>lokottarāhlāda</s>) that follows it, it comes to be designated by the word 'happiness' (<s>sukha</s>). Due to the non-apprehension of — or due to the determination of identity with — the <s>rati</s> etc. that was previously present [in <s>Duṣyanta</s>], it is called 'suggested' (<s>vyaṅgya</s>) and 'worthy of description.' The concealing <s>Duṣyanta</s>-nature too is itself indescribable. And the concealing is the function of being the delimiting factor of the qualifiedness (<s>viśeṣyatā</s>) in the cognition qualified by <s>rati</s> etc. By this [analysis], [the objections are answered:] since the <s>rati</s> etc. belonging to <s>Duṣyanta</s> etc. cannot be savored [by another], it is not <s>rasa</s>. But [the <s>rati</s>] belonging to oneself — how can it be manifested by <s>Śakuntalā</s> etc. who are unrelated to it? And the cognition of non-difference with <s>Duṣyanta</s> etc. upon oneself is defeated by the cognition of sublation — thus [these objections] are set aside.
Furthermore, the universality (<s>sādhāraṇya</s>) of the <s>vibhāvas</s> etc. spoken of by the earlier [authorities] is also difficult to explain without postulating the special defect when <s>Śakuntalā</s> etc. are being presented by poetry through words like '<s>Śakuntalā</s>' etc. that generate cognition having the form of <s>Śakuntalā</s>-nature etc. Therefore, when the special defect must necessarily be postulated, through that very [defect], the cognition of non-difference with <s>Duṣyanta</s> etc. upon one's own self is also well-explained.
Now, even so, let <s>rati</s> (love) generate a special kind of pleasure in the connoisseur just as in <s>Duṣyanta</s>. But in <s>karuṇa rasa</s> (the pathetic sentiment) etc., how can the permanent emotion of grief (<s>śoka</s>) etc., which is well-known to generate suffering, be the cause of delight in the connoisseur? On the contrary, it would be fitting for it to generate suffering in the connoisseur just as in the hero. Nor should it be said that real grief generates suffering but not imagined [grief] — since [even] the snake-on-a-rope etc. would then fail to produce fear, trembling, etc. And even <s>rati</s> in the connoisseur, being imagined, could not produce pleasure. True. If, from poetry with <s>karuṇa</s> as predominant, just as from poetry with <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic) as predominant, delight alone is attested by the connoisseur's heart, then — since the cause must be postulated to conform to the effect — the extraordinary operation of poetry must be postulated to be not only productive of delight but also obstructive of suffering.
But if suffering too, like delight, is established by valid evidence, then the obstructive power need not be postulated, and both [delight and suffering] will arise from their respective causes. [Objection:] Then how can poets be motivated to compose, and connoisseurs to listen? Since turning away from what is a means to the undesirable would be proper. [Reply:] Because the desired [result] is greater and the undesired less, motivation is justified, as in the case of applying sandalwood paste etc. [which involves some discomfort]. But for those who hold that [aesthetic experience produces] delight alone, motivation is entirely unhindered. Even the shedding of tears etc. [occurs] from the natural accompaniment of the experience of that particular bliss, not from suffering. For this very reason, the shedding of tears etc. by devotees of the Lord upon hearing descriptions of the Lord is well-explained — for there is never any experience of suffering there.
Nor should it be said: 'In <s>karuṇa rasa</s> etc., if there is delight from the superimposition upon one's own self of identity with <s>Daśaratha</s> etc. who is filled with grief etc., then in dreams or in delirium also, where such superimposition upon oneself occurs, there should be [delight]; but what is experienced there is suffering alone; therefore here too [suffering] alone is fitting.' For this is the very glory of the extraordinary operation of poetry: that even objects such as grief etc. that are not delightful, when brought about by it, generate an unworldly delight. For the relishing born of the operation of poetry is of a distinctive, beautiful kind, different from experience born of other means of knowledge. And the 'generation' [by poetry] means having as its object the <s>rati</s> etc. that is generated by the <s>bhāvanā</s> generated by it [poetry]. Therefore, there is no harm even though the savoring of <s>rasa</s> is generated by the operation of poetry. But the arising of the knowledge of the unapproachable nature in <s>Śakuntalā</s> etc. is obstructed by the cognition of non-difference with <s>Duṣyanta</s> etc. upon one's own self.' — thus they say.
(4) Others, however, [say]: 'Even without accepting the operation of <s>vyañjanā</s> (suggestion) or the indescribable cognition (<s>anirvacanīyakhyāti</s>), through the glory of the aforementioned special defect, the mental cognition — which engages in the identity of oneself with <s>Duṣyanta</s> etc. and [apprehends] the <s>rati</s> etc. having <s>Śakuntalā</s> etc. as its object as non-different [from one's own] — [this cognition] possessing a distinctive kind of objectivity, is <s>rasa</s>. But a cognition in dreams etc. of such a kind is not born from the contemplation of poetic content, and so it is not <s>rasa</s>. Hence there is no unwanted consequence of such delight there.
Even so, how can there be an experience of <s>rati</s> etc. that does not exist in oneself? Not so — for this is not a worldly direct perception of <s>rati</s> etc., where the existence of the object would necessarily be required. Rather, it is an error (<s>bhrama</s>). But the convention of calling the savoring as having <s>rasa</s> as its object is based on its having <s>rati</s> etc. as its object.' — thus they also say.
And by these [scholars], the cognition — whether [understood as] engaging in the qualifiedness of the self as delimited by <s>Duṣyanta</s>-nature and the distinction of <s>rati</s> having <s>Śakuntalā</s> etc. as its object, or as engaging in the identity with <s>Duṣyanta</s> who is distinguished by <s>rati</s> having <s>Śakuntalā</s> etc. as its object upon the self distinguished by self-hood, or as engaging in the distinction of <s>Duṣyanta</s>-nature and <s>rati</s> having <s>Śakuntalā</s> as its object upon the self distinguished by self-hood — in all three ways, the cognition should be accepted as the entity denoted by the word '<s>rasa</s>.' Therein, 'since <s>rati</s> as qualifier is not cognized from the word, and since <s>vyañjanā</s> (suggestion) which would convey it is not accepted — inference through signs such as gestures etc. must first be accepted for the knowledge of the qualifier.'
(5) 'Primarily, <s>rasa</s>, which is <s>rati</s> etc., exists in <s>Duṣyanta</s> etc. themselves; it is directly experienced through being superimposed on the actor who skillfully presents the enactment of the charming <s>vibhāvas</s> etc. by imitating <s>Duṣyanta</s> etc.' — thus [say] some. In this view, the direct experience 'This is <s>Duṣyanta</s>, possessing <s>rati</s> toward <s>Śakuntalā</s> etc.' — is worldly with respect to the <s>dharmin</s>-portion (the substrate), as before, but is unworldly with respect to the superimposed portion.
(6) 'The <s>rati</s> etc. residing in <s>Duṣyanta</s> etc. — in the actor who is apprehended as <s>Duṣyanta</s>, through <s>vibhāvas</s> etc. that are artificial but apprehended as non-artificial — <s>rasa</s> is inferred through the strength of the totality of inferential evidence about a different object — that is, the inference of <s>rasa</s> in the actor who is the inferential subject' — thus [say] others.
(7) 'The three [factors] — <s>vibhāvas</s>, <s>anubhāvas</s>, and <s>vyabhicārin</s> [bhāvas] — taken together, are <s>rasa</s>' — thus [say] a few.
(8) 'Among the three, whatever produces aesthetic wonder (<s>camatkāra</s>), that alone is <s>rasa</s>; otherwise, [even] all three are not [<s>rasa</s>]' — thus [say] many.
(9) 'The <s>vibhāva</s> itself, when contemplated upon (<s>bhāvyamāna</s>), is <s>rasa</s>' — thus [say] others.
(10) 'Likewise, the <s>anubhāva</s> [when contemplated upon is rasa]' — thus [say] still others.
(11) 'Likewise, the <s>vyabhicārin</s> (transitory emotion) itself so transforms' — thus [say] some.
Therein, the sūtra 'From the combination of <s>vibhāva</s>, <s>anubhāva</s>, and <s>vyabhicārin</s>, the <s>rasa</s> arises (<s>niṣpatti</s>)' is interpreted in accordance with each respective view: In the first [view]: 'From the combination, i.e., the suggestion (<s>vyañjana</s>), of <s>vibhāvas</s>, <s>anubhāvas</s>, and <s>vyabhicārins</s>, the arising (<s>niṣpatti</s>) of <s>rasa</s> — whose nature is the permanent emotion qualified by consciousness and bliss, or whose nature is consciousness and bliss qualified by the permanent emotion — means the shining forth in its own form.' In the second: 'From the combination, i.e., the realization (<s>bhāvanā</s>) through the operation of <s>bhāvakatva</s>, of the <s>vibhāvas</s>, <s>anubhāvas</s>, and <s>vyabhicārins</s> properly made universal — the arising of <s>rasa</s>, whose form is the bliss of one's own Self illuminated by the predominance of <s>sattva</s> qualified by the permanent emotion, means being objectified through the direct realization called enjoyment (<s>bhoga</s>).' In the third: 'From the combination, i.e., the defect in the form of a special <s>bhāvanā</s>, of <s>vibhāvas</s>, <s>anubhāvas</s>, and <s>vyabhicārins</s>, the arising (<s>niṣpatti</s>) means the production of <s>rasa</s> whose nature is the indescribable <s>Duṣyanta</s>-<s>rati</s> etc.' In the fourth: 'From the combination, i.e., the knowledge of <s>vibhāvas</s> etc., the arising of <s>rasa</s> whose nature is a special knowledge, means production.' In the fifth: 'From the connection of <s>vibhāvas</s> etc., the arising of <s>rasa</s>, which is <s>rati</s> etc., means superimposition on the actor.' In the sixth: 'From the combination of <s>vibhāvas</s> etc. — artificial yet apprehended as non-artificial — the arising of <s>rasa</s>, which is <s>rati</s> etc., means inference; the subject being the actor.' In the seventh: 'From the combination, i.e., the aggregate, of the three — <s>vibhāvas</s> etc. — the arising of <s>rasa</s> means the conventional usage of the word <s>rasa</s>.' In the eighth: 'From the proper combination (<s>samyagyoga</s>), i.e., the aesthetic wonder (<s>camatkāra</s>), among the <s>vibhāvas</s> etc.' Thus, in the last three views, there is contradiction with the sūtra.
Since each one of the <s>vibhāvas</s>, <s>anubhāvas</s>, and <s>vyabhicārins</s>, being common to other <s>rasas</s>, cannot be the determinate suggestor of a specific <s>rasa</s> — therefore their combination is mentioned in the sūtra. And thus, when the combination is established as the suggestor by valid evidence, wherever the awakening of <s>rasa</s> occurs from even a single exclusive [element], the other two should be understood as implied. Hence there is no inconclusiveness.
Thus, even though understood in many different ways by intellects of various kinds, <s>rasa</s>, being perceived as invariably accompanied by supreme delight, undoubtedly brings beauty (<s>ramaṇīyatā</s>) to this world.
And it is —
'<s>Śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic), <s>Karuṇa</s> (the pathetic), <s>Śānta</s> (the peaceful), <s>Raudra</s> (the furious), <s>Vīra</s> (the heroic), <s>Adbhuta</s> (the wondrous), <s>Hāsya</s> (the comic), <s>Bhayānaka</s> (the terrible), and <s>Bībhatsa</s> (the disgusting) — these are the nine.' //
The words of the sage [<s>Bharata</s>] are the authority here.
Some, however, say: 'Since <s>Śānta</s> (the peaceful) is to be achieved through tranquility (<s>śama</s>), and since that is impossible in an actor, there are only eight <s>rasas</s> in drama; <s>Śānta</s> is not appropriate there.' // But others do not accept this. For: the reason 'due to the absence of tranquility in the actor' is incongruent, because the manifestation of <s>rasa</s> in the actor is not accepted [by us; it is in the audience]. Since, due to the audience members possessing tranquility, there is no obstacle to the awakening of that <s>rasa</s> there. Nor should it be said that due to the actor's lack of tranquility, he cannot convincingly portray its enactment — because, since the actor also lacks fear, anger, etc., the incongruence would extend to the portrayal of those [emotions] as well. And if it is observed that even though the actor's lack of anger means the impossibility of real effects of anger such as killing and binding, yet there is no obstacle to the production of artificial effects [of anger] acquired through training and practice — then the same applies in the present case.
Now, if [one objects that] in drama, since distracting elements like music and dance are present, how can <s>Śānta</s>, whose nature is aversion from sense objects, predominate even in audience members? — those who accept <s>Śānta rasa</s> in drama, by the force of the result, do not postulate that music and dance etc. are opposed to it. For if the general thinking about sense objects is accepted as opposed to it, then even the substrate of that [<s>rasa</s>] — the impermanence of <s>saṃsāra</s> — and its excitants (<s>uddīpana</s>) such as hearing <s>Purāṇas</s>, association with the virtuous, seeing holy forests and pilgrimage sites — would also, being sense objects, [undesirably] become opposed [to it]. For this very reason, in the final chapter of the <s>Saṃgītaratnākara</s> —
'Some have declared that there are only eight <s>rasas</s> in drama. That is ungraceful, because the actor does not savor any [particular] <s>rasa</s>.' //

body.text:
ityādinā nāṭye 'pi śānto raso 'stīti vyavasthāpitam/ yair api nāṭye śānto raso nāstīty abhyupagamyate tair api bādhakābhāvān mahābhāratādiprabandhānāṃ śāntarasapradhānatayā akhilalokānubhavasiddhatvāc ca kāvye so 'vaśyaṃ svīkāryaḥ/ atra eva "aṣṭau nāṭye rasāḥ smṛtāḥ" ity upakramya "śānto 'pi navamo rasaḥ" iti mammaṭabhaṭṭā apy upasamahārṣuḥ/
amīṣāṃ ca--
"ratiḥ śokaś ca nirvedakrodhotsāhaś ca vismaya/
hāso bhayaṃ jugupsā ca sthāyibhāvāḥ kramād amī//"
rasebhyaḥ sthāyibhāvānāṃ ghaṭāder ghaṭādyavacchinnākāśād iva prathamadvitīyayor matayoḥ, satyarajatasyānirvacanīyarajatād iva tṛtīye, viṣayasya (rajatādeḥ) jñānād iva caturthe bhedo bodhyaḥ/ tatra ā prabandhaṃ sthiratvād amīṣāṃ bhāvānāṃ
sthāyitvam/ na ca cittavṛttirūpāṇām eṣām āśuvināśitvena sthiratvaṃ durlabham, vāsanārūpatayā sthiratvaṃ tu vyabhicāriṣv atiprasaktam iti vācyam/ vāsanārūpāṇām amīṣāṃ muhurmuhur abhivyakter eva sthirapadārthatvāt/ vyabhicāriṇāṃ tu naiva, tadabhivyakter vidyududdyotaprāyatvāt/
yadāhuḥ--
"virūddhair aviruddhair vā bhāvair vicchidyate na yaḥ/
ātmabhāvaṃ nayatyāśu sa sthāyī lavaṇākaraḥ//
body.translated_text: By such [statements] and the like, it is established that the <s>Śānta</s> (tranquil) <s>rasa</s> exists even in drama. Even by those who hold that the <s>Śānta rasa</s> does not exist in drama, it must necessarily be accepted in poetry (<s>kāvya</s>), because there is no contradicting evidence, because compositions such as the <s>Mahābhārata</s> and the like are predominantly of the <s>Śānta rasa</s>, and because it is established through the experience of the entire world. Here indeed, <s>Mammaṭa Bhaṭṭa</s> too, having begun with 'Eight <s>rasas</s> are recognized in drama,' concluded with 'the <s>Śānta</s> is also a ninth <s>rasa</s>.' And for these [rasas]: '<s>Rati</s> (love), <s>śoka</s> (grief), <s>nirveda</s> (world-weariness), <s>krodha</s> (anger), <s>utsāha</s> (enthusiasm), <s>vismaya</s> (wonder), <s>hāsa</s> (laughter), <s>bhaya</s> (fear), and <s>jugupsā</s> (disgust) — these are the <s>sthāyibhāvas</s> (permanent emotions) in order.' The difference between the <s>sthāyibhāvas</s> and the <s>rasas</s> should be understood as [the difference] between a pot etc. and the space delimited by a pot etc., according to the first and second views; as [the difference] between real silver and indescribable silver [in the rope-silver illusion], according to the third [view]; and as [the difference] between the object (silver etc.) and the knowledge [of it], according to the fourth [view]. Therein, the permanence (<s>sthāyitva</s>) of these emotions [consists in their] stability throughout the composition. Nor should one object: 'Since these, being mental states (<s>citta-vṛtti</s>), are quickly perishable, stability is difficult [to maintain]; while stability in the form of latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) would over-extend to the transitory emotions (<s>vyabhicārins</s>) as well.' For these [permanent emotions], being in the form of latent impressions, are permanent entities precisely because they are repeatedly manifested. But the transitory emotions are not so, because their manifestation is like the flash of lightning. As they say: 'That which is not interrupted by either contrary or non-contrary emotions, and which quickly brings [all else] to its own nature — that permanent [emotion] is [like] a mine of salt.'

body.text:
ciraṃ citte 'vatiṣṭhante saṃbadhyante 'nubandhibhiḥ/
rasatvaṃ ye prapadyante prasiddhāḥ sthāyino 'tra te//"
ciram iti vyabhicārivāraṇāya/ anubandhibhir vibhāvādyaiḥ/
tathā--
"sajātīyavijātīyair
atiraskṛtamūrtimān/
yāvad rasaṃ vartamānaḥ sthāyibhāva udāhṛtaḥ//" iti/
kecit tu ratyādyanyatamatvaṃ sthāyitvam āhuḥ/ tan na/ ratyādīnām ekasmin prarūḍhe 'nyasyāprarūḍhasya vyabhicāritvopagamāt/ prarūḍhatvāprarūḍhatve bahvalpavibhāvajatve/
taduktaṃ ratnākare--
"ratyādayaḥ sthāyibhāvāḥ syur bhūyiṣṭhavibhāvajāḥ/
stokaṃ vibhāvair utpannās ta eva vyabhicāriṇaḥ// iti/
evaṃ ca vīrarase pradhāne krodho, raudre cotsāhaḥ, śṛṅgāre hāso vyabhicārī bhavati, nāntarīyakaś ca/ yadā tu pradhānaparipoṣārthaṃ so 'pi bahuvibhāvajaḥ kriyate tadā tu rasālaṃkāra ityādi bodhyam/
tatra--
body.translated_text: 'Those which remain in the mind for a long time, which are connected with accompanying [factors], and which attain the state of <s>rasa</s> — these are known here as the permanent [emotions] (<s>sthāyins</s>).' 'For a long time' is [said] to exclude the transitory emotions. 'With accompanying [factors]' means with the <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants) and the like. Likewise: 'By those of the same kind and those of a different kind...'

body.text: strīpuṃsayor anyonyālambanaḥ premākhyaś cittavṛttiviśeṣo ratiḥ sthāyibhāvaḥ//
body.translated_text: The particular mental state called love (<s>preman</s>), which takes the form of mutual dependence (<s>ālambana</s>) between a man and a woman, is <s>rati</s> — the <s>sthāyibhāva</s> (permanent emotion). //

body.text: gurudevatāputrādyālambanas tu vyabhicārī/
body.translated_text: But [love] that takes as its <s>ālambana</s> a teacher, deity, son, and the like is a <s>vyabhicārin</s> (transitory emotion).

body.text: putrādiviyogamaraṇādijanmāvaiklavyākhyaścittavṛttiviśeṣaḥ śokaḥ//
body.translated_text: The particular mental state of distress (<s>vaiklavya</s>) born from separation, death, and similar [events concerning] a son and the like is <s>śoka</s> (grief). //

body.text: strīpuṃsayos tu viyoge jīvitatvajñānadaśāyāṃ vaiklavyapoṣitāyā rater eva prādhānyāc chṛṅgāro vipralambhākhyo rasaḥ/ vaiklavyaṃ tu saṃcārimātram/ mṛtatvajñānadaśāyāṃ tu ratipoṣitasya vaiklavyasyeti karuṇa eva/ yadā tu saty api mṛtatvajñāne devatāprasādādinā punar ujjīvanajñānaṃ kathaṃcit syāt, tadālambanasyātyantikanirāsābhāvāc cirapravāsa iva vipralambha eva, na sa karuṇaḥ/ yathā candrāpīḍaṃ prati mahāśvetāvākyeṣu/ kecit tu rasāntaram evātra karuṇavipralambhākhyam icchanti/
body.translated_text: However, in the case of separation between a man and a woman, when [the beloved's] being alive is known, since <s>rati</s> itself — nourished by distress — predominates, the <s>rasa</s> is <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic) in its form called <s>Vipralambha</s> (love-in-separation). Distress is merely a <s>saṃcārin</s> (transitory emotion). But when death is known, since it is the distress — nourished by <s>rati</s> — [that predominates], it is the <s>Karuṇa</s> (pathetic) <s>rasa</s>.

body.text: nityānityavastuvicārajanmā viṣayavirāgākhyo nirvedaḥ//
body.translated_text: <s>Nirveda</s> (world-weariness) is the dispassion toward sense-objects born from the discernment between eternal and non-eternal things. //

body.text: gṛhakalahādijas tu vyabhicāri/
body.translated_text: But [dispassion] arising from domestic quarrels and the like is a <s>vyabhicārin</s> (transitory emotion).

body.text: gurubandhuvadhādiparamāparādhajanmā prajvalanākhyaḥ krodhaḥ//
body.translated_text: <s>Krodha</s> (anger) — called blazing (<s>prajvalana</s>) — is born from the most grievous offenses such as the killing of teachers and relatives. //

body.text: ayaṃ ca paravināśādihetuḥ/ kṣudrāparādhajanmā tu paruṣavacanāsaṃbhāṣaṇādihetuḥ/ ayam evāmarṣākhyo vyabhicārīti vivekaḥ/
body.translated_text: This [anger] is a cause of the destruction of the enemy and the like. But [anger] born from minor offenses — which is a cause of harsh speech, refusal to speak, and the like — this same [emotion], called <s>amarṣa</s> (indignation), is a <s>vyabhicārin</s>. This is the distinction.

body.text: paraparākramadānādismṛtijanmā aunnatyākhya utsāhaḥ//
body.translated_text: <s>Utsāha</s> (enthusiasm) — called elation (<s>aunnatya</s>) — is born from the recollection of the valor, generosity, and the like of another. //

body.text: alaukikavastudarśanādijanmā vikāsākhyo vismayaḥ//
body.translated_text: <s>Vismaya</s> (wonder) — called expansion (<s>vikāsa</s>) — is born from the sight of extraordinary objects and the like. //

body.text: vāgaṅgādivikāradarśanajanmā vikāsākhyo hāsaḥ//
body.translated_text: <s>Hāsa</s> (laughter) — called expansion (<s>vikāsa</s>) — is born from the sight of distortions of speech, body, and the like. //

body.text: vyāghradarśanādijanmā paramānarthaviṣayako vaiklavyākhyaḥ sa bhayam//
body.translated_text: <s>Bhaya</s> (fear) — a particular mental state called distress (<s>vaiklavya</s>), having as its object the greatest calamity, born from the sight of a tiger and the like — that is fear. //

body.text: paramānarthaviṣayakatvābhāve tu sa eva trāso vyabhicāri/ apare tu autpātikaprabhavas trāsaḥ, svāparādhadvārotthaṃ bhayam iti bhayatrāsayor bhedam āhuḥ/
body.translated_text: But in the absence of having the greatest calamity as its object, that very [emotion] is <s>trāsa</s> (alarm), a <s>vyabhicārin</s>. Others, however, state the distinction between <s>bhaya</s> and <s>trāsa</s> thus: <s>trāsa</s> has its origin in portents, while <s>bhaya</s> arises through the medium of one's own offense.

body.text: kadaryavastuvilokanajanmā vicikitsākhyaś cittavṛttiviśeṣo jugupsā//
body.translated_text: <s>Jugupsā</s> (disgust) — a particular mental state called aversion (<s>vicikitsā</s>), born from the sight of vile objects — is disgust. //

body.text: evam eṣāṃ sthāyibhāvānāṃ loke tattannāyakagatānāṃ yānyālambanatayoddīpanatayā vā kāraṇatvena prasiddhāni tāny eṣu kāvyanāṭyayor vyajyamāneṣu vibhāvaśabdena vyapadiśyante//
body.translated_text: Thus, when these <s>sthāyibhāvas</s> (permanent emotions), existing in the world as pertaining to their respective heroes (<s>nāyakas</s>), are suggested in poetry and drama — those things which are well-known as causes in the role of <s>ālambana</s> (foundational) or <s>uddīpana</s> (excitant) determinants are designated by the term <s>vibhāva</s>. //

body.text: vibhāvayantīti vyutpatteḥ/
body.translated_text: Because they cause to perceive (<s>vibhāvayanti</s>) — this is the etymology.

body.text: yāni ca kāryatayā tāny anubhāvaśabdena//
body.translated_text: And those which [are well-known] in the role of effects are [designated] by the term <s>anubhāva</s>. //

body.text: anu paścād bhāva utpattir yeṣām/ anubhāvayantīti vā vyutpatteḥ/
body.translated_text: [The etymology is:] those after (<s>anu</s>) which there is production (<s>bhāva</s>, i.e., <s>utpatti</s>). Or: because they cause to experience (<s>anubhāvayanti</s>).

body.text: yāni saha caranti tāni vyabhicāriśabdena//
body.translated_text: Those which accompany (<s>saha caranti</s>) [the permanent emotions] are [designated] by the term <s>vyabhicārin</s>. //

body.text:
tatra śṛṅgārasya strīpuṃsāvālambane/ candrikāvasantavividhopavanarahaḥsthānādaya uddīpanavibhāvāḥ/ tanmukhāvalokanatadguṇaśravaṇakīrtanādayo 'nye sāttvikabhāvāś cānubhāvāḥ/ smṛticintādayo vyabhicāriṇaḥ/
karuṇasya bandhunāśādaya ālambanāni/ tatsambandhigṛhaturagābharaṇadarśanādayas tatkathāśravaṇādayaś coddīpakāḥ/ gātrakṣepāśrupātādayo 'nubhāvā glānikṣayamohaviṣādacintautsukyadīnatājaḍatādayo vyabhicāriṇaḥ/
śāntasyānityatvena jñātaṃ jagadālambanam/ vedāntaśravaṇatapovanatāpasadarśanādyuddīpanam/ viṣayāruciśatrumittrādyaudāsīnyaceṣṭāhānināsāgradṛṣṭyādayo 'nubhāvāḥ/ harṣonmādasmṛtimatyādayo vyabhicāriṇaḥ/
raudrasyāgaskṛtpuruṣādir ālambanam/ tatkṛto 'parādhādir uddīpakaḥ/ vadhabandhādiphalako netrāruṇyadantapīḍanaparuṣabhāṣaṇaśastragrahaṇādir anubhāvaḥ/ amarṣavegaugryacāpalādayaḥ saṃcāriṇaḥ/
evaṃ yasyāś cittavṛtter yo viṣayaḥ sa tasyā ālambanam/ nimittāni coddīpakānīti bodhyam/
tatra śṛṅgāro dvividhaḥ/ saṃbhogo vipralambhaś ca/ rateḥ saṃyogakālāvacchinnatve prathamaḥ/ viyogakālāvacchinnatve dvitīyaḥ/ saṃyogaś ca na daṃpatyoḥ sāmānādhikaraṇyam/ ekatalpaśayane 'pīrṣyādisadbhāve vipralambhasyaiva varṇanāt/ evaṃ viyogo 'pi na vaiyadhikaraṇyam/ doṣasyoktatvāt/ tasmād dvāv imau saṃyogaviyogākhyāv antaḥkaraṇavṛttiviśeṣau/ yat saṃyukto viyuktaś cāsmīti dhīḥ/ tatrādyo yathā "śayitā savidhe 'pyanīśvarā" ity atra nirūpitaḥ/
yat tu citramīmāṃsāyām--
body.translated_text: Therein, for <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic <s>rasa</s>), the woman and man are the <s>ālambana</s> (foundational determinants). Moonlight, spring, various pleasure gardens, secluded places, and the like are the <s>uddīpana-vibhāvas</s> (excitant determinants). Gazing at the face [of the beloved], hearing and praising [the beloved's] virtues, and the like, as well as the <s>sāttvika bhāvas</s> (involuntary psychophysical reactions), are the <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequents). Memory, anxious thought, and the like are the <s>vyabhicārins</s> (transitory emotions).

body.text:
"vāgarthāviva saṃpṛktau" ityatra rasadhvaniḥ/
niratiśayapremaśālitāvyañjanāt" ititaddhvanimārgānākalananibandhanam/ pārvatīparameśvaraviṣayakakaviratau pradhāne niratiśayapremṇo guṇībhāvāt/ na hi guṇībhūtasya ratyāde rasadhvanivyapadeśahetutvaṃ yuktam/ "bhinno rasādyalaṃkārād alaṃkāryatayā sthitaḥ" iti siddhāntāt/
dvitīyo yathā--
"vāco māṅgalikīḥ prayāṇasamaye jalpaty analpaṃ jane
kelīmandiramārutāyanamukhe vinyastavaktrāmbujā/
niḥśvāsaglapitādharoparipatadbāṣpārdravakṣoruhā
bālā lolavilocanā śiva śiva prāṇeśam ālokate//"
atrāpy ālambanasya nāyakasya, niḥśvāsāśrupātāder anubhāvasya, viṣādacintāvegādeś ca vyabhicāriṇaḥ, saṃyogād ratir abhivyajyamānā viyogakālāvacchinnatvād vipralambharasavyapadeśahetuḥ/
yathā vā--
"āvirbhūtā yadavādhi madhusyandinī nandasūnoḥ
kāntiḥ kācin nikhilanayanākarṣaṇe kārmaṇajñā/
śvāso dīrghas tadavādhi mukhe pāṇḍimā gaṇḍayugme
śūnyā vṛttiḥ kulamṛgadṛśāṃ cetasi prādurāsīt//"
yathā vā--
"nayanāñcalāvamarśaṃ yā na kadācit purā sehe/
āliṅgitāpi joṣaṃ tasthau sā gantukena dayitena//"
body.translated_text: In [the verse] '<s>vāgarthāviva saṃpṛktau</s>' ('Like word and meaning conjoined'), there is <s>rasa-dhvani</s> (the suggestion of <s>rasa</s>). [The claim that] 'because [it] suggests the possession of unsurpassed love' [makes it <s>rasa-dhvani</s>] — this is grounded in a failure to discern the path of <s>dhvani</s>. For since the unsurpassed love — in the <s>rati</s> of the poet directed toward <s>Pārvatī</s> and <s>Parameśvara</s> — which is the principal [suggested meaning], becomes subordinate, it is not proper. For a subordinate [element]...

body.text:
ihāpi sahajacāñcalyanivṛttir jaḍatā cānubhāvavyabhicāriṇau/ imaṃ ca pañcavidhaṃ prāñcaḥ pravāsādibhir upādhibhir āmananti/ te ca pravāsābhilāṣaviraherṣyāśāpānāṃ viśeṣānupalambhān nāsmābhiḥ prapañcitāḥ/
karuṇo yathā--
"apahāya sakalabāndhavacintām udvāsya gurukulapraṇayam/
hā tanaya vinayaśālin katham iva paralokapathiko 'bhūḥ//"
atra pramītatanaya ālambanam/ tatkālāvacchinnabāndhavadarśanādy uddīpanam/ rodanam anubhāvaḥ/ dainyādayaḥ saṃcāriṇaḥ/
śānto yathā--
"malayānilakālakūṭayo ramaṇīkuntalabhogibhogayoḥ/
śvapanātmabhuvor nirantarā mama jātā paramātmani sthitiḥ//"
atra prapañcaḥ sarvo 'py ālambanam/ sarvatra sāmyam anubhāvaḥ/ matyādayaḥ saṃcāriṇaḥ/ yady api prathamārdhe uttamādhamayor upakramā dvitīyārdhe 'dhamottamavacanaṃ kramabhaṅgam āvahati, tathāpi vaktur brahmātmakatayottamādhamajñānavaikalyaṃ saṃpannam iti dyotanāya kramabhaṅgo guṇa eva/
idaṃ punar nodāhāryam--
"surasrotasvinyāḥ pulinam adhitiṣṭhan nayanayor
vidhāyāntarmudrām atha sapadi vidrāvya viṣayān/
vidhūtāntardhvānto madhuramadhurāyāṃ citi kadā
nimagnaḥ syāṃ kasyāṃcana navanabhasyāmbudaruci//"
atrāpi yady api viṣayagaṇālambanaḥ surasrotasvinītaṭādyuddīpito nayananimīlanādibhir anubhāvitaḥ sthāyi nirvedaḥ pratīyate, tathāpi
bhagavadvāsudevālambanāyāṃ kaviratau guṇībhūta iti na śāntarasadhvanivyapadeśahetuḥ/ idaṃ ca padyaṃ mannirmitāyāṃ bhagavadbhaktipradhānāyāṃ karuṇālaharyām upanibaddham iti tatpradhānabhāvaprādhānyam evārhati/ śāntarasānanuguṇaś cāyam ojasvī gumpha iti cānudāhāryam evaitat/ pūrvapadye tu "paramātmani sthitiḥ" ity anena tattādrūpyāvagamād rater apratipattiḥ/
raudro yathā--
"navocchalitayauvanaspharadakharvagarvajvare
madīyagurukārmukaṃ galitasādhvasaṃ vṛścati/
ayaṃ patatu nirdayaṃ dalitadṛptabhūbhṛdgala-
skhaladrudhiraghasmaro mama paraśvadho bhairavaḥ//"
atra tadānīṃ rāmatvenājñāto gurukārmukabhañjaka ālambanam/ ata eva viśeṣyānupādānam/ gurudruho nāmagrahaṇānaucityāt, krodhāviṣkārād vā/ dhvaniviśeṣānumito niḥśaṅkadhanurbhaṅga uddīpakaḥ/ paruṣoktir anubhāvaḥ/ garvogratvādayaḥ saṃcāriṇaḥ/ eṣā ca dhanurbhaṅgadhvanibhagnasamādher bhārgavasyoktiḥ/
vṛttir apy atra mahoddhatā raudrasya paramaujasvitāṃ paripuṣṇāti/ anyatra gurusmaraṇe saty ahaṃbhāvavigamasyāvaśyakatayā prakṛte cājahatsvārthalakṣaṇāmūladhvananena madīyety anena garvotkarṣasyaiva prakāśanāt sphuṭaṃ gamyamānena vivekaśunyatvena krodhasyādhikyaṃ gamyate/
idaṃ tu nodāhāryam--
"dhanurvidalanadhvaniśravaṇatatkṣaṇāvirbhavan
mahāguruvadhasmṛtiḥ śvasanavegadhūtādharaḥ/
vilocanaviniḥsaradbahalavisphuliṅgavrajo
raghupravaram ākṣipañ jayati jāmadagnyo muniḥ//"

atrāpy aparādhāspadena raghunandanenālambito dhanurvidalanadhvaniśravaṇenoddīpito niḥśvāsanetrajvalanādibhir anubhāvito mahāguruvadhasmṛtigarvogratvādibhiś ca saṃcāritaḥ krodho yady api vyajyate, tathāpy asau tatprabhāvavarṇanabījabhūtāyāṃ kaviratau guṇībhūta iti na raudrarasadhvanivyapadeśahetuḥ/ kāvyaprakāśagataraudrarasodāharaṇe tu "kṛtam anumataṃ dṛṣṭaṃ vā yair idaṃ gurupātakam" iti padye raudrarasavyajanakṣamā nāsti vṛttiḥ, atas tatkaver aśaktir eva/
vīraś caturdhā/ dānadayāyuddhadharmāis tadupādher utsāhasya caturvidhatvāt/
tatrādyo yathā--
"kiyad idam adhikaṃ me yaddvijāyārthayitre
kavacam aramaramaṇīyaṃ kuṇḍale cārpayāmi/
akaruṇam avakṛttya drākkṛpāṇena niryad-
bahalarudhiradhāraṃ maulim āvedayāmi//"
eṣā dvijaveṣāyendrāya kavacakuṇḍaladānodyatasya karṇasya taddānavismitān sabhyān pratyuktiḥ/ atra yācamāna ālambanam/ tadudīritā stutir uddīpikā/ kavacādivitaraṇaṃ tatra laghutvabuddhyādikaṃ cānubhāvaḥ/ me ity arthāntarasaṃkramitavācyadhvanyutthāpito garvaḥ svakīyalokottarapitṛjanyatvādismṛtiś ca saṃcāriṇau/ vṛttir apy atra tattadarthānurūpodgamavirāmaśālitayā sahṛdayaikacamatkāriṇī/ tathā hi--utsāhapoṣakaṃ kavacakuṇḍalārpaṇayor laghutvanirūpaṇaṃ vidhātuṃ pūrvārdhe tadanukūlaśithilabandhātmikā/ uttarārdhe tu maulitaḥ prāgvaktṛgatagarvotsāhaparipoṣaṇāyoddhatā/ tataḥ paraṃ brāhmaṇe savinayatvaṃ prakāśayituṃ tanmūlībhūtaṃ garvarāhityaṃ dhvanayituṃ punaḥ śithilaiva/ ata evāvedayāmīty uktam/ na tu dadāmi vitarāmīti vā/
idaṃ tu nodāharaṇīyam--

yasyoddāmadivāniśārthivilasaddānapravāhaprathām
ākarṇyāvanimaṇḍalāgataviyadbandīndravṛndānanāt/
īrṣyānirbharaphullaromanikaravyāvalgadūdhaḥsravat-
pīyūṣaprakaraiḥ surendrasurabhiḥ prāvṛṭpayodāyate//

atrendrasabhāmadhyagatasakalanirīkṣakālambanaḥ avanimaṇḍalāgataviṣayavandīndravadanavinirgatarājadānavarṇanoddīpitaḥ, ūdhaḥprasnutapīyūṣaprakarair anubhāvitaḥ, asūyādibhiḥ saṃcāribhiḥ paripoṣito 'pi kāmagavīgata utsāho rājastutiguṇībhūta iti na rasavyapadeśahetuḥ/
ata evedam api nodāharaṇam--
"sābdhidvīpakulācalāṃ vasumatīm ākramya saptāntarāṃ
sarvāṃ dyām api susmitena hariṇā mandaṃ samālokitaḥ/
prādurbhūtaparapramodavidaladromāñcitas tatkṣaṇaṃ
vyānamrīkṛtakaṃdharo 'suravaro mauliṃ puro nyastavān//"
iha ca bhagavadvāmanālambanaḥ tatkartṛkamandanirīkṣaṇoddīpitaḥ, romāñcādibhir anubhāvitaḥ, harṣādibhiḥ poṣitaḥ, utsāho vyajyamāno 'pi guṇaḥ/ prāg anyagatasyeva prakṛte rājagatasyāpi tasya rājastutyutkarṣakatvāt/ etena
"tyāgaḥ saptasamudramudritamahīnirvyājadānāvadhiḥ" iti śrīvatsalāñchanoktam udāharaṇaṃ parāstam/ tasya guṇībhūtavyaṅgyatvena rasadhvaniprasaṅge 'nudāharaṇīyatvāt/ nanu "akaruṇam avakṛtya-" ity atrāpi pratīyamānasya dānavīrasya karṇastutyaṅgatvāt kathaṃ dhvanitvam iti cet, satyam/ atra kaveḥ karṇavacanānuvādamātratātparyakatvena
karṇastutau tātparyavirahāt/ karṇasya ca mahāśayatvenātmastutau tātparyānupapatteḥ stutir avākyārtha eva/ paraṃ tu vīrarasapratyayānantaraṃ tādṛśotsāhena liṅgena svādhikaraṇe sānumīyate/ rājavarṇanapadye tu rājastutau tātparyād vākyārthataiva tasyāḥ/
dvitīyo yathā--
"na kapota bhavantam aṇv api spṛśatu śyena samudbhavaṃ bhayam/
idam adya mayā tṛṇīkṛtaṃ bhavadāyuḥkuśalaṃ kalevaram//"
athavaivaṃ vinyāsaḥ--
"na kapotakapotakaṃ tava spṛśatu śyena manāg api spṛhā/
idam adya mayā samarpitaṃ bhavate cārutaraṃ kalevaram//"
eṣā śiveḥ kapotaṃ śyenaṃ prati coktiḥ/ atra kapota ālambanam/ tadgataṃ vyākulībhavanam uddīpanam/ tasya kṛte svakalevarārpaṇam anubhāvaḥ/ na cātra śarīradānapratyayād dānavīradhvanitvāpattir iti vācyam/ śyenakapotayor bhakṣyabhakṣakabhāvāpannatvena śibiśarīrasyārthino 'bhāvāt tadapratipatteḥ/ śyena śarīranivedanasya kapotaśarīratrāṇopādhikatayā vinimayapadavācyatvāt/
tṛtīyo yathā--
"raṇe dīnān devān daśavadana vidrāvya vahati
prabhāvaprāgalbhyaṃ tvayi tu mama ko 'yaṃ parikaraḥ/
lalāṭodyajjvālākavalitajagajjālavibhavo
bhavo me kodaṇḍacyutaviśikhavegaṃ kalayatu//"
eṣā daśavadanaṃ prati bhagavato rāmasyoktiḥ/ iha bhava ālambanam/ raṇadarśanam uddīpanam/ daśavadanāvajñānubhāvaḥ/ garvaḥ saṃcārī/ vṛttir atra devānāṃ prastāve tadgatakātaryaprakāśanadvārā vīrarasānālambanatvāvagataye 'nuddhataiva/
daśavadanaprastāve tu devadarpadamanavīratvapratipādanāyoddhatāpi
tasyāvajñayā rāmagatotsāhānālambanatvena tadālambanasya rasasyāpratyayān na prakarṣavatī/ bhagavato bhavasya tu paramottamālambanavibhāvatvāt tatprastāve tadālambanasyaujasvino vīrarasasya niṣpatteḥ prakṛṣṭoddhatā/
caturtho yathā--
"sapadi vilayam etu rājyalakṣmīr upari patantv athavā kṛpāṇadhārāḥ/
apaharatutarāṃ śiraḥ kṛtānto mama tu matir na manāg apaiti dharmāt//"
eṣādharmeṇāpi ripur jetavya iti vadantaṃ prati yudhiṣṭhirasyoktiḥ/ atra dharmaviṣaya ālambanam/ "na jātu kāmān na bhayān na lobhād dharmaṃ tyajej jīvītasyāpi hetoḥ" ity ādivākyālocanam uddīpanam/ śiraśchedādyaṅgīkāro 'nubhāvaḥ/ dhṛtiḥ saṃcāriṇī/ itthaṃ vīrarasasya cāturvidhyaṃ prapañcitaṃ prācām anurodhāt/
vastutas tu bahavo vīrarasasya śṛṅgārasyeva prakārā nirūpayituṃ śakyante/ tathā hi--prācīna eva "sapadi vilayam etu" ityādi padye "mama tu matir na manāg apaiti satyāt" iti caramapādavyatyāsena padyāntaratāṃ prāpite satyavīrasyāpi saṃbhavāt/ na ca satyasyāpi dharmāntargatatayā dharmavīrarasa eva tadvīrasyāpy antarbhāva iti vācyam/ dānadayayor api tadantargatatayā tadvīrayor api dharmavīrāt pṛthaggaṇanānaucityāt/
evaṃ pāṇḍityavīro 'pi pratīyate/
yathā--
"api vakti girāṃ patiḥ svayaṃ yadi tāsām adhidevatāpi vā/
ayam asmi puro hayānanasmaraṇollaṅghitavāṅmayāmbudhiḥ//"
atra bṛhaspatyādyālambanaḥ sabhādidarśanoddīpito nikhilavidvattiraskārānubhāvito garveṇa saṃcāriṇā poṣita utsāho vaktuḥ pratīyate/ nanu cātra yuddhavīratvam/ yuddhatvasya vādasādhāraṇasya vācyatvād iti cet/ kṣamāvīre kiṃ brūyāḥ/
yathā--
api bahaladahanajālaṃ mūrdhni ripur me nirantaraṃ dhamatu/
pātayatu vāsidhārām aham aṇumātraṃ na kiṃcid ābhāṣe//"
kṣamāvata uktir iyam/
balavīre vā kiṃ samādadhyāḥ/
yathā--
"pariharatu dharāṃ phaṇipravīraḥ sukhamayatāṃ kamaṭho 'pi tāṃ vihāya/"
aham iha puruhūta pakṣakoṇe nikhilam idaṃ jagad aklamaṃ vahāmi//
body.translated_text:
Here, the <s>utsāha</s> (enthusiasm) whose <s>ālambana</s> (foundational stimulus) is all the spectators seated in <s>Indra's</s> assembly hall, whose <s>uddīpana</s> (excitant) is the description of the king's generosity issuing from the mouths of the panegyrists who have come from the surface of the earth, whose <s>anubhāva</s> (consequent) is manifested through streams of nectar flowing from the udder [of the wish-fulfilling cow], and which is nourished by <s>saṃcārī</s> (transitory) emotions such as envy — even though it is present in the <s>Kāmadhenu</s> (wish-fulfilling cow), it is subordinated to the praise of the king, and thus is not the basis for the designation of <s>rasa</s>.
For this very reason, this too is not a valid illustration—
"Having conquered the earth with its oceans, islands, and mountain ranges, extending to seven [continents],
and all of heaven too, when gently gazed upon with a smile by <s>Hari</s>,
at that very instant the chief of the <s>Asuras</s>, his body bristling with horripilation born of supreme delight,
bent his neck and placed his crown before [the Lord]."
Here too, the <s>ālambana</s> is Lord <s>Vāmana</s>, the <s>uddīpana</s> is His gentle gaze, the <s>anubhāva</s> is manifested through horripilation and the like, and though nourished by joy and other [emotions], the <s>utsāha</s> being suggested is [merely] a <s>guṇa</s> (subordinate element). Just as previously [the enthusiasm] belonging to another [was subordinate], so too in the present case, even though belonging to the king, it enhances the praise of the king. By this, the illustration cited by <s>Śrīvatsalāñchana</s> — 'generosity whose limit is the unstinting gift of the earth sealed by seven oceans' — is also set aside, since being <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> (suggested meaning subordinated to something else), it should not be cited as an illustration in the context of <s>rasadhvani</s>. If one objects: 'In the verse beginning "akaruṇam avakṛtya" as well, the suggested <s>dānavīra</s> (heroism of generosity) is subordinate to the praise of <s>Karṇa</s>, so how can it be <s>dhvani</s>?' — true. Here, because the poet's intention is merely to report <s>Karṇa's</s> own words, there is no authorial intent toward praising <s>Karṇa</s>. And because <s>Karṇa</s>, being noble-minded, could not plausibly intend self-praise, the praise is only an implied meaning, not the sentence meaning. Rather, after the cognition of <s>vīrarasa</s> (heroic sentiment), the [praise] in its own locus is inferred through such <s>utsāha</s> as an inferential mark. But in the verse describing the king, since there is authorial intent toward praising the king, the praise has the status of sentence meaning alone.
The second [type of <s>vīrarasa</s>] is illustrated as follows—
"O pigeon, may not even the slightest fear born of the hawk touch you;
this body, [which ensures] the welfare of your life, has today been rendered [as worthless as] a blade of grass by me."
Or alternatively arranged thus—
"O pigeon, may the hawk's desire not touch your little pigeon even slightly;
this most beautiful body has today been offered to you by me."
This is the speech of <s>Śibi</s> addressed to the pigeon and the hawk. Here the pigeon is the <s>ālambana</s>; its distress is the <s>uddīpana</s>; the offering of one's own body for its sake is the <s>anubhāva</s>. And one should not say that because of the cognition of bodily giving, there is the fallacy of <s>dānavīradhvani</s> (heroism of generosity), because since the pigeon and hawk have entered the relation of prey and predator, there is no supplicant for <s>Śibi's</s> body, and hence no cognition of [generosity]; since <s>Śibi's</s> offering of his body, being conditional upon protecting the pigeon's body, is expressible by the word 'exchange.'
The third [type] is illustrated as follows—
"O ten-faced one, in battle, having routed the wretched gods, [you] bear the might of [your] prowess — but against you, what use is this retinue of mine?
Let <s>Bhava</s> (Śiva), whose splendor has consumed the world's net with flames rising from his forehead, reckon with the force of the arrow released from my bow!"
This is the speech of Lord <s>Rāma</s> addressed to <s>Rāvaṇa</s> (the ten-faced one). Here <s>Bhava</s> (Śiva) is the <s>ālambana</s>; witnessing the battle is the <s>uddīpana</s>; contempt for <s>Rāvaṇa</s> is the <s>anubhāva</s>; pride is the <s>saṃcārī</s>. The style (<s>vṛtti</s>) here, in the context of the gods, by revealing the cowardice inherent in them, serves to make clear that they are not the <s>ālambana</s> of <s>vīrarasa</s> — it is indeed restrained.
But in the context of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, though the style is elevated for establishing heroism in subduing the pride of the gods, because [<s>Rāma's</s>] contempt for him means that <s>Rāma's</s> <s>utsāha</s> does not have him as its <s>ālambana</s>, there is no cognition of the <s>rasa</s> having him as its foundation, so the elevated style is not prominent. But since Lord <s>Bhava</s> (Śiva) is the supremely excellent <s>ālambana-vibhāva</s>, in his context, the powerful <s>vīrarasa</s> having him as its <s>ālambana</s> arises — hence the style is eminently elevated.
The fourth [type] is illustrated as follows—
"Let royal fortune perish instantly, or let sword blades fall upon me from above;
let <s>Kṛtānta</s> (Death) take away my head — but my mind shall not deviate even slightly from <s>dharma</s>!"
This is the speech of <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> addressed to one who says that an enemy should be conquered even by unrighteous means. Here <s>dharma</s> is the <s>ālambana</s>; reflecting on statements such as 'One should never abandon <s>dharma</s> for desire, fear, greed, or even for life itself' is the <s>uddīpana</s>; accepting even the severing of one's head is the <s>anubhāva</s>; <s>dhṛti</s> (fortitude) is the <s>saṃcārī</s>. Thus the fourfold nature of <s>vīrarasa</s> has been elaborated, in accordance with the earlier authorities.
But in reality, many varieties of <s>vīrarasa</s> can be identified, just as with <s>śṛṅgārarasa</s>. For instance: in the very same verse beginning 'sapadi vilayam etu,' if the last quarter is altered to 'mama tu matir na manāg apaiti satyāt' ('my mind shall not deviate even slightly from truth'), it becomes a different verse, and the possibility of <s>satyavīra</s> (heroism of truthfulness) also arises. And one should not say that since truth is also included within <s>dharma</s>, the heroism of truth is subsumed under <s>dharmavīra</s> — for since generosity (<s>dāna</s>) and compassion (<s>dayā</s>) are also included within <s>dharma</s>, it would be inappropriate to count their respective types of heroism separately from <s>dharmavīra</s>.
Thus <s>pāṇḍityavīra</s> (heroism of learning) is also perceived. For example—
"Even if the Lord of Speech himself speaks, or even the presiding deity of words —
here I stand, having leapt across the ocean of literature through the mere remembrance of <s>Hayānana</s> (Hayagrīva)!"
Here, <s>Bṛhaspati</s> and others are the <s>ālambana</s>; witnessing the assembly and such is the <s>uddīpana</s>; contempt for all scholars is the <s>anubhāva</s>; pride is the <s>saṃcārī</s> that nourishes the <s>utsāha</s> perceived in the speaker. If one objects: 'But this is <s>yuddhavīra</s> (battle heroism), since battle, being common to debate as well, is the expressed meaning' — then what would you say about <s>kṣamāvīra</s> (heroism of forbearance)?
For example—
"Even if my enemy continually blows dense masses of fire upon my head, or brings down sword blades — I shall not utter even a single word!"
This is the utterance of a forbearing person.
Or what would you determine about <s>balavīra</s> (heroism of strength)?
For example—
"Let the serpent-chief abandon the earth; let the tortoise too give it up and be at ease —
O <s>Puruhūta</s> (Indra), I effortlessly bear this entire world on the tip of my wing!"

body.text:
puruhūtaṃ pratyeṣā garutmata uktiḥ/ nanu "api vakti-"pariharatu dharām-" iti padyadvaye garva eva notsāhaḥ/ madhyasthapadye tu dhṛtir eva dhvanyate iti bhāvadhvanaya evaite na rasadhvanaya iti cet tarhi yuddhavīrādiṣv api garvādidhvanitām eva kiṃ na brūyāḥ/ rasadhvanisāmānyam eva vā kiṃ na tadvyabhicāradhvananena gatārthayeḥ/ sthāyipratītir durapahnavā cet tulyaṃ prakṛte 'pi/ anantaroktapadye tu notsāhaḥ pratīyate/ dayāvīrādiṣu pratīyata iti tu rājājñāmātram/
adbhuto yathā--
"carācarajagajjālasadanaṃ vadanaṃ tava/
galadgaganagāmbhīryaṃ vīkṣyāsmi hṛtacetanā//"
kadācid bhagavato vāsudevasya vadanam ālokitavatyā yaśodāyā iyam uktiḥ/ atra vadanam ālambanam/ antargatacarācarajagajjāladarśanam uddīpanam/ hṛtacetanatvam, tena gamyaṃ romāñcanetrasphāraṇādi cānubhāvaḥ/ trāsādayo vyabhicāriṇaḥ/ naivātra vidyamānāpi putragatā prītiḥ pratīyate/ vyañjakābhāvāt/
pratītāyāṃ vā tasyāṃ vismayasya guṇatvaṃ na yujyate/ evaṃ kaścin mahāpuruṣo 'yam iti bhaktir api tasyāḥ mamāyaṃ bāla iti niścayena pratibandhād utpattam eva neṣṭe/ atas tasyām api vismayasya guṇībhāvo na śaṅkyaḥ/
yat tu sahṛdayaśiromaṇibhiḥ prācīnair
udāhṛtam--
"citraṃ mahān eṣa navāvatāraḥ, kva kāntir eṣābhinavaiva bhaṅgiḥ/
lokottaraṃ dhairyam aho prabhāvaḥ kāpy ākṛtir nūtana eṣa sargaḥ// iti,
tatredaṃ vaktavyam-- pratīyatāṃ nāmātra vismayaḥ paraṃ tv asau kathaṃkāraṃ adbhutarasa] dhvanivyapadeśahetuḥ/ pratipādyamahāpuruṣaviśeṣaviṣayāyāḥ pradhānībhūtāyāḥ stotṛgatabhaktaḥ prakarṣakatvenāsya guṇībhūtatvāt/ yathā mahābhārate gītāsu viśvarūpaṃ dṛṣṭavataḥ pārthasya "paśyāmi devāṃs tava deva dehe sarvāṃs tathā bhūtaviśeṣasaṃghān" ity ādau vākyasaṃdarbhe/ itthaṃ cāsya rasālaṃkāratvam ucitam/ bhaktir naivātra pratīyata iti ced daramukulitalocanaṃ vidāṃkurvantu sahṛdayāḥ/
hāsyo yathā--
"śrītātapādair vihite nibandhe nirūpitā nūtanayuktir eṣā/
aṅgaṃ gavāṃ pūrvam aho pavitraṃ na vā kathaṃ rāsabhadharmapatnyāḥ//"
tārkikaputro 'trālambanam/ tadīyā niḥśaṅkoktir uddīpikā/ radanaprakāśādir udvegādayaś cānubhāvavyabhicāriṇaḥ/
atrāhuḥ-
"ātmasthaḥ parasaṃsthaścety asya bhedadvayaṃ matam/
ātmastho draṣṭur utpanno vibhāvekṣaṇamātrataḥ//
body.translated_text:
This is the speech of <s>Garutmat</s> (<s>Garuḍa</s>) to <s>Puruhūta</s> (<s>Indra</s>). Now, if [one objects:] 'In the two verses beginning with "api vakti-" and "pariharatu dharām-," it is indeed pride (<s>garva</s>), not enthusiasm (<s>utsāha</s>); and in the neutral verse, it is fortitude (<s>dhṛti</s>) alone that is suggested — thus these are instances of <s>bhāva-dhvani</s> (suggestion of transitory emotion), not <s>rasa-dhvani</s> (suggestion of aesthetic sentiment)' — then why would you not equally say that even in martial heroism (<s>yuddha-vīra</s>) etc., it is pride etc. alone that is suggested? Or why not render the general [category of] <s>rasa-dhvani</s> superfluous through the suggestion of those transitory emotions? If the cognition of the permanent emotion (<s>sthāyin</s>) is undeniable, the same applies in the present case too. But in the verse stated immediately [after], enthusiasm is not what is perceived. That it is perceived in compassionate heroism (<s>dayā-vīra</s>) etc. is merely an arbitrary assertion.
<s>Adbhuta</s> (the wondrous sentiment), for example:
'Your face, which is the abode of the network of the movable and immovable world, having a depth from which the sky pours forth — seeing [it], I have become bereft of consciousness.'
This is the speech of <s>Yaśodā</s>, who once beheld the face of the Lord <s>Vāsudeva</s>. Here the face is the <s>ālambana</s> (foundational determinant). The vision of the network of the movable and immovable world within is the <s>uddīpana</s> (excitant). The loss of consciousness, and thereby inferred horripilation, widening of eyes, etc., are the <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequents). Fear (<s>trāsa</s>) etc. are the <s>vyabhicārins</s> (transitory emotions). Here, even though maternal love (<s>prīti</s>) directed toward the son exists, it is not perceived — due to the absence of suggestive elements (<s>vyañjaka</s>).
Or, even if it [maternal love] were perceived, the subordinate status (<s>guṇatva</s>) of wonder (<s>vismaya</s>) would not be appropriate. Similarly, devotion (<s>bhakti</s>) [arising from the thought] 'this is some great being (<s>mahāpuruṣa</s>)' — even that, due to being prevented from arising by her firm conviction 'this is my child,' is not desired [as arising here]. Therefore, the subordination (<s>guṇībhāva</s>) of wonder to that [devotion] too should not be suspected.
Now, as for what the earlier connoisseurs (<s>sahṛdaya-śiromaṇi</s>), the ancients, have cited as an example:
'How wondrous! This is a great new incarnation (<s>avatāra</s>); what splendor, what utterly novel grace! Transcendent is [his] composure — oh, the power! Some indescribable form — this is a new creation!'
To this the following must be said: let wonder indeed be perceived here; however, how can that be the ground for designating it as <s>dhvani</s> of <s>adbhuta-rasa</s>? Because, with respect to the predominant devotion (<s>bhakti</s>) of the praiser directed toward the special <s>mahāpuruṣa</s> (great being) that is being described, this [wonder] is subordinate (<s>guṇībhūta</s>) due to being an intensifying factor. Just as in the <s>Mahābhārata</s>, in the <s>Gītā</s>, in the series of utterances of <s>Pārtha</s> (<s>Arjuna</s>), who had seen the universal form (<s>viśvarūpa</s>), beginning with 'I see all the gods, O Lord, in your body, and also the hosts of various beings.' Thus, for this [verse], the status of <s>rasālaṃkāra</s> (ornament of aesthetic sentiment, i.e., subordinated rasa) is appropriate. If [one says] 'devotion is not perceived here at all' — then let the connoisseurs open their slightly closed eyes a little wider!
<s>Hāsya</s> (the comic sentiment), for example:
'In the treatise composed by the venerable <s>Tātapāda</s>, this novel argument has been established — the forepart of a cow is sacred, oh! But how [could the forepart] of the she-donkey, the lawful wife of an ass, [not be sacred]?'
The son of a logician (<s>tārkika</s>) is the <s>ālambana</s> (foundational determinant) here. His fearless utterance is the <s>uddīpikā</s> (excitant). The flashing of teeth etc. are the <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequents), and agitation (<s>udvega</s>) etc. are the <s>vyabhicārins</s> (transitory emotions).
Here they say: 'This [<s>hāsya</s>] is considered to have two divisions: <s>ātmastha</s> (self-based) and <s>parasaṃstha</s> (other-based). <s>Ātmastha</s> is that which arises in the spectator merely from seeing the <s>vibhāva</s> (determinant).'

body.text:
hasantam aparaṃ dṛṣṭvāvibhāvaḥ copajāyate/
yo 'sau hāsyarasas tajjñaiḥ parasthaḥ parikīrtitaḥ//
body.translated_text: And that which arises upon seeing another person laughing, even without [the spectator directly perceiving] the <s>vibhāva</s> — that <s>hāsya-rasa</s> is declared by the experts as <s>parastha</s> (other-based).

body.text:
uttamānāṃ madhyamānāṃ nīcānām apy asau bhavet/
tryavasthaḥ kathitas tasya ṣaḍbhedāḥ santi cāpare//
body.translated_text: It [<s>hāsya</s>] can belong to the highest (<s>uttama</s>), the middling (<s>madhyama</s>), and the lowest (<s>nīca</s>) [persons]; it is said to have three grades, and moreover there are six subdivisions of it.

body.text:
smitaṃ ca hasitaṃ proktam uttame puruṣe budhaiḥ/
bhaved vihasitaṃ copahasitaṃ madhyame nare//
body.translated_text: The wise have said that <s>smita</s> (gentle smile) and <s>hasita</s> (laughter) [belong to] the highest person; <s>vihasita</s> (open laughter) and <s>upahasita</s> (derisive laughter) [belong to] the middling person.

body.text:
nīce 'pahasitaṃ cātihasitaṃ parikīrtitam/
īṣaphullakapolābhyāṃ kaṭākṣair apy analbaṇaiḥ//
body.translated_text: <s>Apahasita</s> (scornful laughter) and <s>atihasita</s> (excessive laughter) are declared for the lowest [person]. With cheeks slightly bloomed and with unaffected sidelong glances,

body.text:
adṛśyadaśano hāso madhuraḥ smitam ucyate/
vaktranetrakapolaiś ced utphullair upalakṣitaḥ//
body.translated_text: A sweet laugh in which the teeth are not visible is called <s>smita</s> (gentle smile). If marked by blooming face, eyes, and cheeks,

body.text:
kiṃcillakṣitadantaś ca tadā hasitam iṣyate/
saśabdaṃ madhuraṃ kāyagataṃ vadanarāgavat//
body.translated_text: And with teeth slightly visible, then it is considered <s>hasita</s> (laughter). [That which is] accompanied by sound, sweet, bodily, with facial glow,

body.text:
ākuñcitākṣi mandraṃ ca vidur vihasitaṃ budhāḥ/
nikuñcitāṃsaśīrṣaś ca jihmadṛṣṭivilokanaḥ//
body.translated_text: With contracted eyes and deep-toned — the wise know [this] as <s>vihasita</s> (open laughter). With hunched shoulders and head, and with a crooked gaze,

body.text:
utphullanāsiko hāso nāmnopahasitaṃ matam/
asthānajaḥ sāśrudṛṣṭir ākampaskandhamūrdhajaḥ//
body.translated_text: The laugh with distended nostrils is considered by name <s>upahasita</s> (derisive laughter). [That which] arises at an inappropriate occasion, with tearful eyes, with trembling shoulders and head —

body.text:
śārṅgadevena gadito hāso 'pahasitāhvayaḥ/
sthūlakarṇakaṭudhvāno bāṣpapūraplutekṣaṇaḥ/
karopagūḍhapārśvaś ca hāso 'tihasitaṃ matam// iti//
body.translated_text: Is stated by <s>Śārṅgadeva</s> as the laugh called <s>apahasita</s> (scornful laughter). The laugh with a coarse, harsh sound, eyes flooded with tears, and sides clasped by the hands — that is considered <s>atihasita</s> (excessive laughter). Thus [ends the discussion].

body.text:
bhayānako yathā--
"śyenam ambaratalād upāgataṃ śuṣyadānanabilo vilokayan/
kampamānatanur ākulekṣaṇāḥ spandituṃ na hi śaśāka lāvakaḥ//"
body.translated_text:
The terrible (<s>bhayānaka</s> [rasa]), for example:
'Looking at the hawk that descended from the vault of the sky, with its mouth-cavity drying up, its body trembling, its gaze agitated — the lark (<s>lāvaka</s>) was indeed unable to move.'

body.text:
atra śyena ālambanam/ savegāpatanam uddīpanam/ ānanaśoṣādayo 'nubhāvāḥ/ dainyādayaḥ saṃcāriṇaḥ/
bībhatso yathā--
"nakhair vidāritāntrāṇāṃ śavānāṃ pūyaśoṇitam/
ānaneṣv anulimpanti hṛṣṭā vetālayoṣitaḥ//"
śavā ihālambanam/ antravidāraṇādy uddīpanam/ ākṣiptā romāñcanetranimīlanādayo 'nubhāvāḥ/ āvegādayaḥ saṃcāriṇaḥ/
nanu ratikrodhotsāhabhayaśokavismayanirvedeṣu prāg udāhṛteṣu yathālambanāśrayayoḥ saṃpratyayaḥ na tathā hāse jugupsāyāṃ ca/ tatrālambanasyaiva pratīteḥ/ padyaśrotuś ca rasāsvādādhikaraṇatvena laukikahāsajugupsāśrayatvānupapatter iti cet/ satyam/ tadāśrayasya draṣṭṛpuruṣaviśeṣasya tatrākṣepyatvāt/ tadanākṣepe tu śrotuḥ svīyakāntāvarṇanapadyād iva rasodbodhe bādhakābhāvāt/
evaṃ saṃkṣepeṇa nirūpitā rasāḥ/ eṣāṃ prādhānye dhvanivyapadeśahetutvam guṇībhāve tu rasālaṃkāratvam/ kecit tu "prādhānya evaiṣāṃ rasatvam anyathālaṃkāratvam eva/ rasālaṃkāravyapadeśas tv alaṃkāradhvanivyapadeśavat,
brāhmaṇaśramaṇanyāyāt/ evam asaṃlakṣyakramatāyām eva/ anyathā tu vastumātram" ity āhuḥ/ ete cāsaṃlakṣyakramavyaṅgyāḥ sahṛdayena rasavyaktau jhagiti jāyamānāyāṃ vibhāvānubhāvavyabhicārivimarśakramasya sato 'pi sūcīśatapattraśatavedhakramasyevālakṣaṇāt, na tv akramavyaṅgyaḥ, vyaktes taddhetūnāṃ ca hetuhetumadbhāvāsaṃgatyāpatteḥ/
atha katham eta eva rasāḥ/ bhagavadālambanasya romāñcāśrupātādibhir anubhāvitasya harṣādibhiḥ paripoṣitasya bhāgavatādipurāṇaśravaṇasamaye bhagavadbhaktair
anubhūyamānasya bhaktirasasya durapahnavatvāt/ bhagavadanurāgarūpā bhaktiś cātra sthāyibhāvaḥ/ na cāsau śāntarase 'ntarbhāvam arhati/ anurāgasya vairāgyaviruddhatvāt/ ucyate-- bhakter devādiviṣayaratitvena bhāvāntargatatayā rasatvānupapatteḥ/
"ratir devādiviṣayā vyabhicārī tathāñjitaḥ/
bhāvaḥ proktas tadābhāsā hy anaucityapravartitāḥ//"
iti hi prācāṃ siddhāntāt/ na ca tarhi kāminīviṣayāyā api rater bhāvatvam astu, ratitvāviśeṣāt/ astu vā bhagavadbhakter eva sthāyitvam, kāminyādiratīnāṃ ca bhāvatvam vinigamakābhāvāt, iti vācyam/ bharatādimunivacanānām evātra rasabhāvatvādivyavasthāpakatvena svātantryayogāt/
anyathā putrādiviṣayāyā api rateḥ sthāyibhāvatvaṃ kuto na syāt/ na syād vā kutaḥ śuddhabhāvatvaṃ jugupsāśokādīnām ity akhiladarśanaṃ vyākulī syāt/ rasānāṃ navatvagaṇanā ca munivacananiyantritā bhajyeta, iti yathāśāstram eva jyāyaḥ/
eteṣāṃ parasparaṃ kair api virodhaḥ/ tatra vīraśṛṅgārayoḥ, śṛṅgārahāsyayoḥ, vīrādbhutayoḥ, vīraraudrayoḥ, śṛṅgārādbhutayoś cāvirodhaḥ/ śṛṅgārabībhatsayoḥ śṛṅgārakaruṇayoḥ, vīrabhayānakayoḥ, śāntaraudrayoḥ, śāntaśṛṅgārayoś ca virodhaḥ/ atra kavinā prakṛtarasaṃ paripoṣṭukāmena tadabhivyañjake kāvye tadviruddharasāṅgānāṃ nibandhanaṃ na kāryam/ yathā hi sati tadabhivyaktau viruddhaḥ prakṛtaṃ bādheta/ sundopasundanyāyena vobhayor upahatiḥ syāt/ yadi tu viruddhayor api rasayor ekatra samāveśa iṣyate tadā virodhaṃ parihṛtya vidheyaḥ/ tathā hi-- virodhas tāvad dvividhaḥ/ sthitivirodho jñānavirodhaś ca/ ādyas
tadadhikaraṇāvṛttitārūpaḥ/
dvitīyas tajjñānapratibaddhajñānakatvalakṣaṇaḥ/
tatrādhikaraṇāntare virodhinaḥ sthāpane prathamo nivartate/ yathā nāyakagatatvena vīrarase varṇanīye pratināyake bhayānakasya/ rasapadenātra prakaraṇe tadupādhiḥ sthāyibhāvo gṛhyate/ rasasya sāmājikavṛttitvena nāyakādyavṛttitvāt/ advitīyānandamayatvena virodhāsambhavāc ca/
udāharaṇam--
"kuṇḍalīkṛtakodaṇḍadordaṇḍasya puras tava/
mṛgārāter iva mṛgāḥ pare naivāvatasthire//"
rasāntarasyāvirodhinaḥ saṃdhikartur ivāntarāle 'vasthāne dvitīyo 'pi nivartate/ yathā mannirmitāyām ākhyāyikāyāṃ kaṇvāśramagatasya śvetaketor maharṣeḥ śāntarasapradhāne varṇane prastute "kim idam anākalitapūrvaṃ rūpam, ko 'yam anirvācyo vacanaracanāyā madhurimā" ity adbhutasyāntaravasthāpanena varavarṇinīṃ pratyanurāgavarṇane/
yathā vā--
"surāṅganābhir āśliṣṭā vyomni vīrā vimānagāḥ/
vilokante nijān dehān pherunārībhir āvṛtān//"
atra surāṅganāmṛtaśarīrālambanayoḥ śṛṅgārabībhatsayor antaḥ svargalābhākṣipto vīraraso niveśitaḥ/ antarniveśaś ca tadubhayacarvaṇākālāntarvartikālagatacarvaṇākatvam/ tac ca prakṛtapadye prathamārdha eva śṛṅgāracarvaṇottaraṃ vīrasya carvaṇād anantaraṃ ca dvitīyārdhe bībhatsasyeti sphuṭam eva/ "bhūreṇudigdhān" ity ādi kāvyaprakāśagatapadyakadambetu prathamaśrutabībhatsasāmagrīvaśād bībhatsacarvaṇottaraṃ tatsāmagryākṣiptaniḥśaṅkaprāṇatyāgādirūpasāmagrīkasya vīrasya carvaṇe śṛṅgāracarvaṇeti
vivekaḥ/ itthaṃ codāsīnacarvaṇena pratibandhakajñānanivṛttau niṣpratyūhaḥ pratibadhyacarvaṇodaya iti phalito 'rthaḥ/ aṅgāṅginoḥ, aṅginy anyasminn aṅgayor vā na virodhaḥ/ aṅgatvānupapattiprasaṅgāt/
yathā--
pratyudgatā savinayaṃ sahasā sakhībhiḥ smeraiḥ smarasya sacivaiḥ sarasāvalokaiḥ/
mām adya mañjuracanair vacanaiś ca bāle hā leśato 'pi na kathaṃ vada satkaroṣi//
body.translated_text:
Here the hawk is the <s>ālambana</s> (determinant). The swift descent is the <s>uddīpana</s> (excitant). Drying of the face and so on are the <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequents). Dejection and others are the <s>saṃcārins</s> (transitory emotions).
<s>Bībhatsa</s> (disgust) is illustrated as follows—
"The delighted women of the <s>vetālas</s> smear pus and blood of corpses whose entrails have been torn open by nails upon their faces."
Corpses are the <s>ālambana</s> here. Tearing open of entrails and the like is the <s>uddīpana</s>. The involuntary horripilation, closing of eyes, and similar reactions are the <s>anubhāvas</s>. Agitation and others are the <s>saṃcārins</s>.
Now, an objection: in the cases of <s>rati</s> (love), <s>krodha</s> (anger), <s>utsāha</s> (enthusiasm), <s>bhaya</s> (fear), <s>śoka</s> (grief), <s>vismaya</s> (wonder), and <s>nirveda</s> (dispassion) previously illustrated, the identification of both <s>ālambana</s> and <s>āśraya</s> (locus) is clear, but not so in the case of <s>hāsa</s> (laughter) and <s>jugupsā</s> (disgust), since only the <s>ālambana</s> is apprehended there. And since the listener of the verse, being the locus of <s>rasāsvāda</s> (aesthetic relish), cannot be the locus of mundane laughter or disgust. To this we reply: true, but the <s>āśraya</s>, namely a particular observer, is implied therein. And in the absence of such implication, there is no obstacle to the arousal of <s>rasa</s> in the listener, just as from a verse describing one's own beloved.
Thus the <s>rasas</s> have been briefly examined. When they are predominant, they are the cause of being designated as <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion); when subordinate, they constitute <s>rasālaṃkāra</s> (rasa as figure of speech). Some, however, say: "When predominant, these have the status of <s>rasa</s>; otherwise they are simply <s>alaṃkāra</s>. The designation <s>rasālaṃkāra</s> is like the designation <s>alaṃkāradhvani</s>,
following the principle of <s>brāhmaṇa-śramaṇa</s> (where the latter term is subordinated to the former). This applies only in the case of <s>asaṃlakṣyakrama</s> (imperceptible sequence); otherwise, it is merely <s>vastu</s> (content)." These <s>rasas</s> are suggested through imperceptible sequence, because even though the sequence of deliberation on <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants), <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequents), and <s>vyabhicārins</s> (transitory emotions) exists, it is imperceptible—like the sequence of piercing a hundred petals with a hundred needles—when <s>rasa</s> manifests instantaneously in the <s>sahṛdaya</s> (connoisseur). They are not suggested without sequence, for that would lead to the absurdity of there being no cause-effect relationship between the manifestation and its causes.
Now, how can these alone be the <s>rasas</s>? For the <s>bhaktirasa</s> (devotional sentiment) experienced by devotees of the Lord during the hearing of <s>Bhāgavata</s> and other <s>Purāṇas</s>—having the Lord as its <s>ālambana</s>, manifested by <s>anubhāvas</s> such as horripilation and tears, nourished by joy and other emotions—is undeniable. And <s>bhakti</s> (devotion) in the form of passionate love for the Lord is here the <s>sthāyibhāva</s> (permanent emotion). Nor can it be subsumed under <s>śāntarasa</s> (tranquil sentiment), since passionate love is opposed to dispassion. We reply: because <s>bhakti</s>, being a form of <s>rati</s> (love) directed toward deities and the like, is included among the <s>bhāvas</s> (emotions) and therefore cannot have the status of <s>rasa</s>.
"<s>Rati</s> directed toward deities and the like is a <s>vyabhicārin</s> (transitory emotion); when so characterized, it is called a <s>bhāva</s>; and semblances thereof are those prompted by impropriety."
Such is indeed the established doctrine of the ancients. And if so, then should not <s>rati</s> directed toward a woman also have the status of a mere <s>bhāva</s>, since there is no difference in its being <s>rati</s>? Or should devotion to the Lord alone have the status of <s>sthāyibhāva</s>, with <s>rati</s> toward women and others being mere <s>bhāvas</s>, since there is no determining factor? This cannot be said, because the utterances of sages like <s>Bharata</s> alone have the authority to establish the hierarchy of <s>rasa</s> and <s>bhāva</s>.
Otherwise, why should <s>rati</s> directed toward sons and others not also have the status of <s>sthāyibhāva</s>? Or why should <s>jugupsā</s>, <s>śoka</s>, and others not have the status of pure <s>bhāva</s>? The entire system would be thrown into confusion. And the enumeration of nine <s>rasas</s>, which is regulated by the sage's word, would be violated. Therefore, it is best to follow the <s>śāstra</s> (authoritative treatise).
Among these <s>rasas</s>, some are mutually incompatible. Here, <s>vīra</s> (heroic) and <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic), <s>śṛṅgāra</s> and <s>hāsya</s> (comic), <s>vīra</s> and <s>adbhuta</s> (marvelous), <s>vīra</s> and <s>raudra</s> (furious), <s>śṛṅgāra</s> and <s>adbhuta</s> are mutually compatible. <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> and <s>bībhatsa</s> (disgust), <s>śṛṅgāra</s> and <s>karuṇa</s> (compassionate), <s>vīra</s> and <s>bhayānaka</s> (terrible), <s>śānta</s> (tranquil) and <s>raudra</s>, <s>śānta</s> and <s>śṛṅgāra</s> are mutually incompatible. Here, a poet wishing to nourish the principal <s>rasa</s> should not introduce the components of a <s>rasa</s> that is incompatible with it in the poem that suggests it. For if that incompatible <s>rasa</s> were to manifest, it would obstruct the principal one, or by the principle of <s>Sunda</s> and <s>Upasunda</s>, both would be destroyed. But if the co-presence of two mutually incompatible <s>rasas</s> is desired, then the incompatibility should be resolved. Incompatibility is of two kinds: incompatibility of co-existence and incompatibility of cognition. The first is defined as mutual non-occurrence in the same locus.
The second is defined as the property of being a cognition that is obstructed by the cognition of the other.
Of these, the first is resolved by placing the incompatible elements in different loci. For example, when the <s>vīrarasa</s> (heroic sentiment) is to be described in the hero, the <s>bhayānaka</s> (terrible) is placed in the antagonist. By the word '<s>rasa</s>' in this context, the <s>sthāyibhāva</s> (permanent emotion) that is its basis is understood, since <s>rasa</s> itself, being located in the spectator, is not located in the hero and others, and since being of the nature of incomparable bliss, incompatibility is impossible.
An illustration:
"Before you, whose arm-staff has coiled your bow, the enemies did not stand their ground, just as deer before the lord of beasts."
The second type of incompatibility is also resolved by placing a non-incompatible <s>rasa</s> in between, like an intermediary at a peace conference. For instance, in the narrative composed by me, when a description predominantly featuring <s>śāntarasa</s> was being presented about the great sage <s>Śvetaketu</s> at the hermitage of <s>Kaṇva</s>, by interposing <s>adbhuta</s> (wonder)—"What is this form never before perceived, what is this indescribable sweetness of verbal composition?"—a transition was made to the description of love toward the fair lady.
Or as illustrated:
"Embraced by celestial women in the sky, the heroes riding their aerial chariots gaze down at their own bodies surrounded by <s>pherū</s> women (female jackals)."
Here, between <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic) whose <s>ālambana</s> is the celestial women and <s>bībhatsa</s> (disgust) whose <s>ālambana</s> is the dead bodies, <s>vīrarasa</s> (heroic) evoked by the attainment of heaven is inserted in between. The interposition means having its relish occur in the interval between the relishing of those two. And in the verse in question, this is clear: after the relishing of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> in the first half, the relishing of <s>vīra</s> follows, and then in the second half, the relishing of <s>bībhatsa</s>. In the cluster of verses found in <s>Kāvyaprakāśa</s> beginning with "covered with much dust," the analysis is: after the relishing of <s>bībhatsa</s> due to its elements being heard first, then the relishing of <s>vīra</s> whose elements include fearless sacrifice of life implied by that <s>bībhatsa</s> material, and then the relishing of <s>śṛṅgāra</s>.
Thus, through dispassionate relishing, when the obstructing cognition ceases, the unobstructed relishing of the obstructed <s>rasa</s> arises—this is the essential meaning. Between a principal and subordinate <s>rasa</s>, or between two subordinate <s>rasas</s> of another principal, there is no incompatibility, for otherwise the very possibility of subordination would be undermined.
As illustrated:
Greeted respectfully and suddenly by her friends, by the smiling allies of <s>Smara</s> (the god of love)—the sidelong glances full of passion—and by her charming and sweet words, O maiden, tell me, why do you not honor me even a little?

body.text:
iyaṃ ca puro nipatitāṃ pramītāṃ nāyikāṃ prati nāyakasyoktiḥ/ iha nāyikālambanā, aśrupātādibhir anubhāvair āvegaviṣādādibhiḥ saṃcāribhiś ca vyajyamānā nāyakagatā ratis tulyasāmagryabhivyakte prakṛtatvāt pradhānībhūte tadgata eva śoke prakarṣakatvād aṅgam/ yadi tu nāyakagatā ratir nātra pratīyate, kiṃ tu niruktasāmagryā śoka eva prakṛtatvād ity āgṛhyate tadā nāyakālambanā pratyudgamādyanubhāvitā harṣādibhiḥ poṣitā nāyikāśrayā ratir eva tatrāṅgam astu/ nāyikāgatarater nāyakaśokaprakarṣahetutāyāḥ sarvasaṃmatatvāt/ na ca nāyikāyā nāśāt tadgatāyā rater asaṃnidhānāt katham aṅgateti vācyam/ saṃnidhānasyāṅgatāyām atantratvena smaryamāṇāyās tasyā aṅgatvopapatteḥ/
aṅgayor yathā--
"utkṣiptāḥ kabarībharaṃ, vivalitāḥ pārśvadvayaṃ nyakkṛtāḥ
pādāmbhojayugaṃ ruṣā parihṛtā dūreṇa celāñcalam/
gṛhṇanti tvarayā bhavatpratibhaṭakṣmāpālavāmabhruvāṃ
yāntīnāṃ gahaneṣu kaṇṭakacitāḥ ke ke na bhūmīruhāḥ//"
atra samāsoktyavayavābhyāṃ tarukāmikartṛkaripukāminīkabaryādigrahaṇarūpābhyāṃ prakṛtāprakṛtavyavahārābhyāṃ vyaktayoḥ karuṇaśṛṅgārayo rājaviṣayakaratibhāvāṅgatvam/ kiṃ ca prakṛtarasaparipuṣṭim icchatā virodhino 'pi rasasya bādhyatvena nibandhanaṃ kāryam eva/ tathā hi sati vairivijayakṛtā varṇyasya kāpi śobhā saṃpadyate/ bādhyatvaṃ ca rasasya prabalair virodhino rasasyāṅgair vidyamāneṣv api svāṅgeṣu niṣpitteḥ pratibandhaḥ/ vyabhicāriṇo bādhyatvaṃ tu tadīyarasaniṣpattipratibandhamātrāt, na tv anabhivyattayā/ ābhivyaktau bādhakābhāvāt/
na ca virodhyaṅgābhivyatyā pratibandhān nābhivyaktir iti vācyam/ tadvyañjakaśabdārthajñānasamaye virodhyaṅgābhivyañjakaśabdārthajñānasyāsaṃnidhānāt/ pratibadhyapratibandhakabhāvakalpane mānābhāvāt, bhāvaśabalatāyā ucchedāpatteś ca/ rasaniṣpatteḥ pratibandhas tv anubhavasiddha iti tāṃ praty eva virodhyaṅgānāṃ balavatām abhivyakteḥ pratibandhakatvaṃ nyāyyam/ api ca yatra sādhāraṇaviśeṣaṇamahimnā viruddhayor abhivyaktis tatrāpi virodho nivartate/
yathā--
"nitāntaṃ yauvanonmattā gāḍharaktāḥ sadāhave/
vasundharāṃ samāliṅgya śerate vīra te 'rayaḥ//"
ittham avirodhasaṃpādanenāpi nibadhyamāno raso rasaśabdena śṛṅgārādiśabdair vā nābhidhātum ucitaḥ, anāsvādyatāpatteḥ/ tadāsvādaś ca vyañjanamātraniṣpādya ity uktatvāt/ yatra vibhāvādibhir abhivyaktasya rasasya svaśabdenābhidhānaṃ tatra ko doṣa iti cet, vyaṅgyasya vācyīkaraṇe sāmānyato vamanākhyadoṣasya vakṣyamāṇatvāt/ āsvādyatāvacchedakarūpeṇa pratyayājanakatayā rasasthale vācyavṛtteḥ kāpeyakalpatvena viśeṣadoṣatvāc ca/ evaṃ sthāyivyabhicāriṇām api śabdavācyatvaṃ doṣaḥ/ evaṃ vibhāvānubhāvayor asamyakpratyaye vilambena pratyaye vā na rasāsvāda iti tayor doṣatvam/ samabalaprabalapratikūlarasāṅgānāṃ nibandhanaṃ tu prakṛtarasapoṣaprātīpikam iti doṣaḥ/ prabandhe prakṛtasya prasaṅgāntareṇa vicchinnasya punardīpane sāmājikānāṃ na sāmagryeṇa rasāsvāda iti vicchinnadīpanaṃ doṣaḥ/ tathā tattadrasaprastāvanānarhe 'vasare prastāvaḥ,
vicchedānarhe ca vicchedaḥ/ yathā sandhyāvandanadevayajanādidharmavarṇane prasakte kayāpi kāminyā saha kasyacitkāmukasyānurāgavarṇane/ yathā ca samupasthiteṣu mahāhavadurmadeṣu pratibhaṭeṣu marmabhindi vacanāny udgiratsu nāyakasya saṃdhyāvandanādivarṇane cety ubhayam anucitam/
evam apradhānasya pratināyakāder nānāvidhānāṃ caritānām anekavidhāyāś ca saṃpado nāyakasambandhibhyas tebhyo nātiśayo varṇanīyaḥ/ yathā sati varṇayitumiṣṭo nāyakasyotkarṣo na siddhyet/ tatprayukto rasapoṣaś ca na syāt/ na ca pratināyakotkarṣasya tadabhibhāvakanāyakotkarṣāṅgatvāt katham avarṇanīyatvam iti vācyam/ yādṛśasya pratināyakotkarṣavarṇanasya tadabhibhāvakanāyakotkarṣāṅgatāsaṃpādakatvaṃ tādṛśasyeṣṭatvāt/ tadvirodhina eva niṣedhyatvāt/ na ca pratipakṣasya prakṛtāpekṣayā varṇyamāno 'py utkarṣaḥ svāśrayahantṛtāmātrād eva prakṛtagatam utkarṣam atiśāyayet, ato na doṣāvaha iti vācyam/ evaṃ hi sati mahārājaṃ kam api viṣaśarakṣepamātreṇa vyāpāditavato varākasya śabarasyeva prakṛtasya nāyakasya na ko 'py utkarṣaḥ syād iti/ tathā rasālambanāśrayayor anusaṃdhānam antarāntarā viratā na ced, doṣaḥ/ tadanusaṃdhānādhīnā hi rasapratipattidhārā tadananusaṃdhāne viratā syāt/ evaṃ prakṛtarasānupakārakasya vastuno varṇanam api prakṛtarasavirāmahetutvād doṣa eva/ anaucityaṃ tu rasabhaṅgahetutvāt pariharaṇīyam/ bhaṅgaś ca pānakādirasādau sikatādinipātajanitevāruṃtudatā/ tac ca jātideśakālavarṇāśramavayovasthāprakṛtivyavahārādeḥ prapañcajātasya tasya yasya yallokaśāstrasiddham ucitadravyaguṇakriyādi, tadbhedaḥ/ jātyāder anucitaṃ yathā--gavādes tejobalakāryāṇi parākramādīni, siṃhādeś ca sādhubhāvādīni/ svarge jarāvyādhyādi, bhūloke sudhāsevanādi/ śiśire jalavihārādīni, grīṣme vahnisevā/ brāhmaṇasya mṛgayā, bāhujasya pratigrahaḥ, śūdrasya nigamādhyayanam/ brahmacāriṇo yateś ca tāmbūlacarvaṇam, dāropasaṃgraḥ/ bālavṛddhayoḥ strīsevanam, yūnaś ca virāgaḥ/ daridrāṇām āḍhyācaraṇam, āḍhyānāṃ ca daridrācāraḥ/ prakṛtayo divyāḥ,
adivyāḥ, divyādivyāś ca/ dhīrodāttadhīroddhatadhīralalitadhīraśāntā utsāhakrodhakāminīratinirvedapradhānā uttamamadhyamādhamāś ca/ tatra ratyādīnāṃ bhayātiriktasthāyibhāvānāṃ sarvatra samatve 'pi rateḥ saṃbhogarupāyā manuṣyeṣv ivottamadevatāsu sphuṭīkṛtasakalānubhāvavarṇanam anucitam/
krodhasya ca lokabhasmīkaraṇapaṭor dinarātrivyatyayādyanekāścaryakāriṇo divyeṣv ivādivyeṣu/ ālambanagatārādhyatvasyānubhāvagatamithyātvasya ca pratītyā rasānullāsāpatteḥ/ na ca sādhāraṇīkaraṇād ārādhyatvajñānānutpattir iti vācyam/ yatra sahṛdayānāṃ rasodbodhaḥ pramāṇasiddhas tatraiva sādhāraṇīkaraṇasya kalpanāt/ anyathā svamātṛviṣayakasvapitṛrativarṇane 'pi sahṛdayasya rasodbodhāpatteḥ/ jayadevādibhis tu gītagovindādiprabandheṣu sakalasahṛdayasaṃmato'yaṃ samayo madonmattamataṅgajair iva bhinna iti ca tannidarśanenedānīṃtanena tathā varṇayituṃ sāṃpratam/ tathā vidyāvayovarṇāśramatapobhir utkṛṣṭaiḥ svato 'pakṛṣṭeṣu na sabahumānena vacasā vyavahartavyam/ vyavahartavyaṃ cāpakṛṣṭair utkṛṣṭeṣu/ tatrāpi tatrabhavan bhagavann ityādibhiḥ saṃbodhanair munigurudevatāprabhṛtaya eva na rājādayaḥ, jātyottamair dvijair eva, nādhamaiḥ śūdrādibhiḥ, parameśvaretyādisaṃbodhanaiś cakravartina eva, na muniprabhṛtayaḥ saṃbodhyāḥ/
tathā nāhuḥ--
"anaucityād ṛte nānyad rasabhaṅgasya kāraṇam/
