prasiddhaucityabandhas tu rasasyopaniṣatparā//" iti/
yāvatā tv anaucityena rasasya puṣṭis tāvat tu na vāryate, rasapratikūlasyaiva tasya niṣedhyatvāt/ ata eva--
"brahmann adhyayanasya naiṣa samayas tūṣṇīṃ bahiḥ
sthīyatāṃ
svalpaṃ jalpa bṛhaspate jaḍamate naiṣā sabhā vajriṇaḥ/
vīṇāṃ saṃhara nārada stutikathālāpair alaṃ tumburo
sītārallakabhallabhagnahṛdayaḥ svastho na laṅkeśvaraḥ//"
iti kasyacin nāṭakasya padye vipralambhaśṛṅgārāṅgībhūtavīrarasākṣepakaparamaiśvaryaparipoṣakatayā sthitadauvārikavacanasya brahmādyadhikṣepaparasyānaucityaṃ na doṣaḥ/ evam eva "ale le saddaḥsamuppāḍia hariyakusaggaṃthimayācchamālāpai vittivissambhia bālavihavaṃdaḥkaaṇā bamhaṇā" ity ādividūṣakavacane 'pi reśabdādiprayogasya tattathā, hāsyānuguṇatvāt/ eṣā hi digupadarśitā/ anayā sudhībhir anyad apy ūhyam/
raseṣu caiteṣu nigaditeṣu mādhuryaujaḥprasādākhyāṃs trīn guṇān āhuḥ/ tatra "śṛṅgāre saṃyogākhye yanmādhuryaṃ tato 'tiśayitaṃ karuṇe, tābhyāṃ vipralambhe , tebhyo 'pi śānte/ uttarottaram atiśayitāyāś cittadruter jananāt/ saṃyogaśṛṅgārāt karuṇaśāntayos tābhyām api vipralambhe" ity apare/ saṃyogaśṛṅgārāt karuṇavipralambhaśānteṣv atiśayitam eva na punas tatrāpi tāratamyam" ity anye/ tatra prathamacaramayor matayoḥ "karuṇe vipralambhe tacchānte cātiśayānvitam" iti prācāṃ sūtram anukūlam/ tasyottarasūtragatasya krameṇeti padasyāpakarṣānapakarṣābhyāṃ vyākhyādvayasya saṃbhavāt/ madhyasthe tu mate karuṇaśāntābhyāṃ vipralambhasya mādhuryātiśaye yadi sahṛdayānām anubhavo 'sti sākṣī tadā sa pramāṇam/
vīrabībhatsaraudreṣv ojaso yathottaram atiśayaḥ, uttarottaram atiśayitāyāś cittadīpter jananāt/ adbhutahāsyabhayānakānāṃ guṇadvayayogitvaṃ kecid icchanti/ apare tu prasādamātram/ prasādas tu sarveṣu raseṣu sarvāsu racanāsu ca sādhāraṇaḥ/
guṇānāṃ caiṣāṃ drutidīptivikāsākhyās tisraś cittavṛttayaḥ krameṇa prayojyāḥ/ tattadguṇaviśiṣṭarasacarvaṇājanyā iti yāvat/ evam eteṣu guṇeṣu rasamātradharmeṣu
vyavasiteṣu madhurā racanā, ojasvī bandha ity ādayo vyavahārā ākāro 'sya śūra ity ādivyavahāravad aupacārikā iti mammaṭabhaṭṭādayaḥ/
ye 'mī mādhuryaujaḥ prasādārasamātradharmatayoktās teṣāṃ rasadharmatve kiṃ mānam? pratyakṣam eveti cet, na/ dāhādeḥ kāryād analagatasyoṣṇasparśasya yathā bhinnatayānubhavas tathā drutyādicittavṛttibhyo rasakāryebhyo 'nyeṣāṃ rasagataguṇānām ananubhavāt/ tādṛśaguṇaviśiṣṭarasānāṃ drutyādikāraṇatvāt kāraṇatāvacchedakatayā guṇānām anumānam iti cet, prātisvikarūpeṇaiva rasānāṃ kāraṇatopapattau guṇakalpane gauravāt/ śṛṅgārakaruṇaśāntānāṃ mādhuryavattvena drutikāraṇatvaṃ, prātisvikarūpeṇa kāraṇatvakalpanāpekṣayā laghubhūtam iti tu na vācyam/ pareṇa
madhuratarādiguṇānāṃ pṛthag drutataratvādi kāryatāratamyaprayojakatayābhyupagamena mādhuryavattvena kāraṇatāyā gaḍubhūtatvāt/ itthaṃ ca prātisvikarūpeṇaiva kāraṇatve lāghavam/
kiṃ cātmano nirguṇatayātmarūparasaguṇatvaṃ mādhuryādīnām anupapannam/ evaṃ tadupādhiratyādiguṇatvam api, mānābhāvāt, pararītyā guṇe guṇāntarasyānaucityāc ca/ atha śṛṅgāro madhura ity ādivyavahāraḥ katham iti cet, evaṃ tarhi drutyādicittavṛttiprayojakatvam, prayojakatāsaṃbandhena drutyādikam eva vā mādhuryādikam astu/ vyavahāras tu vājigandhoṣṇetivyavahāravad akṣataḥ/
prayojakatvaṃ cādṛṣṭādivilakṣaṇaṃ śabdārtharasaracanāgatam eva grāhyam/ ato na vyavahārātiprasaktiḥ/ tathā ca śabdārthayor api mādhuryāder īdṛśasya sattvād upacāro naiva kalpya iti tu mādṛśāḥ/
jarattarās tu--
śleṣaḥ prasādaḥ samatā mādhuryaṃ sukumāratā/
arthavyaktir udāratvam ojaḥkāntisamādhayaḥ//"
iti daśā śabdaguṇān, daśaiva cārthaguṇān āmananti/ nāmāni punas tāny eva, lakṣaṇaṃ tu bhinnam/
tathā hi--
śabdānāṃ bhinnānām apy ekatvapratibhānaprayojakaḥ saṃhitayaikajātīyavarṇavinyāsaviśeṣo gāḍhatvāparaparyāyaḥ śleṣaḥ//
body.translated_text: The particular arrangement of phonemes of the same class, brought together in compound (<s>saṃhitā</s>), which causes the cognition of unity even among distinct words, is compactness (<s>gāḍhatva</s>), otherwise known as <s>śleṣa</s> (close joining).

body.text: yadāhuḥ- "śliṣṭam aspaṣṭaśaithilyam" iti/ yathā--"anavaratavidvaddrumadrohidāridryamādyaddvipoddāmadarpaughavidrāvaṇaprauḍhapañcānanaḥ iti/
body.translated_text: As they say: "<s>Śliṣṭa</s> (closely joined) is that in which looseness is imperceptible." For example: "<s>anavaratavidvaddrumadrohidāridryamādyaddvipoddāmadarpaughavidrāvaṇaprauḍhapañcānanaḥ</s>" [He whose mighty lion-like prowess drives away the torrents of unbridled arrogance of elephants maddened by poverty that is hostile to the trees of unceasing scholars].

body.text: gāḍhatvaśaithilyābhyāṃ vyutkrameṇa miśraṇaṃ bandhasya prasādaḥ//
body.translated_text: The mixing in reverse order of compactness (<s>gāḍhatva</s>) and looseness (<s>śaithilya</s>) of composition is <s>prasāda</s> (lucidity).

body.text:
yathā--
"kiṃ brūmas tava vīratāṃ vayam amī, yasmin dharākhaṇḍala-
krīḍākuṇḍalitabhruśoṇanayane dormaṇḍalaṃ paśyasi/
māṇikyāvalikāntidanturatarair bhūṣāsahastrotsarair
vindhyāraṇyaguhāgṛhāvaniruhās tatkālam ullāsitāḥ//"
atra yasminn ityantaṃ śaithilyam, bhruśabdāntaṃ gāḍhatvam, punar nayanetyantaṃ prathamam ityādi bodhyam/
body.translated_text: For example: "What shall we say of your valor, O you in whose reddened eyes with brows curled in the sport of being the <s>Indra</s> of the earth one sees the circle of arms? With ornamental cascades of a thousand [gems] beautified by rows of rubies rivaling teeth, the trees in the cave-dwellings of the forests of <s>Vindhya</s> were at that very moment made to blossom." Here, up to "in whom" (<s>yasmin</s>) there is looseness; up to the word "brow" (<s>bhru</s>) there is compactness; then again up to "eye" (<s>nayana</s>) there is the first [looseness], and so on—this should be understood.

body.text: upakramād āsamāpte rītyabhedaḥ samatā//
body.translated_text: Uniformity of <s>rīti</s> (style) from the beginning to the end is <s>samatā</s> (evenness).

body.text: yathā vakṣyamāṇamādhuryodāharaṇe/ tatra hy upanāgarikayaivopakramasaṃhārau/
body.translated_text: As in the forthcoming example of <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness). For there, both the opening and the conclusion are in the <s>upanāgarikā</s> (elegant/urbane) [style] alone.

body.text: saṃyogaparahrasvātiriktavarṇaghaṭitatve sati pṛthakpadatvaṃ mādhuryam//
body.translated_text: <s>Mādhurya</s> (sweetness) is the quality of being composed of separate words, with the condition that [the composition] consists of phonemes other than conjunct consonants and short vowels.

body.text:
yathā--
"nitarāṃ paruṣā sarojamālā na mṛṇālāni vicārapeśalāni/
yadi komalatā tavāṅgakānām atha kā nāma kathāpi pallavānām//"
body.translated_text: For example: "The garland of lotuses is exceedingly harsh, nor are the lotus stalks delicate in discernment; if such is the softness of your limbs, then what talk is there even of tender shoots?"

body.text: aparuṣavarṇaghaṭitatvaṃ sukumāratā//
body.translated_text: <s>Sukumāratā</s> (delicacy) is being composed of non-harsh phonemes.

body.text:
yathā--
svedāmbusāndrakaṇaśālikapolapālidolāyitaśravaṇakuṇḍalavandanīyā/
ānandam aṅkurayati smaraṇena kāpi ramyā daśā manasi me madirekṣaṇāyāḥ//"
atra pūrvārdhe/ uttarārdhe tu mādhuryam api/
body.translated_text: For example: "Adorned with a row of full, round drops of perspiration on her cheeks, with earrings swaying—worthy of salutation—some delightful state of that intoxicant-eyed woman sprouts joy in my mind through remembrance." Here [this applies to] the first half. In the second half, however, there is also <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness).

body.text: jhagiti pratīyamānārthānvayakatvam arthavyaktiḥ//
body.translated_text: <s>Arthavyakti</s> (clarity of meaning) is the quality of enabling the immediately perceived connection of meaning.

body.text: yathā "nitarām" ityādau/
body.translated_text: As in the previously [cited verse] beginning with "exceedingly" (<s>nitarām</s>) and so forth.

body.text: kaṭhinavarṇaghaṭanārūpavikaṭatvalakṣaṇodāratā//
body.translated_text: <s>Udāratā</s> (grandeur) is defined as ruggedness (<s>vikaṭatva</s>), which consists in the arrangement of harsh phonemes.

body.text:
yathā--
"pramodabharatundilapramathadattatālāvalī-
vinodini vināyake ḍamaruḍiṇḍimadhvānini/
lalāṭataṭavisphuṭannavakṛpīṭayonicchaṭo
haṭhoddhatajaṭodbhaṭo gatapaṭo naṭo nṛtyati//"
"padānāṃ nṛtyatprāyatvaṃ vikaṭatā" iti kāvyaprakāśaṭīkākārā vyācakṣate/ udāharanti ca "svacaraṇaviniviṣṭair nūpurair nartakīnāṃ jhaṭiti raṇitam āsīt" ityādi/ tatra teṣām etādṛśīṃ vikaṭatvalakṣaṇām udāratām ojasy
antarbhāvayan kāvyaprakāśakāraḥ katham anukūla iti ta eva jānanti/ na hy atraujaso vaipulyena pratibhānam asti/
"viniviṣṭair nūpurair narta-" ity atra sannapy ojaso lavo na camatkārī/ nāpi tatra nṛtyatprāyatvaṃ varṇānām anubhavanti sahṛdayāḥ/ aṃśāntare tu mādhuryam eva/
body.translated_text: For example: "When <s>Vināyaka</s> (<s>Gaṇeśa</s>) sports, made jubilant by the overflowing delight, with the rhythmic clapping bestowed by the enraptured <s>Pramatha</s> attendants, while the <s>ḍamaru</s> drum and <s>ḍiṇḍima</s> drum resound, the dancer (<s>Naṭa</s>, i.e., <s>Śiva</s>) dances—unclothed, with matted locks flying upward in a sudden burst of the blazing fire born from the new <s>kṛpīṭa</s> (cremation ground) flashing on the surface of his forehead." The commentators of the <s>Kāvyaprakāśa</s> explain: "The quality of words appearing to dance is <s>vikaṭatā</s> (ruggedness)." And they cite as example: "The anklets fastened upon the feet of the dancing girls suddenly jingled" and so forth. In that case, how the author of the <s>Kāvyaprakāśa</s>, who subsumes this kind of <s>udāratā</s> characterized as <s>vikaṭatva</s> under <s>ojas</s> (vigor), can be considered consistent—only those [commentators] themselves know. For there is no cognition here of <s>ojas</s> in its fullness. In "<s>viniviṣṭair nūpurair narta-</s>," even though a trace of <s>ojas</s> is present, it does not produce <s>camatkāra</s> (aesthetic wonder). Nor do <s>sahṛdayas</s> (connoisseurs) experience the dance-like quality of phonemes there. In the other portion, however, there is indeed <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness).

body.text: saṃyogaparahrasvaprācuryarūpaṃ gāḍhatvam ojaḥ//
body.translated_text: <s>Ojas</s> (vigor) is compactness (<s>gāḍhatva</s>) characterized by an abundance of conjunct consonants and short vowels.

body.text:
yathā--
"sāhaṃkārasurāsurāvalikarākṛṣṭabhramanmandara-
kṣubhyatkṣīradhivalguvīcivalayaśrīgarvasarvaṃkaṣāḥ/
tṛṣṇātāmyadamandatāpasakulaiḥ sānandam ālokitā
bhūmībhūṣaṇa bhūṣayanti bhūvanābhogaṃ bhavatkīrtayaḥ//"
yathā vā "ayaṃ patatu nirdayam" ityādiprāg udāhṛte/
body.translated_text: For example: "Your glories, O ornament of the earth, which abrade all the splendor and beauty of the waves of the charming rippling circles of the churning milk-ocean, agitated by <s>Mandara</s> mountain whirling as it is pulled by the rows of hands of the arrogant gods and demons—those glories, gazed upon with delight by throngs tormented by the heat of unrelenting desire, adorn the expanse of the world." Or as in the previously cited [verse] beginning with "Let this one fall mercilessly" and so forth.

body.text: avidagdhavaidikādiprayogayogyānāṃ padānāṃ parihāreṇa prayujyamāneṣu padeṣu lokottaraśobhārūpam aujjvalyaṃ kāntiḥ//
body.translated_text: <s>Kānti</s> (brilliance) is the quality of extraordinary beauty (<s>aujjvalya</s>) in the words employed, through the avoidance of words suitable for use by the unrefined, in Vedic [ritual contexts], and the like.

body.text: yathā "nitarām" ityādi prāg udāhṛte/

children.translated_text: <s>Samādhi</s> (compositional balance) is the arrangement in order of compactness (<s>gāḍhatva</s>) and looseness (<s>śithilatva</s>) in connected [discourse].

body.translated_text: As in the previously cited [verse] beginning with "exceedingly" (<s>nitarām</s>) and so forth.

body.text:
anayor eva prācīnair ārohāvarohavyapadeśaḥ kṛtaḥ/ krama eva hi tayoḥ prasādād asya bhedakaḥ/ tatra hi tayor vyutkrameṇa vṛtteḥ/
yathā--
svarganirgatanirargalagaṅgātuṅgubhaṅgurataraṅgasakhānām/
body.translated_text: These same two [qualities] were designated by the ancients as ascent (<s>āroha</s>) and descent (<s>avaroha</s>). For it is precisely the order [of arrangement] that distinguishes this [<s>samādhi</s>] from <s>prasāda</s> (lucidity); since in that [<s>prasāda</s>], the two occur in reverse order. For example: "Whose lotus-face is the dancing hall of words that shower nothing but nectar, companions of the tall, curving waves of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> descending unimpeded from heaven."

body.text:
kevalāmṛtamucāṃ vacanānāṃ yasya lāsyagṛham āsyasarojam//"
atrārohaḥ prathame 'rdhe/ tṛtīyacaraṇe tv avarohaḥ/ gaṅgety ādau mādhuryasya vyañjakeṣu varṇeṣu satsv api dīrghasamāsāntaḥpātitayāna tasya prarohaḥ/ uttarārdhe tu so 'pi/ ete daśa śabdaguṇāḥ/
body.translated_text: Here there is ascent (<s>āroha</s>) in the first half. In the third quarter, however, there is descent (<s>avaroha</s>). From "<s>Gaṅgā</s>" onward, even though phonemes that suggest <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness) are present, that [sweetness] does not sprout because [the words] are subsumed within a long compound. In the latter half, however, it [sweetness] also [appears]. These are the ten qualities of sound (<s>śabdaguṇa</s>).

body.text: evaṃ kriyāparamparayā vidagdhaceṣṭitasya tadasphuṭatvasya tadupapādakayukteś ca sāmānādhikaraṇyarūpaḥ saṃsargaḥ śleṣaḥ//
body.translated_text: Thus, <s>śleṣa</s> [as a quality of meaning] is the co-predication (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>), which takes the form of a connection between the clever action (<s>vidagdhaceṣṭita</s>), its non-obviousness, and the reasoning that establishes it, [all brought about] through a sequence of actions.

body.text: yāvad arthakapadatvarūpam arthavaimalyaṃ prasādaḥ//
body.translated_text: <s>Prasāda</s> [as a quality of meaning] is clarity of meaning (<s>arthavaimalya</s>), which takes the form of using only as many words as are needed to convey the sense.

body.text: yathā-- "kamalānukāri vadanaṃ kila tasyāḥ" ityādi/ pratyudāharaṇaṃ tu "kamalakāntyanukāri vaktram" ityādi /
body.translated_text: For example: "Her face, they say, resembles a lotus" and so forth. A counter-example would be: "Her face imitates the beauty of a lotus" and so forth.

body.text: prakramābhaṅgenārthaghaṭanātmakam avaiṣamyaṃ samatā//
body.translated_text: <s>Samatā</s> (evenness) [as a quality of meaning] is the absence of unevenness (<s>avaiṣamya</s>), which consists in the construction of meaning without breaking the established pattern (<s>prakrama</s>).

body.text:
yathā--
"hariḥ pitā harirmātā harirbhrātā hariḥ suhṛt/
hariṃ sarvatra paśyāmi harer anyan na bhāti me//"
atra viṣṇur bhrātety ādinirmāṇe prakramabhaṅgātmakaṃ vaiṣamyam/
body.translated_text: For example: "<s>Hari</s> is [my] father, <s>Hari</s> is [my] mother, <s>Hari</s> is [my] brother, <s>Hari</s> is [my] friend; I see <s>Hari</s> everywhere, nothing other than <s>Hari</s> shines for me." Here, in the construction "<s>Viṣṇu</s> is a brother" and so forth, there would be unevenness (<s>vaiṣamya</s>) in the form of breaking the established pattern.

body.text: ekasyā evokter bhaṅgyantareṇa punaḥ kathanātmakam uktivaicitryaṃ mādhuryam//
body.translated_text: <s>Mādhurya</s> [as a quality of meaning] is variety of expression (<s>uktivaicitrya</s>), which consists in stating the same idea again through a different turn of phrase.

body.text:
yathā--
"vidhattāṃ niḥśaṅkaṃ niravadhisamādhiṃ vidhir aho
sukhaṃ śeṣe śetāṃ harir avīrataṃ nṛtyatu haraḥ/
kṛtaṃ prāyaścittair alam atha tapodānayajanaiḥ
body.translated_text: For example: "Let <s>Vidhī</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) without apprehension undertake unlimited meditation, ah! Let <s>Hari</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) sleep at ease upon <s>Śeṣa</s>, let <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) dance unceasingly; enough with penances, enough with austerities, gifts, and sacrifices,

body.text:
savitrī kāmānāṃ yadi jagati jāgarti bhavatī//"
atra vidhyādibhir nāsti kim api prayojanam ity eṣo 'rthaḥ samādhividhānādipreraṇārūpeṇoktivaicitryeṇābhihitaḥ/ anyathānavīkṛtatvāpatteḥ/
body.translated_text: if <s>Sāvitrī</s> (<s>the goddess</s>), the fulfiller of desires, is awake in the world as you [O lady]." Here, the meaning that there is no purpose whatsoever for <s>Vidhi</s> and the others is expressed through the variety of expression (<s>uktivaicitrya</s>) in the form of exhorting [them] to undertake meditation and so forth. Otherwise, the fault of not being novel would arise.

body.text: akāṇḍe śokadāyitvābhāvarūpam apāruṣyaṃ sukumāratā//
body.translated_text: <s>Sukumāratā</s> (delicacy) [as a quality of meaning] is non-harshness (<s>apāruṣya</s>), which takes the form of not causing grief unexpectedly.

body.text:
yathā-- "tvarayā yāti pāntho 'yaṃ priyāvirahakātaraḥ"/
"priyāmaraṇakātaraḥ" ity atra tu śokadāyino maraṇaśabdasya sattvāt pāruṣyam/ idaṃ cāślīlatādoṣavyāpyam/
body.translated_text: For example: "This traveler goes in haste, anxious from separation from his beloved." But in "anxious from the death of his beloved," there is harshness (<s>pāruṣya</s>) due to the presence of the word "death" (<s>maraṇa</s>), which causes grief. And this is pervaded by the fault of <s>aślīlatā</s> (impropriety).

body.text: vastuno varṇanīyasyāsādhāraṇakriyārūpayor varṇanam arthavyaktiḥ//
body.translated_text: <s>Arthavyakti</s> (clarity of meaning) [as a quality of meaning] is the description of the unique actions and forms of the object being described.

body.text:
yathā--
gurumadhye kamalākṣī kamalākṣeṇa prahartukāmaṃ mām/
radayantritarasanāgraṃ taralitanayanaṃ nivārayāṃcakre//"
ayam evedānīṃtanaiḥsvabhāvoktyalaṃkāra iti vyapadiśyate/
body.translated_text: For example: "The lotus-eyed one, in the midst of the elders, restrained me who wished to strike with a glance from [her] lotus eyes, with the tip of her tongue held back by her teeth, with trembling eyes." This very [quality] is now designated by modern [rhetoricians] as the figure called <s>svabhāvokti</s> (natural description).

body.text: "cumbanaṃ dehi me bhārye kāmacāṇḍālatṛptaye" ity ādigrāmyārthaparihāra udāratā//
body.translated_text: <s>Udāratā</s> (grandeur) [as a quality of meaning] is the avoidance of vulgar meanings such as "Give me a kiss, O wife, to satisfy the <s>Cāṇḍāla</s> (outcaste) of desire" and the like.

body.text: ekasya padārthasya bahubhiḥ padair abhidhānaṃ, bahūnāṃ caikena, tathaikasya vākyārthasya bahubhir vākyaiḥ, bahuvākyārthasyaikavākyenābhidhānaṃ, viśeṣaṇānāṃ sābhiprāyatvaṃ ceti pañcavidham ojaḥ//
body.translated_text: <s>Ojas</s> (vigor) [as a quality of meaning] is fivefold: the expression of one thing by many words; and of many things by one word; likewise the expression of one sentence-meaning by many sentences; and of many sentence-meanings by one sentence; and the purposefulness of qualifiers.

body.text:
yad āhuḥ--
padārthe vākyaracanā vākyārthe ca padābhidhā/
prauḍhir vyāsasamāsau ca sābhiprāyatvam asya ca// iti/
pūrvārdhapratipādyaṃ dvayaṃ vyāsasamāsau ceti catuṣprakārā prauḍhiḥ, sābhiprāyatvaṃ ceti pañcaprakāram oja ity arthaḥ/ prauḍhiḥ pratipādanavaicitryam/
yathā--
"sarasijavanabandhuśrīsamārambhakāle
rajaniramaṇarājye nāśam āśu prayāti/
paramapuruṣavaktrād udgatānāṃ narāṇāṃ
madhumadhuragirāṃ ca prādurāsīd vinodaḥ//"
atroṣasīty ekapadārthasyābhidhānāya prathamacaraṇaḥ/ ity ādyagre 'pi bodhyam/
"khaṇḍitānetrakañjālimañjurañjanapaṇḍitāḥ/
maṇḍitākhiladikprāntāś caṇḍāṃśor bhānti bhānavaḥ//"
atra "yasyāḥ parāṅganāgehāt patiḥ prātargṛhe 'ñcati" iti vākyārthe khaṇḍitāpadābhidhānam/
"ayācitaḥ sukhaṃ datte yācitaś ca na yacchati/
sarvasvaṃ cāpi harate vidhir ucchṛṅkhalo nṛṇām//"
atra daivādhīnaṃ sarvam ity ekasmin vākyārthe nānāvākyaracanātmako vyāsapadavācyo vistaraḥ/
"tapasyato muner vaktrād vedārtham adhigatya saḥ/
vāsudevaniviṣṭātmā
viveśa param padam//"
atra "munis tapasyati", "tadvaktrāt sa vedārtham adhigatavān", "tadanantaraṃ vāsudeve parabrahmaṇi manaḥ prāveśayat", "tataś ca mukto 'bhūd" iti vākyārthakalāpaḥ śatṛ-ktvā-bahuvrīhibhis tiṅantena cānuvādyavidheyabhāvenaikavākyārthīkṛtaḥ/ sābhiprāyatvaṃ caprakṛtārthapoṣakatā/
yathā--
"gaṇikājāmilamukhyānavatā bhavatā batāham api/
sīdanbhavamarugarte karuṇāmūrte na sarvathopekṣyaḥ//"
atropekṣābhāve karuṇāmūrtitvaṃ poṣakam/ pāpiṣṭhavāt karuṇāyā abhāve prakṛte 'syāḥ saṃpādanāya gaṇikety ādi sīdann iti ca/
body.translated_text:
As they state—
"Sentence construction for a word-meaning, and word-denotation for a sentence-meaning; maturity (<s>prauḍhi</s>), elaboration (<s>vyāsa</s>) and compression (<s>samāsa</s>), and purposefulness (<s>sābhiprāyatva</s>) of it." //
The two topics taught in the first half, together with elaboration and compression, make four types of <s>prauḍhi</s> (maturity); adding purposefulness makes five types of <s>ojas</s> (vigor)—this is the meaning. <s>Prauḍhi</s> is variety in the mode of expression.
For example—
"At the time when the beauty of the friend of the lotus-grove begins, when in the kingdom of the lover of night destruction swiftly approaches, for men there arose delight in the honey-sweet words that issued from the mouth of the Supreme Person." //
Here, the first quarter is employed to denote the single word-meaning 'dawn' (<s>uṣas</s>). This should be understood similarly in subsequent examples as well.
"Having shattered the beautiful collyrium-adorned tips of the lotus-like eyes, the rays of the fierce-rayed one (<s>Sūrya</s>) shine forth, adorning all the quarters' edges." //
Here, the word <s>khaṇḍitā</s> denotes the sentence-meaning 'she whose husband goes from another woman's house to his own home in the morning' (<s>yasyāḥ parāṅganāgehāt patiḥ prātargṛhe 'ñcati</s>).
"Unasked, he happily gives; but when asked, he does not give; and he takes away everything—such is fate (<s>vidhi</s>), unrestrained toward men." //
Here, for the single sentence-meaning 'everything depends on fate,' there is elaboration (<s>vyāsa</s>)—expansion through multiple sentence constructions, which is what the term <s>vyāsa</s> denotes.
"Having learned the meaning of the <s>Vedas</s> from the mouth of the sage who was performing austerities, he, with his mind fixed on <s>Vāsudeva</s>, entered the supreme abode." //
Here, the cluster of sentence-meanings—'the sage performs austerities,' 'from his mouth he learned the Vedic meaning,' 'thereafter he directed his mind to <s>Vāsudeva</s>, the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>,' 'and then he was liberated'—is unified into a single sentence-meaning through present participles (<s>śatṛ</s>), absolutives (<s>ktvā</s>), possessive compounds (<s>bahuvrīhi</s>), and a finite verb (<s>tiṅanta</s>) in the relationship of topic and predicate. Purposefulness (<s>sābhiprāyatva</s>) is the quality of nourishing the subject at hand.
For example—
"By you who have saved the chief sinners like the courtesan and <s>Jāmila</s>—alas!—even I, sinking in the desert-pit of <s>saṃsāra</s>, O embodiment of compassion, should not be altogether neglected!" //
Here, the quality of being an embodiment of compassion (<s>karuṇāmūrti</s>) nourishes the argument against neglect. And for [establishing] the presence of compassion—which, in the absence of the speaker being a greater sinner [than those already saved], would be absent from the subject—the phrases 'the courtesan etc.' and 'sinking' serve to secure it.

body.text: dīptarasatvaṃ kāntiḥ//
body.translated_text: The state of having brilliant <s>rasa</s> is <s>kānti</s> (lustre). //

body.text: tac ca sphuṭapratīyamānarasatvam/ udāharaṇaṃ ca varṇitam eva rasaprakaraṇe, varṇayiṣyate ca/
body.translated_text: And that is the quality of having clearly perceived <s>rasa</s>. Examples have already been given in the section on <s>rasa</s>, and more will be given.

body.text: avarṇitapūrvo 'yam arthaḥ pūrvavarṇitacchāyo veti kaver ālocanaṃ samādhiḥ//
body.translated_text: The poet's reflection on whether 'this meaning has not been described before' or 'it has the semblance of what was previously described' is <s>samādhi</s> (poetic contemplation). //

body.text:
jñānasya viṣayatāsaṃbandhenārthaniṣṭhatvād arthaguṇatā/
ādyo yathā-- "tanayamainākagaveṣaṇa" ityādau, dvitīyas tu prāyaśaḥ sarvatraivety āhuḥ/ apare tv eṣu guṇeṣu katipayān prāguktais tribhir guṇair vakṣyamāṇadoṣābhāvālaṃkāraiś ca gatārthayantaḥ kāṃścid vaicitryamātrarūpatayā, kvacid doṣatayā ca manyamānā na tāvataḥ svīkurvanti/ tathā hi-- śleṣodāratāprasādasamādhīnām ojovyañjakaghaṭanāyām antarbhāvaḥ/ na ca śleṣodāratayoḥ sarvāṃśe gāḍhabandhātmanor ojovyañjakaghaṭanāntarbhāvo 'stu nāma, prasādasamādhyos tu
gāḍhaśithilātmanor aṃśenaujovyañjakāntarbhāve 'py aṃśāntareṇa kutrāntarbhāva iti vācyam/ mādhuryābhivyañjake prasādābhivyañjake veti suvacatvāt/ mādhuryaṃ tu pareṣām asmadabhyupagatamādhuryavyañjakam eva/ evaṃ ca sarvatra vyañjake vyaṅgyaśabdaprayogo bhāktaḥ/ samatā tu sarvatrānucitaiva/ pratipādyodbhaṭatvānudbhaṭatvābhyāmekasminn eva padye mārgabhedasyeṣṭatvāt/
yathā--
"nirmāṇe yadi mārmiko 'si nitarām atyantapākadravan-mṛdvīkāmadhumādhurīmadaparīhāroddhurāṇāṃ girām/
kāvyaṃ tarhi sakhe sukhena kathaya tvaṃ saṃmukhe mādṛśāṃ
no ced duṣkṛtam ātmanā kṛtam iva svāntād bahir mā kṛthāḥ//"
atra pūrvārdhe tṛtīyacaraṇe ca lokottaranirmāṇapratipādake yo mārgo na sa caturthacaraṇe kadaryakāvyapratipādaka iti vaiṣamyam eva guṇaḥ/ grāmyatvakaṣṭatvayos tyāgāt kāntisaukumāryayor gatārthatā/ prasādena cārthavyakter iti/
arthaguṇeṣv api-- śleṣaḥ ojasa ādyāś catvāro bhedāś ca uktivaicitryamātrarūpā iti na guṇāntarbhāvam arhanti/ anyathā pratiślokam arthavaicitryavailakṣaṇyād guṇabhedāpatteḥ/ anadhikapadatvātmā prasādaḥ, uktivaicitryavapur mādhuryam, apāruṣyaśarīraṃ saukumāryam, agrāmyarūpodāratā, vaiṣamyābhāvalakṣaṇā samatā, sābhiprāyatvātmakaḥ pañcama ojasaḥ prakāraḥ, svabhāvasphuṭatvātmikārthavyaktiḥ, sphuṭarasatvarūpā kāntiś ca, adhikapadatvānavīkṛtatvāmaṅgalarūpāślīlatvagrāmya-bhagnaprakramāpuṣṭārtharūpāṇāṃ doṣāṇāṃ nirākaraṇena svabhāvoktyalaṃkārasya rasadhvanirasavadalaṃkārayoś ca svīkaraṇena ca gatārthāni/ samādhis tu kavigataḥ kāvyasya kāraṇaṃ na tu guṇaḥ, pratibhāyā api kāvyaguṇatvāpatteḥ/ atas traya eva guṇā iti mammaṭabhaṭṭādayaḥ/
tatra ṭavargavarjitānāṃ vargāṇāṃ prathamatṛtīyaiḥ śarbhir antasthaiś ca ghaṭitā, naikaṭyena prayuktair anusvāraparasavarṇāiḥ śuddhānunāsikaiś ca śobhitā, vakṣyamāṇaiḥ sāmānyato viśeṣataś ca niṣiddhaiḥ saṃyogādyair acumbitā, avṛttir muduvṛttirvā racanānupūrvyātmikā mādhuryasya vyañjikā/ dvitīyacaturthās tu vargyā guṇasyāsya nānukūlāḥ, nāpi pratikūlāḥ, dūratayā saṃniveśitāś cet/ naikaṭyena tu pratikūlā api bhavanti, yadi tadāyatto nānuprāsaḥ/ anye tu vargasthānāṃ pañcānām apy aviśeṣeṇa mādhuryavyañjakatām āhuḥ/
udāharaṇam--
tāṃ tamālatarukāntilaṅghinīṃ kiṃkarīkṛtanavāmbudatviṣam
svānta me kalaya śāntaye ciraṃ naicikīnayanacumbitāṃ śriyam//"
yathā vā--
"svedāmbusāndrakaṇaśālikapolapālir antaḥsmitālasavilokanavandanīyā/
ānandam aṅkurayati smaraṇena kāpi ramyā daśā manasi me madirekṣaṇāyāḥ//"
prathame padye 'tiśayoktyalaṃkṛtasya bhagavaddhyānautsukyasya bhagavadviṣayakarater vā dhvanyamānāyāḥ śānta eva paryavasānāt tadgatamādhuryasyābhivyañjikā racaneyam/ dvitīye tu smṛtyupaṣṭabdhaśṛṅgāragatasya/ naikaṭyena dvitīyacaturthavargavarṇaṭavargajihvāmūlīyopadhmānīyavisargasakārabahulair varṇāir ghaṭito jhayrephānyataraghaṭitasaṃyogaparahrasvaiś ca naikaṭyena prayuktair āliṅgito dīrghavṛttyātmā gumpha ojasaḥ/ asmin patitāḥ prathamatṛtīyavargyā guṇasyāsya nānukūlā nāpi pratikūlāḥ saṃyogāghaṭakāś cet/
tadghaṭakās tv anukūlā eva/ evam anusvāraparasavarṇā api/ yathā-- "ayaṃ patatu nirdayaṃ dalitadṛpta-" ity ādau prāgudāhṛte/ śrutamātrā vākyārtham karatalabadaram iva nivedayantī ghaṭanā prasādasya/ ayaṃ ca sarvasādhāraṇo guṇaḥ/ udāharaṇāny atra prāyaśo madīyāni sarvāṇy eva padyāni/ tathāpi yathā--
"cintāmīlitamānaso manasijaḥ sakhyo vihīnaprabhāḥ
prāṇeśaḥ praṇayākulaḥ punar asāv āstāṃ samastā kathā/
etat tvāṃ vinivedayāmi mama ceduktiṃ hitāṃ manyase
mugdhe mā kuru mānam ānanam idaṃ rākāpatir jeṣyati//"
atra sarvāvacchedena prasādābhivyañjakatvam aṃśabhedena tu mādhuryaujobhivyañjakatvam api, manasijāntasya mā kurv ādeś ca mādhuryābhivyaktihetutvāt/ sakhya ityāder ojogamakatvāt/ nanv atra śṛṅgārāśrayasya mādhuryasyābhivyaktaye tadanukūlās tu nāma racanā, ojasas tu kaḥ prasaṅgo yad arthaṃ tadanukūlavarṇavinyāsa iti cet/
nāyikāmānopaśāntaye kṛtānekayatnāyās tadīyaṃ hitam upadiśantyāḥ sakhyāḥ sakrodhatvasya vyañjanīyatayā tathāvinyāsasya sāphalyāt/ kiṃ bahunā rasasyaujasvino 'marṣāder bhāvasya cāvivakṣāyām api vaktari kruddhatayā prasiddhe vācye vā krūratare ākhyāyikādau prabandhe vā, paruṣavarṇaghaṭaneṣyate/ yathā vā--
vācā nirmalayā sudhāmadhurayā yāṃ nātha śikṣāmadās
tāṃ svapne 'pi na saṃspṛśāmy aham ahaṃbhāvāvṛto nistrapaḥ/
ity āgaḥśataśālinaṃ punar api svīyeṣu māṃ bibhratas
tvatto nāsti dayānidhir yadupate matto na mattaḥ paraḥ//"
atra guṇāntarāsamānādhikaraṇaḥ prasādaḥ/ idānīṃ
tattadguṇavyañjanakṣamāyā nirmiteḥ paricayāya sāmānyato viśeṣataś ca varjanīyaṃ kiṃcin nirūpyate-- varṇānāṃ svānantaryaṃ sakṛdekapadagatatve kiṃcid aśravyam/ yathā-- "kakubhasurabhiḥ, vitatagātraḥ, palalam ivābhāti" ity ādau/ asakṛc ced adhikam// yathā-- "vitatatarastarur eṣa bhāti bhūmau"/ evaṃ bhinnapadagatatve 'pi/ yathā-- "śuka karoṣi kathaṃ vijane rucim" ity ādau/ asakṛdbhinnapadagatatve tato 'py adhikam/ yathā-- "pika kakubho mukharīkuru prakāmam"/ evaṃ svasamānavargyānantaryaṃ sakṛd ekapadagatatve kiṃcid aśravyam/ yathā-- "vitathas te manorathaḥ"/ asakṛc ced adhikam/ yathā-- "vitathataraṃ vacanaṃ tava pratīmaḥ"/ evaṃ bhinnapadagatatve/ yathā-- "atha tasya vacaḥ śrutvā" ity ādau/ asakṛd bhinnapadagatatve tu tato 'py adhikam/ "atha tathā kuru yena sukhaṃ labhe"/ etac ca vargāṇāṃ prathamadvitīyayos tṛtīyacaturthayor ānantaryam/ prathamatṛtīyayor dvitīyatṛtīyayor vānantaryaṃ tu tathā nāśrāvyam/ kiṃ tv īṣat, nirmāṇamārmikaikavedyam/ etad apy asakṛc cet tato 'dhikatvāt sādhāraṇair api vedyam/ yathā-- "khaga kalānidhir eṣa vijṛmbhate"/ "iti vadati divāniśaṃ sa dhanyaḥ"/ pañcamānāṃ madhuratvena svavargyānantaryaṃ na tathā/ yathā-- "tanute tanutāṃ tanau"/ svānantaryaṃ tv aśravyam eva/ yathā-- "mama mahatī manasi vyathāvirāsīt"/ etāni cāśravyatvāni guruvyavāyenāpodyante/ "saṃjāyatāṃ kathaṃkāraṃ kāke kekākalasvanaḥ"/
yathā vā--
"yathā yathā tāmarasāyatekṣaṇā mayā sarāgaṃ nitarāṃ niṣevitā/
tathā tathā tattvakatheva sarvato vikṛṣya mām ekarasaṃ cakāra sā//"
idaṃ tu dīrghavyavāye/ saṃyogaparavyavāye tu--
sadā jayānuṣaṅgāṇām aṅgānāṃ saṃgarasthalam/
raṅgāṅgāṇam ivābhāti tattatturagatāṇḍavaiḥ//
body.translated_text:
Because cognition is grounded in meaning through the relation of objecthood, [some qualities are] qualities of meaning (<s>arthaguṇa</s>).
The first is illustrated thus — in 'tanayamainākagaveṣaṇa' and so forth; the second, they say, is found practically everywhere. But others, among these qualities, consider some as already accounted for by the three previously mentioned qualities, by the absence of faults to be described, and by figures of speech; some they regard as merely varieties of expression, and some even as faults — and to that extent they do not accept them. Thus: <s>śleṣa</s> (compactness), <s>udāratā</s> (nobility), <s>prasāda</s> (lucidity), and <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) are subsumed under the compositional structure that manifests <s>ojas</s> (vigor). And one should not object that while the subsumption of <s>śleṣa</s> and <s>udāratā</s>, which are entirely of the nature of tight composition, under the structure manifesting <s>ojas</s> may be granted, where is the subsumption for <s>prasāda</s> and <s>samādhi</s>, which are of the nature of tight and loose [composition respectively] — since even if partially subsumed under that which manifests <s>ojas</s>, where is the subsumption of the other part? — because it is easy to say: under that which manifests <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness), or under that which manifests <s>prasāda</s>. And the <s>mādhurya</s> of others is simply what manifests the <s>mādhurya</s> accepted by us. Thus everywhere the use of the word denoting the suggested for the suggestor is figurative. But <s>samatā</s> (evenness) is always inappropriate, since variation of style within a single verse is desirable according to whether the subject being conveyed is lofty or not.
As illustrated—
"If you are truly a connoisseur of composition, of words whose exuberance surpasses the sweetness of the honey of ripe grapes melting in extreme refinement,
then, friend, recite your poetry with ease before the likes of us;
if not, do not bring it out from your heart, as if it were a sin committed by yourself!"
Here, the style in the first half and the third quarter, which convey extraordinary composition, is not the same as in the fourth quarter, which conveys wretched poetry — thus unevenness itself is the quality. Since vulgarity (<s>grāmyatva</s>) and harshness (<s>kaṣṭatva</s>) are rejected, charm (<s>kānti</s>) and delicacy (<s>saukumārya</s>) are already accounted for. And clarity of meaning is [achieved] through <s>prasāda</s>.
Among the qualities of meaning as well — <s>śleṣa</s>, and the first four varieties of <s>ojas</s>, being merely forms of variety of expression, do not merit subsumption among the qualities; otherwise, because of the distinctiveness of semantic variety in every verse, there would be a proliferation of quality-types. <s>Prasāda</s> whose nature is absence of superfluous words; <s>mādhurya</s> whose body is variety of expression; <s>saukumārya</s> whose body is absence of harshness; <s>udāratā</s> whose form is absence of vulgarity; <s>samatā</s> characterized by absence of unevenness; the fifth type of <s>ojas</s> whose nature is purposefulness; <s>arthavyakti</s> (clarity of meaning) whose nature is natural perspicuity; and <s>kānti</s> (charm) whose form is manifest aesthetic savor — all these are already accounted for by the rejection of faults such as superfluous words, lack of refinement, inauspiciousness, indecency, vulgarity, broken sequence, and unsupported meaning, and by the acceptance of the figure of speech <s>svabhāvokti</s> (natural description), <s>rasadhvani</s>, and <s>rasavadalaṃkāra</s>. And <s>samādhi</s>, being a quality of the poet, is a cause of poetry, not a quality [of the poem]; for otherwise <s>pratibhā</s> (genius) too would have to be accepted as a quality of poetry. Therefore there are only three qualities — thus say <s>Mammaṭa Bhaṭṭa</s> and others.
Regarding these: a composition constructed with the first and third consonants of the [five] classes excluding the <s>ṭa</s>-class, with sibilants and semivowels, adorned with <s>anusvāra</s>-homorganic consonants and pure nasals placed in proximity, untouched by consonant clusters and other [combinations] prohibited both generally and specifically as will be described — being either without meter or of soft meter in its sequential arrangement — is the manifester of <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness). The second and fourth class-consonants are neither favorable nor unfavorable to this quality when placed at a distance; but in proximity they can be unfavorable, provided there is no <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration) dependent on them. Others, however, say that all five consonants of each class equally manifest <s>mādhurya</s>.
Illustration—
"May my heart long contemplate, for [its] peace, that radiance which surpasses the beauty of the <s>tamāla</s> tree, which has made the luster of fresh rain-clouds its servant,
and which has been kissed by the eyes of <s>Naicikī</s> (Sītā)."
Or thus—
"With dense drops of perspiration adorning her cheeks, charming with her inner smile and languid gaze,
some delightful state of the doe-eyed one sprouts joy in my mind through [mere] remembrance."
In the first verse, because the suggested <s>dhyāna</s>-eagerness toward the Lord or devotion directed at the Lord, embellished by the figure of hyperbole, ultimately culminates in <s>śānta</s> [rasa] alone, this composition manifests the <s>mādhurya</s> pertaining to that. In the second, it pertains to <s>śṛṅgāra</s> supported by memory. A composition constructed in proximity with second and fourth class-consonants, <s>ṭa</s>-class consonants, the velar fricative, <s>upadhmānīya</s>, <s>visarga</s>, and abundant <s>sa</s>-sounds, embraced in proximity by short vowels following clusters formed with <s>jha</s>, <s>ra</s>, or either, and of long-metered nature — [such composition] is [the manifester] of <s>ojas</s> (vigor). First and third class-consonants falling within this are neither favorable nor unfavorable to this quality, provided they do not form clusters;
but when forming clusters, they are indeed favorable. Similarly with <s>anusvāra</s>-homorganic consonants. As in 'ayaṃ patatu nirdayaṃ dalitadṛpta-' and so forth, previously cited. A composition that delivers the sentence-meaning as readily as a fruit in the palm — heard the moment [it is uttered] — is [the manifester] of <s>prasāda</s> (lucidity). And this is a quality common to all [styles]. Examples here — nearly all verses are my own. Nevertheless, as follows—
"The mind-born god (<s>Manasija</s>) with eyes closed in thought, the companions bereft of luster,
the lord of her life troubled by love — enough, let the whole tale rest;
I tell you this: if you consider my words beneficial,
O naive one, do not sulk — this face [of yours], the lord of the full-moon night will conquer!"
Here, <s>prasāda</s>-manifesting quality pervades the whole; but in different portions there is also the manifestation of <s>mādhurya</s> and <s>ojas</s> — since the portion ending with '<s>manasija</s>' and the portion 'mā kuru' etc. cause the manifestation of <s>mādhurya</s>; and the portion beginning 'sakhya' etc. indicates <s>ojas</s>. If one objects: 'For the manifestation of <s>mādhurya</s>, which is the shelter of <s>śṛṅgāra</s>, the composition is indeed favorable; but what occasion is there for <s>ojas</s>, such that letter-arrangement favorable to it [should be used]?' —
Because the friend (<s>sakhī</s>), who has made numerous efforts to pacify the heroine's sulking, is instructing her in what is beneficial, and since the friend's slight anger needs to be suggested, such arrangement serves its purpose. In brief: even when there is no intention of the vigorous <s>rasa</s> or a <s>bhāva</s> (emotion) such as indignation, when the speaker is known to be angry, or when the subject is cruel, or in a narrative genre (<s>ākhyāyikā</s>) and the like — harsh consonant-arrangement is desirable.
Or as follows—
"The teaching You gave me, O Lord, in pure speech sweet as nectar —
I do not touch it even in my dream, shameless as I am, covered by ego;
yet You, who still hold me, laden with hundreds of sins, among Your own —
there is no ocean of compassion greater than You, O Lord of the <s>Yadus</s>; no one more intoxicated than me!"
Here <s>prasāda</s> is not co-located with any other quality. Now, to familiarize [the reader] with composition capable of manifesting each quality, something to be avoided both generally and specifically is examined — The immediate succession of identical consonants, when occurring once within a single word, is somewhat unpleasant to hear. As in: 'kakubhasurabhiḥ,' 'vitatagātraḥ,' 'palalam ivābhāti,' and so forth. If occurring more than once, it is worse. As in: 'vitatatarastarur eṣa bhāti bhūmau.' Similarly when occurring across different words. As in: 'śuka karoṣi kathaṃ vijane rucim' and so forth. When occurring more than once across different words, it is even worse. As in: 'pika kakubho mukharīkuru prakāmam.' Similarly, the immediate succession of consonants of the same class, when occurring once within a single word, is somewhat unpleasant. As in: 'vitathas te manorathaḥ.' If more than once, it is worse. As in: 'vitathataraṃ vacanaṃ tava pratīmaḥ.' Similarly across different words. As in: 'atha tasya vacaḥ śrutvā' and so forth. When occurring more than once across different words, it is even worse: 'atha tathā kuru yena sukhaṃ labhe.' And this [unpleasantness] applies to the succession of the first and second, or the third and fourth consonants of a class. But the succession of first and third, or second and third, is not so unpleasant — only slightly, perceptible to connoisseurs of composition alone. But even this, if repeated, being greater [in unpleasantness], becomes perceptible to ordinary people as well. As in: 'khaga kalānidhir eṣa vijṛmbhate'; 'iti vadati divāniśaṃ sa dhanyaḥ.' The fifth (nasal) consonants, being sweet, their succession with consonants of their own class is not so [unpleasant]. As in: 'tanute tanutāṃ tanau.' But their self-succession is indeed unpleasant to hear. As in: 'mama mahatī manasi vyathāvirāsīt.' And these unpleasantnesses are remedied by the intervention of a heavy [syllable]. 'saṃjāyatāṃ kathaṃkāraṃ kāke kekākalasvanaḥ.'
Or thus—
"The more the lotus-eyed one was passionately attended upon by me,
the more she, like a discourse on truth, drew me from all sides and made me single-pointed in <s>rasa</s>."
This is with the intervention of a long [syllable]. And with the intervention of a consonant-cluster-following [syllable]—
"The battlefield of those whose limbs are always accompanied by victory
shines like the arena of dancers, with the prancing of their various horses."

body.text:
idaṃ tu bodhyam-- gurur yayor vyavadhāyakas tayor eva varṇayor ānantaryakṛtam aśravyatvam apavadati/ tenātra thakāratakārānantaryakṛtadoṣāpavāde 'pi
takārathakārānantaryakṛtam aśravyatvam anapoditam eva/ evaṃ tryādīnāṃ saṃyogo 'pi prāyeṇāśravyaḥ/ "rāṣṭre tavoṣṭryaḥ paritaś caranti" ity evamādayaḥ śṛutikāṭavabhedā anye 'py anubhavānusāreṇa bodhyāḥ/ atha dīrghānantaryaṃ saṃyogasya bhinnapadagatasya sakṛd apy aśravyam, asakṛt tu sutarām/
"hariṇīprekṣaṇā yatra gṛhiṇī na vilokyate/
sevitaṃ sarvasaṃpadbhir api tadbhavanaṃ vanam//"
ekapadagatasya tu tathā nāśravyatvam/ yathā-- "jāgratā vicitaḥ panthāḥ śātravāṇāṃ vṛthodyamaḥ"/ parasavarṇakṛtasya tu saṃyogasya sarvathā dīrghād
bhinnapadagatatvābhāvān madhuratvāc cānantaryaṃ na manāg apy aśravyam/ yathā-- "tāṃtamālatarukānti-" ity ādipadye/ atra tām ity atra nīm ity atra ca parasavarṇasya pūrvapadabhaktatayā na saṃyogo bhinnapadagataḥ/ pratyekaṃ saṃyogasaṃjñeti pakṣe 'pi bhinnapadagataḥ saṃyogo na dīrghād avyavahitaparaḥ/ navāmbudety atra tv ekādeśasya padadvayabhaktatayā dīrghād bhinnapadagatatve saty avyavahitottaratvaṃ yady api parasavarṇakṛtasaṃyogasya bhavati tathāpy atra bhinnapadagatatvam ekapadagatabhinnatvaṃ vivakṣitam ity adoṣaḥ/ asakṛt tu sutarām/ yathā-- "eṣāṃ priyā me kva gatā trapākulā"/ idaṃ cāśravyatvaṃ kāvyasya paṅgutvam iva pratīyate/
atha svecchayā saṃdhyakaraṇaṃ sakṛd apy aśravyam/ yathā-- "ramyāṇi indumukhi te kilakiñcitāni/ pragṛhyatāprayuktaṃ tv asakṛd eva/ aho amī indumukhīvilāsāḥ"/ evam eva ca ya-va-lopaprayuktam "apara iṣavaete kāminīnāṃ dṛgantāḥ"/
kathaṃ tarhi--
"bhujagāhitaprakṛtayo gāruḍamantrā ivāvanīramaṇa/
tārā iva turagā iva sukhalīnā mantriṇo bhavataḥ//"
iti bhavadīyaṃ kāvyam iti ced akṛtvaiva yalopaṃ
pāṭhān na doṣaḥ/
evaṃ rorutvasya hali lopasya yaṇguṇavṛddhisavarṇadīrghapūrvarūpādīnāṃ naikaṭyena bāhulyam aśravyatāhetuḥ/ evam ime sarve 'py aśravyabhedāḥ kāvyasāmānye varjanīyāḥ/
atha viśeṣato varjanīyāḥ/ tatra madhuraraseṣu ye viśeṣato varjanīyā anupadaṃ vakṣyante ta evaujasviṣv anukūlāḥ, ye cānukūlatayoktās te pratikūlā iti sāmānyato nirṇayaḥ/ madhuraraseṣu dīrghasamāsaṃ jhayghaṭitasaṃyogaparahrasvasya visarjanīyādeśasakārajihvāmūlīyopadhmānīyānāṃ ṭavargajhayāṃ rephahakārānyataraghaṭitasaṃyogasya halāṃ la-ma-na-bhinnānāṃ svātmanā saṃyogasya jhaydvayaghaṭitasaṃyogasya cāsakṛtprayogaṃ naikaṭyena varjayet/ savarṇajhaydvayaghaṭitasaṃyogasya śarbhinnamahāprāṇaghaṭitasaṃyogasya sakṛd apīti saṃkṣepaḥ/
dīrghasamāso yathā--
"lolālakāvalivalannayanāravinda-līlāvaśaṃvaditalokavilocanāyāḥ/
sāyāhani praṇayino bhavanaṃ vrajantyāś ceto na kasya harate gatir aṅganāyāḥ//"
jhayghaṭitasaṃyogaparahrasvānāṃ prācuryaṃ naikaṭyena yathā--
"hīrasphuradradanaśubhrimaśobhi kiṃ ca sāndrāmṛtaṃ vadanam eṇavilocanāyāḥ/
vedhā vidhāya punar uktam ivendubimbaṃ dūrīkaroti na kathaṃ viduṣāṃ vareṇyaḥ//"
atra bhriśabdaparyantaṃ śṛṅgārānanuguṇam/ śiṣṭaṃ tu ramaṇīyam/ uttarārdhe kakāratakārarūpajhaydvayasaṃyogasya sattve 'pi prācuryābhāvān na doṣaḥ/ yadi tu "dantāṃśukāntam aravindaramāpahāri
sāndrāmṛtam, ity ādi kriyate tadā sarvam eva ramaṇīyam/
visargaprācuryaṃ yathā--
sānurāgās sānukampāś caturāś śītalāḥ/
haranti hṛdayaṃ hanta kāntāyās svāntavṛttayaḥ//
body.translated_text:
But this should be understood—a heavy syllable that intervenes between two sounds removes the cacophony caused by their immediate proximity. Therefore, even though the fault caused by the proximity of <s>thakāra</s> and <s>takāra</s> is removed here, the cacophony caused by the proximity of <s>takāra</s> and <s>thakāra</s> remains unresolved. Similarly, consonant clusters beginning with <s>tr</s> and the like are also generally unpleasant to hear. Verses like "<s>rāṣṭre tavoṣṭryaḥ paritaś caranti</s>" and other such varieties of harshness to the ear should be understood through experience. Now, a consonant cluster belonging to different words in immediate proximity to a long vowel is unpleasant to hear even once, and all the more so when repeated.
"Where a wife with the eyes of a deer is not seen, that house, even though served by all prosperity, is a wilderness."
But when occurring within a single word, it is not similarly unpleasant. For example: "<s>jāgratā vicitaḥ panthāḥ śātravāṇāṃ vṛthodyamaḥ</s>." However, a consonant cluster formed by homogeneous sounds is never in the least unpleasant in proximity to a long vowel, due to the absence of belonging to different words and due to its sweetness. For example, in the verse beginning "<s>tāṃtamālatarukānti</s>-". Here, in <s>tām</s> and in <s>nīm</s>, because the homogeneous sound belongs to the preceding word, the cluster does not span different words. Even in the view that each constitutes a separate cluster, the cluster spanning different words does not immediately follow a long vowel. In the case of <s>navāmbud</s>, although the single substitute belongs to both words, making the cluster span different words while immediately following a long vowel—even though this applies to a cluster formed by homogeneous sounds—the term 'spanning different words' here is intended to mean spanning truly different words, not parts of a compound, so there is no fault. But when repeated, all the more so. For example: "<s>eṣāṃ priyā me kva gatā trapākulā</s>." This cacophony is perceived as a kind of lameness in poetry.
Now, the optional making of <s>sandhi</s> (euphonic combination) is unpleasant even once. For example: "<s>ramyāṇi indumukhi te kilakiñcitāni</s>." But the non-application of <s>pragṛhya</s> rules applies when repeated. "<s>aho amī indumukhīvilāsāḥ</s>." Similarly, cases employing the elision of <s>ya</s> and <s>va</s>: "<s>apara iṣavaete kāminīnāṃ dṛgantāḥ</s>."
But then how about:
"O lord of the earth, your ministers are absorbed in ease, like <s>Gāruḍa</s> mantras whose nature has been seized by serpents, like stars, like horses."
—this being your own poetry? The answer is: since it is read without making the elision of <s>ya</s>, there is no fault.
Thus, the abundance in proximity of <s>roruttva</s>, the elision before <s>hal</s> sounds, <s>yaṇ</s>, <s>guṇa</s>, <s>vṛddhi</s>, <s>savarṇadīrgha</s>, <s>pūrvarūpa</s>, and similar operations causes cacophony. Thus all these varieties of cacophony are to be avoided in poetry in general.
Now, those to be avoided in particular cases. Among these, those specifically to be avoided in sweet <s>rasas</s> will be stated presently one by one; those very ones are favorable in vigorous compositions, and those stated as favorable are unfavorable—this is the general principle. In sweet <s>rasas</s>, one should avoid, when occurring in proximity and in abundance: long compounds, consonant clusters formed with <s>jhay</s> sounds followed by short vowels, the <s>visarjanīya</s> substitutes <s>sakāra</s>, <s>jihvāmūlīya</s>, and <s>upadhmānīya</s>, the <s>ṭa</s>-class <s>jhay</s> sounds, consonant clusters formed with <s>repha</s> or <s>hakāra</s> or either of them, geminate consonant clusters of <s>hal</s> sounds other than <s>la</s>, <s>ma</s>, and <s>na</s>, and consonant clusters formed by two <s>jhay</s> sounds. Even a single occurrence should be avoided for: geminate clusters formed by homogeneous <s>jhay</s> sounds and clusters formed by aspirated sounds other than <s>śar</s> sounds. This is the summary.
A long compound, for example:
"At evening, whose gait does not steal the heart—she of the curly locks swaying, with lotus-eyes, whose playful movements captivate all the world's eyes, the beloved woman going to her lover's house?"
Abundance in proximity of short vowels following <s>jhay</s>-formed consonant clusters, for example:
"Is not the face of the doe-eyed woman, resplendent with the luster of sparkling diamond-like teeth and filled with dense nectar, reason enough for the Creator, having made it, to say 'this is like the moon' and yet not surpass the excellence of the learned?"
Here, up to the word <s>bhri</s>, it is unsuitable for <s>śṛṅgāra</s>. The rest, however, is charming. In the second half, though a cluster of the <s>jhay</s> pair <s>ka</s> and <s>ta</s> exists, there is no fault due to the absence of abundance. But if one composes "<s>dantāṃśukāntam aravindaramāpahāri sāndrāmṛtam</s>" and so on, then everything would be charming.
Abundance of <s>visarga</s>, for example:
"Full of passion, full of compassion, clever and cool—alas, the inner dispositions of the beloved steal the heart!"

body.text:
atra śakāradvayasaṃyogāntaṃ pūrvārdhaṃ mādhuryānanuguṇam/
jihvāmūlīprācuryaṃ yathā--
"kalitakuliśaghātāẖ ke 'pi khelanti vātāḥ kuśalam iha kathaṃ vā jāyatāṃ jīvite me/
ayam api bata guñjannāli mākandamaulau culukayati madīyāṃ cetanāṃ cañcarīkaḥ//"
atra dvitīyajihvāmūlīyaparyantam ananuguṇaṃ mādhuryasya/ yadi ca "kathaya katham ivāśā jāyatāṃ jīvite me malayabhujagavāntā vānti vātāḥ kṛtāntāḥ" iti vidhīyate, tathā nāyaṃ doṣaḥ/
upadhmānīyaprācuryaṃ yathā--
"alakāḫ phaṇiśāvatulyaśīlā nayanāntāḫ paripuṅkhiteṣu līlāḥ/
capalopamitā khalu svayaṃ yā bata loke sukhasādhanaṃ kathaṃ sā//"
atra dvāv upadhmānīyāv eva na śāntānuguṇau/
ṭavargajhayāṃ prācuryaṃ yathā--
"vacane tava yatra mādhurī sā hṛdi pūrṇā karuṇā ca komale 'bhūt/
adhunā hariṇākṣi hā kathaṃ vā kaṭutā tatra kaṭhoratāvirāsīt//"
adhunā sakhi tatra hā kathaṃ vā gatir anyaiva vilokyate guṇānām" iti tv anuguṇam/
rephaghaṭitasaṃyogasyāsakṛt prayogo yathā--
tulām anālokya nijām akharvaṃ gaurāṅgi garvaṃ na kadāpi kuryāḥ/
lasanti nānāphalabhāravatyo latāḥ kiyatyo gahanāntareṣu//
body.translated_text:
Here the first half, ending with the cluster of two <s>śa</s> sounds, is unsuitable for sweetness.
Abundance of <s>jihvāmūlīya</s>, for example:
"Some winds play, striking with thunderbolt blows! How can there be well-being in my life? And alas, this bee buzzing on the crown of the mango tree sips away my consciousness!"
Here, up to the second <s>jihvāmūlīya</s>, it is unsuitable for sweetness. But if one composes "tell me, how can hope arise in my life? The winds blow, vomited by the serpent of the <s>Malaya</s> mountain, they are messengers of death"—then this fault does not arise.
Abundance of <s>upadhmānīya</s>, for example:
"Her locks are like young serpents in behavior, the sidelong glances of her eyes are arrows in their playfulness—she who is herself compared to lightning, alas, how can she be a means of happiness in this world?"
Here, the two <s>upadhmānīyas</s> alone are unsuitable for the <s>śānta</s> rasa.
Abundance of <s>ṭa</s>-class <s>jhay</s> sounds, for example:
"Where there was sweetness in your speech and fullness of compassion in your tender heart, O doe-eyed one, alas, how now has harshness and cruelty appeared there?"
But "O friend, alas, how now is a different course of qualities seen there" would be suitable.
Repeated use of clusters formed with <s>repha</s>, for example:
"O fair-limbed one, without looking at your own not-inconsiderable equal, never be proud! How many creepers laden with various fruits flourish in the depths of the forest!"

body.text:
yadi tu "tulām anālokya mahītale 'smin" iti nirmīyate tathā sādhu/
halāṃ la-ma-na-bhinnānāṃsvātmanā saṃyogasyāsakṛt prayogo yathā-- "vigaṇayya me nikāyyaṃ tām anuyāto 'si naiva tannyāyyam/" la-ma-nānāṃ svātmanā saṃyogas tu na tathā pāruṣyam āvahati/yathā--
"iyam ullasitā mukhasya śobhā pariphullaṃ nayanāmbujadvayaṃ te/
jaladālim ayaṃ jagadvitanvan kalitaḥ kvāpi kim āli nīlameghaḥ//"
jhaydvayaghaṭitasaṃyogasya yathā--
"ā sāyaṃ salilabhare savitāram upāsya sādaraṃ tapasā/
adhunābjena manāk tava mānini tulanā mukhasyāptā//"
atra dvitīyārdham aramyam/ "sarasijakulena saṃprati bhāmini te mukhatulādhigatā" iti tu sādhu/
savarṇa jhaydvayaghaṭitasaṃyogasya sakṛt prayogo yathā--
ayi mandasmitamadhuraṃ vadanaṃ tanvaṅgi yadi manāk kuruṣe/
adhunaiva kalaya śamitaṃ rākāramaṇasya hanta sāmrājyam//
body.translated_text:
But if one composes "<s>tulām anālokya mahītale 'smin</s>" (without looking at an equal on this earth), then it would be good.
Repeated use of geminate clusters of <s>hal</s> sounds other than <s>la</s>, <s>ma</s>, and <s>na</s>, for example: "<s>vigaṇayya me nikāyyaṃ tām anuyāto 'si naiva tannyāyyam</s>" (Having disregarded me and despised me, you have followed her—that is not at all proper). But geminate clusters of <s>la</s>, <s>ma</s>, and <s>na</s> do not produce such harshness. For example:
"This radiance of your face has blossomed forth, your pair of lotus-eyes are in full bloom—O friend, has the dark cloud, spreading its beauty over the world, somehow been captured by a water-lily cluster?"
A cluster formed by two <s>jhay</s> sounds, for example:
"Having worshiped the sun with devotion and austerity until evening in the fullness of water, O proud one, now at last with a lotus has a slight comparison to your face been achieved."
Here the second half is uncharming. But "O beautiful one, now with a cluster of lotuses has a comparison to your face been attained" would be good.
A single use of a geminate cluster formed by homogeneous <s>jhay</s> sounds, for example:
O slender-limbed one, if you but make your face sweet with a gentle smile, know that the sovereignty of the beloved of <s>Rākā</s> (the full moon) is now at once quelled!

body.text:
nanv atra
kakāradvayasaṃyogasya halghaṭitasvātmasaṃyogatvenaiva niṣedhāt ka-khasaṃyogasya mahāprāṇasaṃyoganiṣedhaviṣayatvāt tṛtīyasaṃyogasya cāsaṃbhavāt savarṇajhaydvayasaṃyoganiṣedho niravakāśa iti cet, na/ sakṛt prayogaviṣayatvenāsya pārthakyāt/ ānyathā "manāk kuruṣe" iti nirdoṣaṃ syāt/
mahāprāṇaghaṭitasaṃyogo yathā--
"ayi mṛgamadabinduṃ cedbhāle bāle samātanuṣe/"
uttarārdhaṃ tu prācīnam eva/
evaṃ tvapratyayaṃ, yaṅantāni, yaṅalugantāny anyāni ca śābdikapriyāṇy api madhurarase na prayuñjīta/ evaṃ vyaṅgyacarvaṇātiriktayojanāviśeṣāpekṣānāpātato 'dhikacamatkāriṇo 'nuprāsanicayān yamakādīṃś ca saṃbhavato 'pi kavir na nibadhnīyāt/ yato hi te rasacarvaṇāyām anantarbhavantaḥ sahṛdayahṛdayaṃ svābhimukhaṃ vidadhānā rasaparāṅmukhaṃ vidadhīran/vipralambhe tu sutarām/ yato madhuratamatvenāsya nirmalasitānirmitapānakarasasyeva tanīyān api svātantryam āvahan padārthaḥ sahṛdayahṛdayāruṃtudatayāna sarvathaiva sāmānādhikaraṇyam arhati/
yad āhuḥ--
"dhvanyātmabhūte śṛṅgāre yamakādinibandhanam/
śaktāv api pramāditvaṃ vipralambhe viśeṣataḥ//"
ye tu punar akliṣṭatayānunnataskandhatayā ca na pṛthag bhāvanām apekṣante, kiṃ tu rasacarvaṇāyām eva susukhaṃ gocarīkartuṃ śakyāḥ, na teṣām anuprāsādīnāṃ tyāgo yuktaḥ/
yathā--
"kastūrikātilakam
āli vidhāya sāyaṃ smerānanā sapadi śīlaya saudhamaulim/
prauḍhiṃ bhajantu kumudāni mudām udārām ullāsayantu parito harito mukhāni//"
ittham ete prasaṅgato madhurarasābhivyañjikāyāṃ racanāyāṃ saṃkṣepeṇa nirūpitā doṣāḥ/
"ebhir viśeṣaviṣayaiḥ sāmānyair api ca dūṣaṇai rahitā/
mādhuryabhārabhaṅgurasundarapadavarṇavinyāsā//
body.translated_text: Now, if one objects that here, the conjunct of two <s>ka</s>-letters is already prohibited as being a conjunct with its own kind composed of a stop (<s>hal</s>), and the conjunct <s>ka-kha</s> falls under the prohibition of conjuncts with aspirates (<s>mahāprāṇa</s>), and a third conjunct is impossible, so the prohibition of conjuncts of two homogeneous stops (<s>savarṇajhaydvaya</s>) would have no scope—[we reply:] No. Because this has its separate scope as applying to single occurrences [across word boundaries]. Otherwise, "<s>manāk kuruṣe</s>" would be faultless. An example of a conjunct formed with an aspirate: "O young girl, if you apply a dot of musk on your forehead." The latter half, however, is the same as previously [cited]. Thus, one should not employ in the sweet <s>rasa</s> (sentiment): the <s>tva</s>-suffix, <s>yaṅ</s>-ending [intensive] forms, <s>yaṅluk</s>-ending forms, and other forms dear to grammarians. Likewise, even when possible, the poet should not compose accumulations of <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration), <s>yamaka</s> (paronomastic repetition), and the like, which demand a special effort of construction beyond the savoring of the suggested meaning (<s>vyaṅgya</s>) and do not at first glance produce greater <s>camatkāra</s> (aesthetic wonder). For these, not being subsumed within the savoring of <s>rasa</s>, while directing the <s>sahṛdaya</s>'s (connoisseur's) heart toward themselves, would turn it away from <s>rasa</s>—especially so in <s>vipralambha</s> (love-in-separation). Because, this [<s>rasa</s>] being of the utmost sweetness, like a drink made of pure white sugar, even the slightest element that independently asserts itself pierces the <s>sahṛdaya</s>'s heart and therefore does not in every case deserve co-predication [with the <s>rasa</s>]. As they say: "Even for one who is capable, the composition of <s>yamaka</s> and the like in <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment), which is essentially <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion), is an act of carelessness—especially in <s>vipralambha</s>." However, those [alliterations and the like] which, being effortless and flowing with unforced grace, do not require separate contemplation but can be very easily brought within the purview of <s>rasa</s>-savoring—it is not proper to abandon such <s>anuprāsa</s> and the like. For example: "O friend, having applied a <s>kastūrikā</s> (musk) <s>tilaka</s> on [your forehead] in the evening, with a smiling face, quickly ascend to the top of the palace. Let the <s>kumuda</s> (night-lotuses) attain their full bloom, let the faces of the directions everywhere burst into laughter with abundant joy." Thus, these faults in the composition that manifests the sweet <s>rasa</s> have been briefly examined in this connection. "Free from these specific faults as well as from general defects, with a beautiful arrangement of words and phonemes bending under the weight of <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness),

body.text:
vyutpattim udgirantī nirmātur yā prasādayutā/
tāṃ vibudhā vaidarbhīṃ vadanti vṛttiṃ gṛhītaparipākām//
body.translated_text: pouring forth learning, endowed with <s>prasāda</s> (lucidity), and having attained full maturity (<s>paripāka</s>)—the learned call that the <s>Vaidarbhī</s> <s>vṛtti</s> (style) produced by [such] a creator."

body.text:
asyām udāhṛtāny eva kiyanty api padyāni/
yathā vā--
"āyātaiva niśā niśāpatikaraiḥ kīrṇaṃ diśām antaraṃ
bhāminyo bhavaneṣu bhūṣaṇagaṇair ullāsayanti śriyam/
vāme mānam apākaroṣi na manāg adyāpi roṣeṇa te
hā hā bālamṛṇālato 'py atitamāṃ tanvī tanus tāmyati//"
asyāś ca rīter nirmāṇe kavinā nitarām avahitena bhāvyam/ anyathā tu paripākabhaṅgaḥ syāt/ yathāmarukakavipadye--
"śūnyaṃ vāsagṛhaṃ vilokya śayanād utthāya kiṃcicchanair
nidrāvyājam upāgatasya suciraṃ nirvarṇya patyur mukham/
vistrabdhaṃ paricumbya jātapulakām ālokya gaṇḍasthalīṃ
lajjānamramukhī priyeṇa hasatā bālā ciraṃ cumbitā//"
atrotthāya kiṃcicchanair ity atra savarṇajhaydvayasaṃyogas tatrāpi naikaṭyeneti sutarām aśravyaḥ/ evaṃ
jhayghaṭitasaṃyogaparahrasvasyāpi/ tathā śanair nidrety atra, nirvarṇya patyur mukham ity atra ca rephaghaṭitasaṃyogasya, jhayghaṭitasaṃyogaparahrasvasya ca prācuryam/ vistrabdham ity atra mahāprāṇaghaṭitasya, lajjety atra svātmasavarṇajhaydvayaghaṭitasya, mukhī priyeṇety atra bhinnapadagatadīrghānantarasya saṃyogasya, tathā ktvāpratyayasya pañcakṛtvaḥ, lokateś ca dhātor dviḥ prayogaḥ kaver nirmāṇasāmagrīdāridryaṃ prakāśayati/ ity alaṃ parakīyakāvyavimarśanena/ iti saṃkṣepeṇa nirūpitā rasāḥ/
atha bhāvadhvanir nirūpyate/ atha kiṃ bhāvatvam/ vibhāvānubhāvabhinnatve sati rasavyañjakatvam iti cet, rasakāvyavākye 'tivyāptyāpatteḥ/ arthadvārā śabdasyāpi vyañjakatvāt/ dvārāntaranirapekṣatvena vyañjakatve viśeṣite tv asaṃbhavaḥ prasajyeta/ bhāvasyāpi bhāvanādvāraiva vyañjakatvāt, bhāvanāyām ativyāptyāpatteś ca/ ata eva ca vibhāvānubhāvabhinnatvasyeva śabdabhinnatvasyāpi tadviśeṣaṇatve na nistāraḥ/ pradhānadhvanyamānabhāve rasavyañjakatābhāvād avyāptyāpatteś ca/
na ca tatrāpi prānte raso 'bhivyajyata eveti vācyam, bhāvadhvanivilopaprasaṅgāt/ bhāvacamatkāraprakarṣād bhāvadhvanitvam/ rasas tu tatra vyajyamāno 'py acamatkāritvān na dhvanivyapadeśahetur ity api na śakyaṃ vaditum/ camatkārarahitarasavyaktau mānābhāvāt/ rase hi dharmigrāhakamānenānandāṃśāvinābhāvasya prāg evāvedanāt/
astu vā prādhānyena dhvanyamānasyāpi bhāvasya prānte rasābhivyañjakatvam/ tathāpi deśakālavayovasthādinānāpadārthaghaṭite padyavākyārthe tathāpy ativyāptiḥ/ tasya vibhāvānubhāvabhinnatve sati rasābhivyañjakatvāt/ nāpi rasābhivyañjakacarvaṇāviṣayacittavṛttitvaṃ tattvam/bhāvādicarvaṇāyām atiprasaṅgavāraṇāya carvaṇāviṣayeti cittavṛttiviśeṣaṇam iti vācyam/
kālāgurudravaṃ sā hālāhalavadvijānatī nitarām/
api nīlotpalamālāṃ bālā vyālāvaliṃ kilāmunate//
body.translated_text: Several verses have already been cited as examples of this [style]. Or for example: "Night has already arrived, the spaces between the directions are strewn with the rays of the lord of night (<s>the moon</s>), beautiful women in their mansions enhance their splendor with arrays of ornaments; yet you do not set aside your pride even slightly even now in your anger—alas, alas! Your slender body, more delicate than a young lotus stalk, is wasting away." And in the creation of this <s>rīti</s> (style), the poet must be exceedingly attentive. Otherwise, there would be a breakdown of maturity (<s>paripāka</s>). As in the verse of the poet <s>Amaruka</s>: "Seeing the bedchamber empty, rising from the bed, slowly, for a long time gazing at the face of her husband who had come with the pretense of sleep, kissing him confidently, beholding the surface of his cheek covered with goosebumps, the young woman, with her face bent down in shame, was kissed for a long time by her beloved who was laughing." Here, in "rising slowly" (<s>utthāya kiṃcicchanaiḥ</s>), there is a conjunct of two homogeneous stops (<s>savarṇajhaydvaya</s>), and moreover in close proximity—hence all the more unpleasant to the ear. Likewise with a short vowel following a stop-formed conjunct. Similarly, in "<s>śanair nidrā</s>" and in "gazing at her husband's face" (<s>nirvarṇya patyur mukham</s>), there is an abundance of <s>repha</s>-formed conjuncts and short vowels following stop-formed conjuncts. In "<s>vistrabdham</s>," there is an aspirate-formed [conjunct]; in "<s>lajjā</s>," one formed of a doubled homogeneous stop; in "<s>mukhī priyeṇa</s>," a conjunct immediately following a long vowel across separate words; and the <s>ktvā</s>-suffix occurs five times, and the verb from the root <s>lok</s> (to see) is used twice—[all of which] reveals the poverty of the poet's creative resources. But enough of criticism of others' poetry. Thus the <s>rasas</s> have been briefly examined. Now <s>bhāvadhvani</s> (suggestion of transitory emotions) is to be examined. What, then, is the nature of being a <s>bhāva</s> (transitory emotion)? If one says it is being a suggester of <s>rasa</s> while being different from <s>vibhāva</s> (determinant) and <s>anubhāva</s> (consequent)—then there would be over-extension (<s>ativyāpti</s>) to the word in a sentence of <s>rasa</s>-poetry. Because the word too, through meaning, is a suggester. And if the definition is qualified as suggesting without dependence on any other medium, then impossibility would follow. Because <s>bhāva</s> too suggests only through the medium of <s>bhāvanā</s> (realization), and there would be over-extension to <s>bhāvanā</s> itself. For this very reason, even if "being different from word" is added as a qualifier along with "being different from <s>vibhāva</s> and <s>anubhāva</s>," there is no escape. And because there would be the fault of non-inclusion (<s>avyāpti</s>), since the predominantly suggested <s>bhāva</s> does not [always] suggest <s>rasa</s>. Nor can one say that even there, <s>rasa</s> is ultimately suggested; for that would lead to the dissolution of <s>bhāvadhvani</s> [as a separate category]. Nor can one say that it is <s>bhāvadhvani</s> because of the predominance of the <s>camatkāra</s> of the <s>bhāva</s>, and that the <s>rasa</s>, though suggested there, is not a ground for the designation <s>dhvani</s> because it does not produce <s>camatkāra</s>. Because there is no evidence for the manifestation of <s>rasa</s> devoid of <s>camatkāra</s>. For with regard to <s>rasa</s>, through the means of knowledge that grasps the subject (<s>dharmin</s>), the inseparability of the bliss-aspect has already been established. Or let the <s>bhāva</s> that is predominantly suggested also be, at the end, a manifester of <s>rasa</s>. Even so, there would be over-extension to the verse-sentence-meaning composed of various elements such as place, time, age, condition, and other manifold things. Because that [sentence-meaning], while being different from <s>vibhāva</s> and <s>anubhāva</s>, is a manifester of <s>rasa</s>. Nor is the true nature [of <s>bhāva</s>] being a mental state (<s>cittavṛtti</s>) that is an object of the savoring that manifests <s>rasa</s>. If one says the qualifier "object of savoring" modifies <s>cittavṛtti</s> (mental state) in order to prevent over-extension to the savoring of <s>bhāva</s> and the like— "She, thoroughly knowing the <s>kālāguru</s> (dark aloe) liquid to be like <s>hālāhala</s> (deadly poison), the young girl, it seems, considers a garland of blue lotuses to be a row of serpents."

body.text:
ityatra
hālāhalasadṛśatvaprakārajñāne ativyāpteḥ/ tasya vipralambhānubhāvatvena rasābhivyañjakacarvaṇāviṣayatvāt, cittavṛttitvāc ca/ nāpy akhaṇḍam/ tattve mānābhāvāt/ atrocyate--
body.translated_text: Here, there would be over-extension to the knowledge of the mode of resemblance to <s>hālāhala</s> (poison). Because that, as an <s>anubhāva</s> (consequent) of <s>vipralambha</s> (love-in-separation), is an object of the savoring that manifests <s>rasa</s>, and it is a mental state (<s>cittavṛtti</s>). Nor [can the definition be] indivisible (<s>akhaṇḍa</s>). Because there is no evidence for that as the true nature. Here it is stated:

body.text: vibhāvādivyajyamānaharṣādyanyatamatvaṃ tattvam//
body.translated_text: The true nature [of <s>bhāva</s>] is being any one among joy (<s>harṣa</s>) and the rest, which are manifested by <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants) and the like.

body.text:
yad āhuḥ-- "vyabhicāryañjito bhāvaḥ" iti/
harṣādīnāṃ ca sāmājikagatānām eva sthāyibhāvanyāyenābhivyaktiḥ/ sāpi rasanyāyeneti kecit/ vyaṅgyāntaranyāyenetyapare manyante/ vibhāvānubhāvau cātra vyañjakau/ na tv ekasmin vyābhicāriṇi dhvanyamāne vyabhicāryantaraṃ vyañjakatayāvaśyam apekṣyate, tasyaiva prādhānyāpatteḥ/ vastutas tu prakaraṇādivaśāt prādhānyam anubhavati kasmiṃś cid bhāve tadīyasāmagrīvyaṅgyatvena nāntarīyakatayā tanimānam āvahato vyabhicāryantarasyāṅgatve 'pi na kṣatiḥ/ yathā garvādāv amarṣasya, amarṣādau vā garvasya/ na caivaṃ sati guṇībhūtavyaṅgyatvāpattiḥ/ pṛthagvibhāvānubhāvābhivyaktasyaiva (bhāvasya), guṇībhūtavyaṅgyavyapadeśahetutvāt/ ata eva nāntarīyakasya bhāvasya dhvananaṃ bhavati/ anyathā garvādidhvaner uccheda eva bhavet/
vibhāvas tv atra vyabhicāriṇo nimittakāraṇasāmānyam/ na tu rasasyeva sarvathaivālambanoddīpane apekṣite/ yadi tu kvacit saṃbhavatas tadā na vāryete/
harṣādayas tu--
body.translated_text: As they say: "A <s>bhāva</s> is tinged by the transitory emotions (<s>vyabhicārin</s>)." And the manifestation of joy and the rest belonging to the spectators (<s>sāmājika</s>) follows the same principle as that of the <s>sthāyibhāvas</s> (permanent emotions). Some hold that [their manifestation] also follows the principle of <s>rasa</s>. Others consider that it follows the principle of other types of suggested meaning (<s>vyaṅgyāntara</s>). <s>Vibhāva</s> (determinant) and <s>anubhāva</s> (consequent) are here the suggesters. But when one transitory emotion (<s>vyābhicārin</s>) is being suggested, another transitory emotion is not necessarily required as a suggester, because that [other emotion] would then become predominant. In reality, however, when a certain <s>bhāva</s> attains predominance due to the context and other factors, even though another transitory emotion, by being inevitably suggested as part of that [<s>bhāva</s>'s] apparatus, assumes a subordinate role, there is no harm in its being subsidiary. As, for instance, <s>amarṣa</s> (indignation) in the case of <s>garva</s> (pride) and the rest, or <s>garva</s> in the case of <s>amarṣa</s> and the rest. Nor does this give rise to the unwanted consequence of <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s> (subordinated suggestion). Because only a <s>bhāva</s> manifested through its own separate <s>vibhāvas</s> and <s>anubhāvas</s> is the ground for the designation <s>guṇībhūtavyaṅgya</s>. For this very reason, the suggestion of an inevitably concomitant <s>bhāva</s> constitutes [true] <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion). Otherwise, <s>dhvani</s> of <s>garva</s> and the like would be altogether destroyed. <s>Vibhāva</s> here, however, is the general efficient cause (<s>nimittakāraṇa</s>) of the transitory emotion. It is not the case that <s>ālambana</s> (substrate) and <s>uddīpana</s> (excitant) are required in every respect, as they are for <s>rasa</s>. But if they happen to be present somewhere, they are not precluded. Now, joy and the rest are:

body.text: harṣasmṛtivrīḍāmohadhṛtiśaṅkāglānidainyacintāmadaśramagarvanidrāmativyādhitrāsasuptavibodhāmarṣāvahitthogratonmādamaraṇavitarkaviṣādautsukyāvegajaḍatālasyāsūyāpasmāracapalatāḥ/ pratipakṣakṛtadhikkārādijanmā nirvedaś ceti trayastriṃśad vyabhicāriṇaḥ/ gurudevanṛpaputrādiviṣayā ratiś ceti catustriṃśat/
body.translated_text: <s>Harṣa</s> (joy), <s>smṛti</s> (recollection), <s>vrīḍā</s> (shame), <s>moha</s> (delusion), <s>dhṛti</s> (fortitude), <s>śaṅkā</s> (apprehension), <s>glāni</s> (languor), <s>dainya</s> (despondency), <s>cintā</s> (anxiety), <s>mada</s> (intoxication), <s>śrama</s> (fatigue), <s>garva</s> (pride), <s>nidrā</s> (sleep), <s>āmati</s> (distraction), <s>vyādhi</s> (disease), <s>trāsa</s> (terror), <s>supta</s> (dreaming), <s>vibodha</s> (awakening), <s>amarṣa</s> (indignation), <s>avahitthā</s> (dissimulation), <s>ugratā</s> (ferocity), <s>unmāda</s> (madness), <s>maraṇa</s> (death), <s>vitarka</s> (conjecture), <s>viṣāda</s> (dejection), <s>autsukyā</s> (eagerness), <s>āvega</s> (agitation), <s>jaḍatā</s> (stupor), <s>ālasya</s> (indolence), <s>asūyā</s> (envy), <s>apasmāra</s> (epilepsy), and <s>capalatā</s> (fickleness). And <s>nirveda</s> (world-weariness), born from reproach and the like inflicted by an adversary—thus there are thirty-three <s>vyabhicārins</s> (transitory emotions). Together with <s>rati</s> (love) directed toward elders, gods, kings, sons, and the like, there are thirty-four.

body.text: etena vātsalyākhyaṃ putrādyālambanaṃ rasāntaram iti parāstam/ ucchṛṅkhalatāyā munivacanaparāhatatvāt/
body.translated_text: By this, the view that <s>vātsalya</s> (parental affection), having sons and others as its <s>ālambana</s> (substrate), is a separate <s>rasa</s>, is refuted. Because [such] unrestrained [theorizing] is contradicted by the words of the sages.

body.text: tatra
body.translated_text: Among these,

body.text: iṣṭaprāptyādijanmā sukhaviśeṣo harṣaḥ//
body.translated_text: <s>Harṣa</s> (joy) is a particular kind of pleasure born from the attainment of desired objects and the like.

body.text:
tad uktam--
"devabhartṛgurusvāmiprasādaḥ priyasaṃgamaḥ/
manorathāptir aprāpyamanoharadhanāgamaḥ/
tathotpattiś ca putrāder vibhāvo yatra jāyate/
netravaktraprasādaś ca priyoktiḥ pulakodgamaḥ//
body.translated_text: As it has been said: "The favor of gods, husbands, teachers, and masters; the union with the beloved; the attainment of desires; the acquisition of unattainable and captivating wealth; and the birth of sons and the like—these are the <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants) in which [joy] arises. Serenity of the eyes and face, affectionate words, and the arising of goosebumps [are its <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequents)].

body.text:
aśrusvedādayaś cānubhāvā harṣaṃ tam ādiśet//" iti/
udāharaṇam--
"avadhau divasāvasānakāle bhavanadvāri vilocane dadhānā/
avalokya samāgataṃ tadā mām atha rāmā vikasanmukhī babhūva//"
atrāvadhikāle priyāgamanaṃ vibhāvaḥ/ mukhavikāso 'nubhāvaḥ/
body.translated_text:
"And tears, perspiration, and such are the <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequents); it should indicate that joy (<s>harṣa</s>)." //
An example—
"At the appointed time, at the close of day, placing her eyes at the door of the house, having seen me arrived, the beautiful woman then became radiant-faced." //
Here, the arrival of the beloved at the appointed time is the <s>vibhāva</s> (determinant). The blooming of the face is the <s>anubhāva</s> (consequent).

body.text: saṃskārajanyaṃ jñānaṃ smṛtiḥ//
body.translated_text: Knowledge born from latent impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>) is <s>smṛti</s> (memory). //

body.text:
yathā--
"tanmañju mandahasitaṃ śvasitāni tāni sā vai kalaṅkavidhurā madhurānanaśrīḥ/
adyāpi me hṛdayam unmadayanti hanta sāyaṃtanāmbujasahodaralocanāyāḥ//"
cintāviśeṣo 'tra vibhāvaḥ/ bhrūnnatigātraniścalatvādaya ākṣepagamyā anubhāvāḥ/ yady apy atrāsyā eva smṛteḥ saṃcāriṇyāḥ, nāyikārūpasya vibhāvasya, hantapadagamyasya hṛdayavaikalyarūpānubhāvasya saṃyogād vipralambharasābhivyakte rasadhvanitvaṃ śakyate vaktum tathāpi smṛter evātra puraḥsphūrtikatvāc camatkāritvāc ca taddhvanitvam
uktam/
tadāder buddhisthaprakārāvacchinne śaktir iti naye buddheḥ śakyatāvacchedakānugamakatayā na vācyatāsaṃsparśaḥ/ buddhisthatvaṃ śakyatāvacchedakam iti naye 'pi smṛtitvena smṛter vyaktivedyataiva/ tasyāś cātra vākyavedyatve 'pi padasyaiva kurvadrūpatvāt padadhvaniviṣayatvam/ etena bhāvānāṃ padavyaṅgatve na vaicitryam iti parāstam/ sāyaṃtanāmbujopamānena nayanayor uttarottarādhikanimīlanonmukhatvadhvananadvārā tasyā ānandamagnatāprakāśaḥ/
"darānamatkaṃdharabandham īṣannimīlitasnigdhavilocanābjam/
analpaniḥśvāsabharālasāṅgaṃ smarāmi saṅgaṃ ciram aṅganāyāḥ//"
ity atra smṛtir na bhāvaḥ, svaśabdena nivedanād avyaṅgyatvāt/ nāpi smaraṇālaṃkāraḥ, sādṛśyāmūlakatvāt/ sādṛśyamūlakasyaiva smaraṇasyālaṃkāratvam, anyasya tu vyañjitasya bhāvatvam iti siddhāntāt/ kiṃ tu vibhāva eva sundaratvāt kathaṃcid rasaparyavasāyī/
body.translated_text:
For example—
"That charming gentle smile, those sighs, that beauty of her sweet face free from blemish—even now they intoxicate my heart, alas!—of her whose eyes are sisters of the evening lotus." //
Here, a particular type of contemplation is the <s>vibhāva</s>. Knitting of the brows, bodily stillness, and such, understood by implication, are the <s>anubhāvas</s>. Although here it could be said that this very <s>smṛti</s> (memory), being a <s>sañcārin</s> (transitory emotion), in conjunction with the <s>vibhāva</s> in the form of the <s>nāyikā</s> and the <s>anubhāva</s> in the form of heart-disturbance conveyed by the word 'alas,' constitutes <s>rasa-dhvani</s> (suggested <s>rasa</s>) in the manifestation of <s>vipralambha-rasa</s> (love-in-separation), nevertheless, because <s>smṛti</s> here is what comes to the forefront of consciousness and is what produces <s>camatkāra</s> (aesthetic wonder), it has been stated to be the suggested element (<s>dhvani</s>).
According to the theory that denotative power (<s>śakti</s>) is delimited by the mode present in cognition (<s>buddhisthaprakāra</s>), there is no contact with denotation because cognition follows the delimitor of denotability. Even according to the theory that existence-in-cognition (<s>buddhisthatva</s>) is the delimitor of denotability, <s>smṛti</s> as such is cognizable only through individual instances. And even when it is cognizable through the sentence here, since it is the word alone that has the productive function, it falls within the scope of word-suggestion (<s>padadhvani</s>). By this, the objection that there is no variety when <s>bhāvas</s> are suggested by words is refuted. Through the comparison with the evening lotus, by suggesting the progressive closing tendency of her eyes, her state of being immersed in bliss is revealed.
"With slightly bowed neck, with lotus-eyes tenderly half-closed, with body languid from the weight of deep sighs—I remember long the union with that woman." //
Here, <s>smṛti</s> is not a <s>bhāva</s> (emotional state), because it is communicated by its own word and therefore is not suggested. Nor is it the <s>smaraṇālaṃkāra</s> (figure of remembrance), because it is not based on resemblance. For it is the established doctrine that only remembrance based on resemblance is a figure of speech, while other [remembrance] that is suggested is a <s>bhāva</s>. Rather, it is simply a <s>vibhāva</s> (determinant) which, being beautiful, somehow culminates in <s>rasa</s>.

body.text: strīṇāṃ puruṣamukhāvalokanādeḥ puṃsāṃ ca pratijñābhaṅgaparābhavāder utpanno vaivarṇyādhomukhatvādikāraṇībhūtaś cittavṛttiviśeṣo vrīḍā//
body.translated_text: <s>Vrīḍā</s> (shame/modesty) is a particular mental state arising in women from looking at a man's face and such, and in men from breach of promise, defeat, and the like, which causes pallor, downcast face, and similar [reactions]. //

body.text:
yathā--
"kucakalaśayugāntarmāmakīnaṃ nakhāṅkaṃ
sapulakatanu mandaṃ mandam ālokamānā/
vinihitavadanaṃ māṃ vīkṣya bālā gavākṣe
cakitanatanatāṅgī sadma sadyo viveśa//
body.translated_text:
For example—
"Slowly, slowly gazing at the nail-mark I had made between the pair of pitcher-like breasts, her body bristling with goosebumps, the young woman, seeing me at the lattice window with face cast down, with body suddenly bent in startled modesty, at once entered the house." //

body.text:
atra priyasya darśanaṃ, tena nāyikākartṛkatatkucāntarvartipriyanakhakṣatāvalokanajanyaharṣāvedakatatpulakāder darśanaṃ ca vibhāvaḥ/ sadyaḥ sadanapraveśo
'nubhāvaḥ/
yathā vā--
"niruddhya yāntīṃ tarasā kapotīṃ kūjatkapotasya puro dadāne/
mayi smitārdraṃ vadanāravindaṃ sā mandamandaṃ namayāṃbabhūva//"
pūrvatra trāsa ivātrāpi harṣo leśatayā sannapi vrīḍāyā anuguṇa eva/ priyakartṛkaṃ kapotasyāgre kapotyāḥ samarpaṇaṃ vibhāvaḥ/ vadananamanam anubhāvaḥ/
body.translated_text:
Here, the sight of the beloved and his seeing the horripilation revealing the joy born from her beholding the beloved's nail-scratch on her own breasts—this is the <s>vibhāva</s>. The immediate entering of the house is the <s>anubhāva</s>.
Or, for example—
"As I presented before the cooing pigeon the hen-pigeon that I had caught by force as she was going, she slowly, slowly inclined her lotus-face toward me, moist with a smile." //
In the former [verse], as with <s>trāsa</s> (alarm), so here too, <s>harṣa</s> (joy), though present only in a slight degree, is indeed conducive to <s>vrīḍā</s> (modesty). The offering of the hen-pigeon before the [male] pigeon by the beloved is the <s>vibhāva</s>. The bowing of the face is the <s>anubhāva</s>.

body.text: bhayaviyogādiprayojyā vastutattvānavadhāriṇī cittavṛttir mohaḥ/
body.translated_text: <s>Moha</s> (delusion) is a mental state caused by fear, separation, and the like, characterized by inability to ascertain the true nature of things.

body.text:
"avasthāntaraśabalitā sā tathā" iti tu navyāḥ/
udāharaṇam--
"viraheṇa vikalahṛdayā vilapantī dayita dayiteti/
