And thus the simile of the presiding deity, which suggests the universality [of the beloved's presence] arising from the absence of renunciation, [also nourishes that memory]. This is a <s>bhāvābhāsa</s> (semblance of <s>bhāva</s>) because of being directed toward an inappropriate object and because of not being established in both parties. But if this were the utterance of one who is actually going to marry her, then it would be genuine <s>bhāva-dhvani</s> (suggestion of emotion). //

body.text: atha bhāvaśāntiḥ--
body.translated_text: Now, <s>bhāvaśānti</s> (cessation of emotion)—

body.text: bhāvasya prāguktasvarūpasya śāntir nāśaḥ//
body.translated_text: The cessation, i.e., destruction, of a <s>bhāva</s> whose nature has been previously described. //

body.text:
sa cotpattyavacchinna eva grāhyaḥ, tasyaiva sahṛdayacamatkāritvāt/
udāharaṇam--
"muñcasi nādyāpi ruṣaṃ bhāmini mudirālirudiyāya/
iti tanvyāḥ pativacanair apāyi nayanābjakoṇaśoṇaruciḥ//"
iha tādṛśapriyavacanaśravaṇaṃ vibhāvaḥ/ nayanakoṇagataśoṇarucer nāśaḥ,
tadabhivyaktaḥ prasādo vānubhāvaḥ/ utpattikālāvacchinno roṣanāśo vyaṅgyaḥ/
tathā--
body.translated_text:
And that is to be understood only as delimited by its moment of arising, since only that [moment] produces aesthetic wonder (<s>camatkāra</s>) in the sensitive reader.
An example—
"Do you still not let go of your anger, O beautiful one? The clouds have begun to thunder." Thus, by the husband's words to the slender woman, the redness at the corner of her lotus-eyes departed. //
Here, hearing such words of the beloved is the <s>vibhāva</s>. The disappearance of the redness at the corner of the eyes, or the <s>prasāda</s> (contentment) manifested by it, is the <s>anubhāva</s>. The destruction of anger, delimited to the moment of its arising, is the suggested element.
Likewise—

body.text: bhāvodayo bhāvasyotpattiḥ//
body.translated_text: <s>Bhāvodaya</s> (arising of emotion) is the origination of an emotion. //

body.text:
udāharaṇam--
"vīkṣya vakṣasi vipakṣakāminīhāralakṣma dayitasya bhāminī/
aṃsadeśavalayīkṛtāṃ kṣaṇād ācakarṣa nijabāhuvallarīm//"
atrāpi dayitavakṣogatavipakṣakāminīhāralakṣmadarśanaṃ vibhāvaḥ/ priyāṃsadeśavalayīkṛtanijabāhulatākarṣaṇam anubhāvaḥ/ roṣodayo vyaṅgyaḥ/ yady āpi bhāvaśāntau bhāvāntarodayasya, bhāvodaye vā pūrvaṃ bhāvaśānter āvaśyakatvān nānayor vivikto vyavahārasya viṣayaḥ, tathāpi dvayor ekatra camatkāravirahāt, camatkārādhīnatvāc ca vyavahārasya, asti viṣayavibhāgaḥ/
evam--
body.translated_text:
An example—
"Seeing on the chest of her beloved the mark of a rival woman's necklace, the passionate woman in an instant drew back her own arm-creeper that had been made into a bracelet around his shoulder." //
Here too, seeing the mark of the rival woman's necklace on the beloved's chest is the <s>vibhāva</s>. Drawing back her own arm-vine that had encircled the beloved's shoulder is the <s>anubhāva</s>. The arising of anger (<s>roṣa</s>) is the suggested element. Although in <s>bhāvaśānti</s> (cessation of emotion) the arising of another emotion is necessary, and in <s>bhāvodaya</s> the prior cessation of an emotion is necessary, so that neither has a separate domain of application, nevertheless, since in each case only one of the two produces aesthetic wonder (<s>camatkāra</s>), and since practical usage depends on aesthetic wonder, there is indeed a distinction of domain.
Thus—

body.text: bhāvasaṃdhir anyonyānabhibhūtayor anyonyābhibhavanayogyayoḥ sāmānādhikaraṇyam//
body.translated_text: <s>Bhāvasaṃdhi</s> (junction of emotions) is the co-presence of two [emotions] that are neither overpowered by each other, yet are capable of overpowering each other. //

body.text:
udāharaṇam--
"yauvanodgamanitāntaśaṅkitāḥ śīlaśauryabalakāntilobhitāḥ/
saṃkucanti vikasanti rāghave jānakīnayananīrajaśriyaḥ//"
atra bhagavaddāśarathigatasya lokottarayauvanodgamasya, tādṛśasyaiva śīlaśauryādeś ca darśanaṃ vibhāvaḥ/ nayanagatasaṃkocavikāsāv anubhāvaḥ/ vrīḍautsukyayoḥ saṃdhir vyaṅgyaḥ/
tathā--
bhāvaśabalatvaṃ
bhāvānāṃ bādhyabādhakabhāvam āpannānām udāsīnānāṃ vā vyāmiśraṇam//
body.translated_text:
An example—
"Utterly apprehensive at the onset of youth, yet captivated by his character, valor, strength, and beauty—the splendors of <s>Jānakī's</s> (<s>Sītā's</s>) lotus-eyes contract and expand upon [seeing] <s>Rāghava</s> (<s>Rāma</s>)." //
Here, the sight of the extraordinary onset of youth of the blessed son of <s>Daśaratha</s>, and of his character, valor, and such, is the <s>vibhāva</s>. The contraction and expansion in the eyes is the <s>anubhāva</s>. The junction (<s>saṃdhi</s>) of <s>vrīḍā</s> (modesty) and <s>autsukya</s> (eagerness) is the suggested element.
Likewise—
<s>Bhāvaśabalatva</s> (variegation of emotions) is the intermixture of emotions that have attained the relationship of sublating and sublated, or that are mutually indifferent. //

body.text:
ekacamatkṛtijanakajñānagocaratvam iti yāvat/
udāharaṇam--
"pāpaṃ hanta mayā hatena vihitaṃ kītāpi yady āpitā,
sā mām indumukhī vinā bata vane kiṃ jīvitaṃ dhāsyati/
ālokeya kathaṃ mukhāni kṛtināṃ kiṃ te vadiṣyanti māṃ
rājyaṃ yātu rasātalaṃ punar idaṃ na prāṇituṃ kāmaye//"
atra matyasūyāviṣādasmṛtivitarkavrīḍāśaṅkānirvedānāṃ prāguktasvasvavibhāvajanmanāṃ śabalatā/ yat tu kāvyaprakāśaṭīkākāraiḥ "uttarottareṇa bhāvena pūrvapūrvabhāvopamardaḥ śabalatā" ity abhyadhītaya, tan na/ "paśyet kaścic cala capala re kā tvarāhaṃ kumārī hastālambaṃ vitara hahahā vyutkramaḥ kvāsi yāsi" ity atra śaṅkāsūyādhṛtismṛtiśramadainyamatyautsukyānām upamardaleśaśūnyatve 'pi śabalatāyā rājastutiguṇatvena pañcamollāse mūlakṛtaiva nirūpaṇāt/ svottaraviśeṣaguṇena jāyamānas tu nāśo na vyaṅgyaḥ/ na vopamardapadavācyaḥ, nāpi camatkārī tasmāt/
"nārikelajalakṣīrasitākadalamiśraṇe/
vilakṣaṇo tathāsvādo bhāvānāṃ saṃhatau tathā//"
atredaṃ bodhyam-- ya ete bhāvaśāntyudayasaṃdhiśabalatādhvanaya udāhṛtās te 'pi bhāvadhvanaya eva/ vidyamānatayā carvyamāṇeṣv ivotpattyavacchinnatvavinaśyadavasthatvasaṃdhīyamānatvaparasparasamānādhikaraṇatvaiḥ prakāraiś carvyamāṇeṣu bhāveṣv eva prādhānyasyaucityāt, camatkṛtes tatraiva viśrānteḥ/ yady apy utpattivināśasaṃdhiśabalatānāṃ tatsaṃbandhināṃ bhāvānāṃ ca
samānāyāṃ carvaṇāviṣayatāyāṃ na prādhānyaṃ vinigantuṃ śakyate, tathāpi sthitau bhāveṣu pradhānatāyāḥ kḷptatvāt, bhāvaśāntyādiṣv api teṣv eva śāntipratiyogitvādibhir vyajyamāneṣu tasyāḥ kalpayitum aucityāt/ kiṃ ca yadi bhāvaśāntyādau bhāvo na pradhānam, kiṃ tu tadupasarjanakaśāntyādir evety abhyupeyate tadā vyajyamānabhāveṣv abhihitatatpraśamādiṣu kāvyeṣu bhāvapraśamādidhvanitvaṃ na syāt/
tathā hi--
"uṣasi pratipakṣanāyikāsadanād antikam añcati priye/
sudṛśo nayanābjakoṇayor udiyāya tvarayāruṇadyutiḥ//"
atrotpūrvakeṇaitinā bhāvodayasya vācyatayaiva pratyāyanāt/ (nanu)udayasya vācyatve 'pi bhāvasyāvācyatvād dhanitvaṃ sustham iti cet, pradhānasya vyapadeśānaupayikatve 'pradhānakṛtavyapadeśānupapatteḥ/ asmanmate tūtpatter vācyatve 'py utpattyavacchinnasyāmarṣasya pradhānasyāvācyatvād yukta eva bhāvodayadhvanivyapadeśaḥ/ evaṃ vyajyamānabhāvapratiyogikasya praśamasya vācyatve bhāvaśāntidhvanitvaṃ na syāt/ yathā--
"kṣamāpaṇaikapadayoḥ padayoḥ patati priye/
śemuḥ sarojanayanānayanāruṇakāntayaḥ//"
nanu śabdavācyānāṃ praśamādīnām aruṇakāntyaivānvayāt aruṇakāntipraśamāder eva vācyatvaṃ paryavasitam, na tu tādṛśapraśamādivyaṅgyasya roṣapraśamādeḥ, vyaṅgyavyañjakabhedasyāvaśyakatvāt/ na cāruṇyavyaṅgyaroṣasyaiva vācyībhūtapraśamādyanvaya iti vācyam/ vācyavyaṅgyapratītyor ānupūrvyeṇa siddhatayā vācyānvayabodhavelāyāṃ
vācyaiḥ saha vyaṅgyānvayānupapatteḥ/ anyathā "sudṛśo nayanābjakoṇayoḥ" ity asyānvayo na syāt/ maivam/ evam api--
"nirvāsayantīṃ dhṛtim aṅganānāṃ śobhāṃ harer eṇadṛśo dhayantyāḥ/
cirāparādhasmṛtimāṃsalo 'pi roṣaḥ kṣaṇaprāghuṇiko babhūva//"
ityādāv api bhāvapraśamadhvanitvāpatteḥ, bhāvasya vācyatve 'pi pradhānasya tatpraśamasya vyaṅgyatvāt/ ubhayor apy avācyatvam apekṣitam iti cet, prāguktapadyadvaye śamatvodayatvābhyāṃ śamodayayor vācyatvād anudāharaṇatvāpatteḥ/ iṣṭāpattis tu sahṛdayānām anucitaiva/ tasmād bhāvapraśamādiṣv api prādhānyena bhāvānām eva camatkāritvam, praśamādes tūpasarjanatvam ato na tasya vācyatādoṣaḥ/ idaṃ punar bhāvadhvanibhyo bhāvaśāntyādidhvanīnāṃ camatkāravailakṣaṇye nidānam-- yad ekatra carvaṇāyāṃ bhāveṣu sthityavacchinnāmarṣāditvam, amarṣāditvam eva vā prakāraḥ/ anyatra tu praśamāvasthatvādir apīti/ rasasya tu sthāyimūlakatvāt praśamāder asaṃbhavaḥ, saṃbhave vā na camatkāraḥ, iti na sa vicāryate/
so 'yaṃ nigaditaḥ sarvo 'pi ratyādilakṣaṇo vyaṅgyaprapañcaḥ sphuṭe prakaraṇe jhagiti pratiteṣu vibhāvānubhāvavyabhicāriṣu sahṛdayatamena pramātrā sūkṣmeṇaiva samayeta pratīyata iti hetuhetumatoḥ paurvāparyakramasyālakṣaṇād alakṣyakramo vyapadiśyate/ yatra tu vicāravedyaṃ prakaraṇam, unneyā vā vibhāvādayas tatra sāmagrīvilambādhīnaṃ camatkṛter māntharyam iti saṃlakṣyakramo 'py eṣa bhavati/ yathā-- "talpagatāpi ca sutanuḥ" iti prāg udāhṛte padye "saṃprati" ity etadarthāvagatir vilambena/ na khalu dharmigrāhakamānasiddhaṃ ratyādidhvaner alakṣyakramavyaṅgyatvam/ ata eva lakṣyakramaprasaṅge--
"evaṃvādini devarṣau pārśve pitur adhomukhī/
līlākamalapatrāṇi gaṇayāmāsa pārvatī/"
ity atra
kumārīsvābhāvyād apy adhomukhatvaviśiṣṭasya līlākamalapattragaṇanasyopapattyā manāgvilambena nāradakṛtavivāhādiprasaṅgavijñānottaraṃ vrīḍāyāś camatkaraṇāl lakṣyakramo 'yaṃ dhvaniḥ" iti prāhur ānandavardhanācāryāḥ/ rasabhāvādir artho dhvanyamāna eva, na vācyaḥ/ tathāpi na sarvo 'lakṣyakramasya viṣayaḥ" iti cābhinavaguptapādācāryāḥ/ syād etat, yady ayaṃ rasādiḥ saṃlakṣyakramasya viṣayaḥ syāt/ anuraṇanabhedagaṇanaprastāve "arthaśaktimūlasya dvādaśabhedāḥ" ity abhinavaguptoktiḥ, "tenāyaṃ dvādaśātmakaḥ" iti mammaṭoktiś ca na saṃgaccheta, vastvalaṃkārātmanā dvividhena vācyena svataḥsaṃbhavitvakaviprauḍhokti-niṣpannatvakavinibaddhavaktṛprauḍhoktiniṣpannatvais tribhir upādhibhis traividhyam āpannena ṣaḍātmanā vastvalaṃkārayor iva rasāder apy abhivyañjanād aṣṭādaśatvaprasaṅgāt/
atrocyate-- prakaṭair vibhāvānubhāvavyabhicāribhir alakṣyakramatayaiva vyajyamāno ratyādiḥ sthāyibhāvo rasībhavati, na saṃlakṣyakramatayā/ rasībhāvo hi nāma jhagiti jāyamānālaukikacamatkāraviṣayasthāyitvam/ saṃlakṣyakramatayā vyajyamānasya ratyādes tu vastumātrataiva, na rasāditvam iti teṣām āśayasya varṇanena na taduktīnāṃ virodhaḥ/ upapattis tv arthe 'smin vicāraṇīyā/ rasabhāvādir artha ity atra rasādiśabdo ratyādiparaḥ/
taditthaṃ nirūpitasyāsya rasādidhvaniprapañcasya padavarṇaracanāvākyaprabandhaiḥ padaikadeśair avarṇātmakai rāgādibhiś cābhivyaktim āmananti/ tatra vākyagatānāṃ padānāṃ sarveṣām api svārthopasthitidvārā vākyārthajñānopāyatve samāne 'pi kurvadrūpatayā camatkārāyogavyavacchinnatvena kasyacid eva dhvanivyapadeśahetutvam/ yathā "mandam ākṣipati" ity atra mandam ity asya/ racanāvarṇānāṃ tu padavākyāntargatatvena vyañjakatāvacchedakakoṭipraviṣṭatvam eva na tu vyañjakatvam iti yady api suvacam, tathāpi padavākyaviśiṣṭaracanātvena, racanāviśiṣṭapadavākyatvena vā vyañjakatvam iti vinigamanāviraheṇa ghaṭādau daṇḍacakrādeḥ kāraṇatvasyeva pratyekam eva vyañjakatāyāḥ siddhir iti prāñcaḥ/
body.translated_text:
— that is to say, [it consists in] being the object of a cognition that produces a single aesthetic wonder (<s>camatkṛti</s>).
Illustration—
"Sin, alas, has been committed by me who have killed [him] — even if a worm were [all that was] saved;
she, the moon-faced one, without me in the forest — alas, what will she do with her life?
Looking upon the faces of the virtuous — what will they say to me?
Let the kingdom go to the netherworld — I no longer wish to live!"
Here there is a variegation (<s>śabalatā</s>) of <s>mati</s> (deliberation), <s>asūyā</s> (envy), <s>viṣāda</s> (dejection), <s>smṛti</s> (memory), <s>vitarka</s> (conjecture), <s>vrīḍā</s> (modesty), <s>śaṅkā</s> (apprehension), and <s>nirveda</s> (world-weariness), each born from its own previously stated <s>vibhāva</s>. But what the commentators of the <s>Kāvyaprakāśa</s> have maintained — that 'the suppression of each preceding <s>bhāva</s> by each subsequent one constitutes <s>śabalatā</s>' — is incorrect. Because in the verse 'paśyet kaścic cala capala re kā tvarāhaṃ kumārī...' the <s>śabalatā</s> of <s>śaṅkā</s>, <s>asūyā</s>, <s>adhṛti</s>, <s>smṛti</s>, <s>śrama</s>, <s>dainya</s>, <s>mati</s>, and <s>autsukya</s> is analyzed by the original author himself in the fifth <s>ullāsa</s> as a <s>guṇa</s> subordinate to the praise of the king — even though there is not the slightest suppression [of earlier by later bhāvas]. The destruction that occurs through the specific quality of the succeeding [emotion] is not suggested; nor is it denotable by the word 'suppression'; nor is it a cause of aesthetic wonder.
"Just as in the mixture of coconut water, milk, sugar, and banana
there is a distinctive flavor — so too in the combination of <s>bhāvas</s>."
Here this should be understood: those dhvanis of <s>bhāva</s>-cessation, <s>bhāva</s>-arising, junction (<s>saṃdhi</s>), and variegation (<s>śabalatā</s>) that have been illustrated — these too are simply <s>bhāvadhvanis</s> (suggestions of emotional states). Because it is appropriate that primacy belongs to the <s>bhāvas</s> themselves, which are relished in modes such as being delimited by arising, being in a state of perishing, being in a state of junction, and being co-located with one another — just as [bhāvas] that exist [in a stable state] are relished — since aesthetic wonder rests precisely there. Even though when the cessation-arising-junction-variegation and the <s>bhāvas</s> related to them are equally objects of relishing, primacy cannot be determined, nevertheless, since primacy has been established for <s>bhāvas</s> in the stable state, it is appropriate to posit that primacy for them even in <s>bhāva</s>-cessation etc., since the <s>bhāvas</s> are suggested through [qualifications such as] being the counterpart of cessation, etc. Moreover, if in <s>bhāva</s>-cessation etc. the <s>bhāva</s> is not primary but rather the cessation which has the <s>bhāva</s> as its subordinate is primary, then in poems where <s>bhāvas</s> are suggested and their cessation etc. is expressed, there would be no <s>bhāva</s>-cessation-<s>dhvani</s>.
Thus—
"At dawn, as the beloved approaches from the rival heroine's house,
in the corners of the lotus-eyes of the beautiful one, a reddish luster arose swiftly."
Here, because the <s>bhāva</s>-arising is communicated merely as the expressed meaning through the unprecedented suffix '-eti.' (If one objects:) 'Even if the arising is expressed, since the <s>bhāva</s> itself is unexpressed, the <s>dhvani</s>-status is well-established' — [we reply:] when the primary [element] is irrelevant to the designation, the designation based on the subordinate [element] is untenable. But in our view, even when the arising is expressed, since <s>amarṣa</s> (indignation) as delimited by arising — being the primary [element] — is unexpressed, the designation 'suggestion of <s>bhāva</s>-arising' is entirely justified. Similarly, when the cessation that is the counterpart of a suggested <s>bhāva</s> is expressed, there would be no <s>bhāva</s>-cessation-<s>dhvani</s>. As—
"When the beloved falls at the feet [that demand] but one word of apology,
the reddish lusters of the lotus-eyed one's eyes subsided."
(If one objects:) Since the expressed cessation etc. is syntactically connected only with the reddish luster, the expressed meaning that has culminated is the cessation of the reddish luster etc., not the cessation of the anger that is suggested by the reddish luster — because a difference between the suggested and its suggestor is necessary. And one should not say that the cessation etc. is syntactically connected with anger, which is suggested through redness — because since the cognitions of expressed and suggested meaning are established in sequence, at the time of cognizing the syntactic connection of the expressed meaning, a syntactic connection of the suggested meaning with the expressed is untenable; otherwise there would be no syntactic connection of 'of the beautiful one's lotus-eye-corners.' Not so! For even thus, in—
"Of the doe-eyed one who drinks the beauty of <s>Hari</s>, banishing the composure of women,
even anger, thick with the memory of long offenses, became a guest of but a moment"
— there would be the fallacy of this being <s>bhāva</s>-cessation-<s>dhvani</s> as well, since even though the <s>bhāva</s> is expressed, the cessation of the primary [bhāva] is suggested. If one requires that both [bhāva and cessation] be unexpressed — then in the two previously cited verses, because cessation-ness and arising-ness make the cessation and arising expressed, there would be the fallacy of [those verses] not being illustrations [of dhvani]. But such an undesirable consequence would be improper for connoisseurs. Therefore, even in <s>bhāva</s>-cessation etc., it is the <s>bhāvas</s> themselves that primarily produce aesthetic wonder; the cessation etc. is subordinate — hence there is no fault from its being expressed. Now, the reason for the difference in aesthetic wonder between <s>bhāva</s>-<s>dhvanis</s> and <s>bhāva</s>-cessation-etc.-<s>dhvanis</s> is this: in the former, the mode in the relishing is being-delimited-by-stable-state as <s>amarṣa</s> etc., or simply amarṣa-ness etc.; in the latter, however, the mode of being-in-a-state-of-cessation etc. is also [present]. But since <s>rasa</s> is rooted in the permanent emotion (<s>sthāyī</s>), cessation etc. of it is impossible; or even if possible, it does not produce aesthetic wonder — hence that is not discussed.
This entire elaborated scope of the suggested — characterized by <s>rati</s> (love) and other [emotions] — when the <s>vibhāvas</s>, <s>anubhāvas</s>, and <s>vyabhicārīs</s> are manifest and cognized instantly in a transparent context, is apprehended by the most sensitive perceiver (<s>sahṛdayatama</s>) in a subtle manner alone. Therefore, because the sequence of cause and effect is unperceived, it is designated as <s>alakṣyakrama</s> (of imperceptible sequence). But where the context requires investigation, or the <s>vibhāvas</s> etc. must be inferred, there the aesthetic wonder is slow, dependent on the delay of the complete conditions — and so this can also be <s>saṃlakṣyakrama</s> (of perceptible sequence). As in the previously cited verse 'talpagatāpi ca sutanuḥ,' the comprehension of the meaning of 'saṃprati' (now) is delayed. Indeed, the <s>alakṣyakrama-vyaṅgyatva</s> (being suggested through imperceptible sequence) of the <s>dhvani</s> of love etc. is not established by the reasoning that grasps the property-bearer. Therefore, regarding the occasion of perceptible sequence—
"When the divine sage (<s>Nārada</s>) spoke thus, at her father's side, with face downcast,
<s>Pārvatī</s> began counting the petals of her playful lotus."
— Here, the master <s>Ānandavardhana</s> says: 'Because even from maidenlynatural disposition the downward-facing lotus-petal-counting is plausible, with slight delay after the cognition of <s>Nārada's</s> mention of marriage etc., <s>vrīḍā</s> (modesty) produces aesthetic wonder — hence this is <s>dhvani</s> of perceptible sequence.' And the master <s>Abhinavagupta</s> [says]: 'The meaning such as <s>rasa</s> and <s>bhāva</s> is suggested only, not expressed; nevertheless, not every [such suggestion] falls within the scope of imperceptible sequence.' One might think: if this <s>rasa</s> etc. were the object of perceptible sequence, then <s>Abhinavagupta's</s> statement in the enumeration of <s>anuraṇana</s> (resonance) types — 'That which is rooted in the power of meaning has twelve varieties' — and <s>Mammaṭa's</s> statement 'Therefore this [dhvani] has twelve forms' — would not hold; because, just as the twofold expressed content consisting of <s>vastu</s> (content) and <s>alaṃkāra</s> (figure) becomes sixfold through three conditions — being naturally occurring, being produced by the poet's bold expression, and being produced by the bold expression of the character composed by the poet — so too <s>rasa</s> etc. would become eighteen-fold through expression by those same [conditions], just like <s>vastu</s> and <s>alaṃkāra</s>.
To this we reply: the permanent emotion (<s>sthāyī</s>) such as <s>rati</s>, when suggested through manifest <s>vibhāvas</s>, <s>anubhāvas</s>, and <s>vyabhicārīs</s> in imperceptible sequence alone, becomes <s>rasa</s> — not through perceptible sequence. For <s>rasa</s>-hood means being a permanent emotion that is the object of supramundane aesthetic wonder arising instantaneously. But love etc. suggested through perceptible sequence has merely the status of a <s>vastu</s> (content), not of <s>rasa</s> etc. Thus by describing their intent, there is no contradiction with their statements. The justification, however, in this matter requires investigation. In the phrase '<s>rasa</s>-<s>bhāva</s> etc. as meaning,' the word '<s>rasa</s> etc.' refers to <s>rati</s> (love) and other [permanent emotions].
Thus, the elaboration of <s>rasa</s>-etc.-<s>dhvani</s>, which has been analyzed in this way, is said to be expressed by words, phonemes, composition, sentences, literary works, parts of words, and non-phonemic elements such as <s>rāga</s> (melodic modes) etc. Among these, although all the words in a sentence equally serve as the means of sentence-meaning cognition through the presentation of their own meanings, only certain [words] are designated as the basis of <s>dhvani</s>, being delimited by their active role in producing aesthetic wonder. As in 'mandam ākṣipati' (gently glances), the word 'mandam' (gently) [is the dhvani-basis]. As for composition and phonemes, since they are contained within words and sentences, it is easy to say that they enter the delimiting condition of suggestive capacity but do not themselves possess suggestive capacity. Nevertheless, whether the suggestive capacity belongs to the composition as qualified by words and sentences, or to words and sentences as qualified by composition — since there is no way to determine [which], the capacity of each independently is established, just like the causality of the stick, the wheel, etc. in [producing] the pot — thus say the ancients.

body.text: varṇaracanāviśeṣāṇāṃ mādhuryādiguṇābhivyañjakatvam eva na rasābhivyañjakatvam, gauravān mānābhāvāc ca/ na hi guṇyabhivyañjanaṃ vinā guṇābhivyañjakatvaṃ nāstīty asti niyamaḥ, indriyatraye vyabhicārāt/ itthaṃ ca svasvavyañjakopanītānāṃ guṇināṃ guṇānām udāsīnānāṃ ca yathā parasparopaśleṣeṇaudāsīnyena vā tattatpramitigocaratā tathā rasānāṃ tadguṇānāṃ cābhivyāktiviṣayateti tu navyāḥ/ udāharaṇaṃ tu "tāṃ tamāla" ityādi prāg uktam eva vākyasya vyañjakatāyām api "āvirbhūtā yad avadhi" ityādi ca/ prabandhasya tu yogavāsiṣṭharāmāyaṇe śāntakaruṇayoḥ, ratnāvalyādīni ca śṛṅgārasya vyañjakatvān nidarśanāni prasiddhāni/ mannirmitāś ca pañja laharyo bhāvasya/ padaikadeśasya ca "nikhilam idaṃ jagad aṇḍakaṃ vahāmi" iti karūpataddhito vīrarasasya prāg evodāhṛtaḥ/ evaṃ rāgādibhir api vyaṅgyatve sahṛdayahṛdayam eva pramāṇam/ evam eṣāṃ rasādīnāṃ prādhānyena nirūpitāny udāharaṇāni/ guṇībhāve tu vakṣyante, nāmāni ca/ tatra prādhānya evaiṣāṃ rasāditvam, anyathā tu ratyāditvam eva/ nāmani rasapadaṃ tu ratyādiparam ity eke/ asty eva rasāditvaṃ, kiṃ tu na dhvanivyapadeśahetutvam ity apare//
body.translated_text: The particular arrangements of sounds serve to manifest qualities such as <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness) and the like, not to manifest <s>rasas</s>—due to their weightiness and their lack of capacity for this. For there is no rule that without manifesting the qualified entity (<s>guṇin</s>), the manifestation of its quality (<s>guṇa</s>) is impossible, since this is contradicted in the case of the three sense-faculties. Thus, just as the qualified entities, qualities, and neutral elements—each brought forth by their respective suggestive factors—become objects of their respective cognitions through mutual association or through indifference, so too the <s>rasas</s> and their qualities become objects of manifestation—such is the view of the moderns. The illustration is the verse "<s>tāṃ tamāla</s>" and so on, already cited above, for the suggestive capacity of sentences. And also "<s>āvirbhūtā yad avadhi</s>" and the like. As for extended compositions, the <s>Yogavāsiṣṭha-Rāmāyaṇa</s> for <s>śānta</s> (tranquil) and <s>karuṇa</s> (compassionate), and <s>Ratnāvalī</s> and similar works for <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic) are well-known examples of suggestive power. And the five <s>Laharīs</s> composed by me are examples for <s>bhāva</s> (emotion). For a part of a word, the <s>taddhita</s> derivative in <s>karūpa</s>—"I bear this entire universe as an egg"—has already been cited as an example of <s>vīrarasa</s> (heroic sentiment). Thus, in suggestion through <s>rāga</s> (melody) and other means also, the heart of the <s>sahṛdaya</s> (connoisseur) alone is the authority. In this way, illustrations have been given for these <s>rasas</s> and the like in their predominant mode. In their subordinate mode, they will be discussed later, along with their names. Here, only when predominant do they have the status of <s>rasa</s> and so on; otherwise they are merely <s>rati</s> (love) and so on. Some say that the term <s>rasa</s> in the nomenclature refers to <s>rati</s> and the like. Others hold that the status of <s>rasa</s> and so on indeed exists, but it is not the cause for the designation of <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion).
